{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01JyQ8G8dtaxPnJmgJzkUADw","type":"tool_result","content":"# Yamark\n\nYamark is a fast formatter for YAML and Markdown. It formats whole files and embedded content, keeping source readable and changes easy to review. Regions without a supported rewrite stay unchanged.\n\nFor supported embedded code, Yamark can also call Ruff, Air, Prettier, or another configured formatter.\n\nSee the [documentation](https://t-kalinowski.github.io/yamark/) for examples, configuration, editor integrations, and the full syntax reference.\n\n## Install\n\nWith [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) installed, run Yamark directly from [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/yamark/) without a separate install:\n\n```sh\nuvx yamark format config.yaml docs/\n```\n\nThis formats the selected files in place. To install a persistent `yamark` command:\n\n```sh\nuv tool install yamark\n```\n\n## Usage\n\nThe examples below use an installed `yamark` command. To keep running from PyPI without installing it, replace `yamark` with `uvx yamark`.\n\nFormat one or more files or directories in place:\n\n```sh\nyamark format config.yaml docs/\n```\n\nFormat the current directory:\n\n```sh\nyamark format\n```\n\nCheck whether files are already formatted without writing changes:\n\n```sh\nyamark format --check docs/\n```\n\nShow a unified diff without writing changes:\n\n```sh\nyamark format --diff docs/\n```\n\nFormat stdin for editor and CI integrations:\n\n```sh\nyamark format --stdin-file-path config.yaml < config.yaml\n```\n\nConvert JSON-family input from stdin to formatted YAML on stdout:\n\n```sh\nyamark to-yaml --stdin-file-path data.json5 < data.json5\n```\n\nThe path is not read or written. Its suffix selects the exact JSON dialect. This is a conversion, not source formatting.\n\nDirectory traversal skips hidden paths and respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and global Git ignore files by default. Pass a hidden path explicitly to format it.\n\nWhile formatting is enabled, standalone `{{< ... >}}` and `{{% ... %}}` shortcode tokens are preserved, including multiline tokens and quoted arguments. Directive-looking text inside a recognized token is data. Yamark does not match shortcode names or interpret their bodies: Markdown between tokens formats normally. An unterminated token or quote preserves the rest of the enclosing Markdown document or fragment. This does not guarantee rendering equivalence for arbitrary Hugo or Jinja templates.\n\nTo disable body formatting, surround the region with `<!-- fmt: off -->` and `<!-- fmt: on -->`. While formatting is disabled, directives follow the existing linewise policy: a recognized `fmt: on` line resumes formatting even if the surrounding text resembles a shortcode argument, code fence, HTML, or math block.\n\nExplicitly skipped Markdown retains its bytes, including trailing spaces and line endings: `<!-- fmt: skip -->` preserves the next selected node, `<!-- fmt: off -->` preserves the disabled region, and `<!-- fmt: skip file -->` preserves the enclosing Markdown document or fragment. This protection survives supported nesting in Markdown fences and divs; surrounding Markdown still formats.\n\n## Editor integrations\n\nThe VS Code and Positron formatter extension lives in `editors/vscode/`. See the [editor guide][editor-docs] for installation and configuration.\n\n# Repository guides\n\nFor installation, CLI options, configuration, and supported syntax, start with the [user documentation](../website/reference.qmd). The Quarto sources in `website/` own those contracts.\n\n| Contributor task                               | Guide                                             |\n| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |\n| Set up a checkout and choose validation        | [Development](DEVELOPMENT.md)                     |\n| Find the implementation owner and invariants   | [Architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md)                   |\n| Add a public regression or run a focused suite | [Tests](../tests/README.md)                       |\n| Understand retained inline source              | [Inline literal preservation](inline-literals.md) |\n| Record agreed follow-up work                   | [Open work](TODO.md)                              |\n| Prepare and publish a release                  | [Release](../RELEASE.md)                          |\n| Run benchmarks                                 | [Benchmark tools](../tools/bench/README.md)       |\n\n[Design sketches](../design-sketches/README.md) retain completed workpads and dated experiments. Benchmark JSON under `docs/benchmarks/` records individual runs. Neither is a current behavior specification.\n# Inline literal preservation\n\nParagraph preparation recognizes inline boundaries before changing whitespace.\nCode and math recognized by the existing scanners keep their source bytes,\nincluding spaces, tabs, escapes, and LF, CRLF, or CR line endings. Supported\nsurrounding prose, links, and emphasis still receive the requested formatting.\nA multiline literal is one wrapping token and can exceed the requested width.\n\nContainer preparation removes structural prefixes and retains the remaining\ncontent and authored line endings. In a definition list, four authored spaces\ncan precede content even when the formatted continuation prefix has five.\nWhitespace after the structural indentation belongs to the content. The same\ninline pipeline handles supported paragraphs, lists, quotes, definitions,\nfootnotes, and Markdown reached through existing nested document paths.\n\n## Preparation and emission\n\nThe retained representation is a flat set of source ranges. Ordinary text and\ngaps are implicit between ranges. It reuses the existing literal, link, and\nemphasis scanners, including their caches and precedence rules.\n\nResolution normalizes only for the effective options. It builds no canonical\nalternative when canonicalization is disabled, and no measured token array for\n`--wrap none` or paragraph wrapping. Later file-scoped directives derive the\nrequested form from the retained source and recognition facts. Hard breaks\noutside literals retain their existing normalization scopes; nested quotes with\n`--wrap none` also retain authored line scopes.\n\nEmission copies retained decisions and maps literal ranges into output\ncoordinates as it restores prefixes. Nested output carries those ranges through\nthe same verbatim-range mechanism used for explicitly preserved Markdown.\nEditable gaps and structural blank lines still receive ordinary output cleanup.\nLiteral protection also leaves document-level final-newline insertion active.\nExplicit preservation, including standalone shortcode tokens, retains its\nexisting policy for an absent final newline. That policy follows the actual\noutput tail after fragment composition.\n\n## Boundaries\n\nThis does not expand the block grammar, template eligibility, HTML matching, or\nmalformed-delimiter rules. Recognition stops at existing opaque inline tokens;\nit does not recursively interpret code or math inside HTML or strikethrough.\nBlock boundaries still limit which source belongs to one inline paragraph.\n\nAutomatic fallback retains its existing cleanup policy. For example, a list\nstarting with `100.` and a four-space continuation remains unsupported by the\nexisting list formatter. Multiline templates and opaque HTML can also fall back.\nUnlike recognized literals and explicit preservation directives, automatic\nfallback does not promise byte-for-byte preservation or idempotence after its\ntrailing-space cleanup. YAML defines named fields tools can act on; Markdown carries the instructions, examples, and context that shape model behavior. [Benchmarks](benchmarks.qmd) page includes detailed tables, methodology,\nchecked-in results, and reproduction commands.\n---\ntitle: Usage\ndescription: Install Yamark, format files, and choose an integration.\n---\n\n## Install\n\nWith [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) installed, run Yamark directly\nfrom [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/yamark/) without a separate\ninstall:\n\n```sh\nuvx yamark format config.yaml docs/\n```\n\nThis formats the selected files in place. To install a persistent\n`yamark` command:\n\n```sh\nuv tool install yamark\n```\n\nThe examples below use an installed `yamark` command. To keep running\nfrom PyPI without installing it, replace `yamark` with `uvx yamark`.\n\nThe checkout pins Rust 1.98.1. Building from source requires Rust 1.98.1 or newer.\nTo build from a checkout, run:\n\n```sh\ncargo install --path .\n```\n\n## Format files\n\nFormat one or more files or directories in place:\n\n```sh\nyamark format config.yaml docs/\n```\n\nFormat the current directory:\n\n```sh\nyamark format\n```\n\nBy default, Markdown prose wraps at column 72 without forcing sentence\nboundaries. Override this behavior with `--wrap`, for example:\n\n```sh\nyamark format --wrap sentence:88 docs/\n```\n\nDirectory traversal skips hidden paths and respects `.gitignore`,\n`.ignore`, and global Git ignore files by default. Pass a hidden path\nexplicitly to format it.\n\n## CI and stdin\n\nUse check, diff, or stdin modes for integrations:\n\n```sh\nyamark format --check docs/\nyamark format --diff docs/\nyamark format --stdin-file-path config.yaml < config.yaml\n```\n\n`--check` and `--diff` do not write files. Both exit `1` when any\nselected file would change.\n\nConvert JSON-family input from stdin to formatted YAML on stdout:\n\n```sh\nyamark to-yaml --stdin-file-path data.json5 < data.json5\n```\n\nThe path is not read or written. Its suffix selects the exact JSON dialect.\nThis is a conversion, not source formatting.\n\nFor `yamark format`, use `--diagnostics` to explain preserved content. Use\n`--skip-embedded-formatters` when another tool formats the same embedded code.\n\n## Integrations\n\n- [Examples](examples.qmd): focused before-and-after output from the current\n  Yamark binary.\n- [Directives](directives.qmd): put formatting choices beside content in\n  Markdown, YAML, Python, and R files.\n- [Editors](editors.qmd): VS Code, Positron, and compatible forks -\n  commands, settings, format-on-save, formatter chaining, and logs.\n- [Reference](reference.qmd): look up supported files and syntax, formatting\n  settings, `yamark.toml`, directive grammar, and command behavior.\n- [Command line](cli-help.qmd): modes, output, exit status, and generated\n  `--help` for Yamark, `format`, `to-yaml`, and the `git-filter` command group.\n- [Git Filter](git-filter.qmd): an experimental workflow that stores Markdown\n  sentence-per-line while keeping the working tree column-wrapped.\n---\ntitle: Reference\ndescription: Find exact details about Yamark's inputs, settings, configuration, directives, and commands.\ntoc: false\n---\n\nUse this section to look up a specific behavior, setting, or syntax. path-specific formatter setup. |\n| One run | [Command-line flags](cli-help.qmd) | A temporary choice or CI invocation. |\n\nThe [Formatting settings](reference-options.qmd) page groups these surfaces It combines software-readable structure with natural language for prompts,\nskills, reference documents, and generated output. The Before pane shows the\nunformatted source; the After pane shows what `yamark format` writes back.\n\n\n\n:::: {.before-after}\n::: {.before-after-pane #demo-before}\n**Before** <label class=\"softwrap-toggle\"><input type=\"checkbox\" id=\"demo-softwrap-toggle\"> soft wrap</label>\n\n```markdown\n---\ntitle: Why YAML + Markdown?\ndescription: The source languages of LLM work - structured fields for tools alongside instructions, examples, and context for models.\ntags: [llm,authoring,formats]\n---\n\n#   Why YAML + Markdown? ##\n\nWhen LLMs become part of a software system, YAML and Markdown start to feel like programming languages. YAML defines named fields tools can act on; Markdown carries the instructions, examples, and context that shape model behavior. Together they create a shared source file that stays readable to people and models, exposes explicit structure to software, produces clear diffs, and renders directly.\n\nWhere the combination shines:\n\n- Agent skills and prompt files keep names, versions, and tool metadata beside the instructions they describe.\n  - The Markdown body can carry code samples and nested structures with their own syntax and indentation.\n- Reference documents stay readable to authors and models without a separate source format or build step.\n- Tool inputs and model outputs survive chat, Git, and documentation pipelines as recognizable text.\n- One source can render as HTML or PDF and travel unchanged as agent context.\n```\n\n:::\n\n::: {.before-after-pane}\n**After**\n\n```markdown\n---\ntitle: Why YAML + Markdown?\ndescription: >-\n  The source languages of LLM work - structured fields for tools alongside\n  instructions, examples, and context for models.\ntags: [llm, authoring, formats]\n---\n\n# Why YAML + Markdown?\n\nWhen LLMs become part of a software system, YAML and Markdown start to\nfeel like programming languages. Passing a hidden path explicitly selects it.\n\n## JSON-to-YAML projection\n\nFormatting preserves the source language and produces output that can replace\nthe input. Explicit Markdown targets still format; their block content uses deeper indentation when needed to keep the following comment outside the value.\n\n### JSON Lines (JSONL) as YAML streams\n\nPath-aware formatting recognizes a `.yaml` or `.yml` stream made of two or more\nunmarked, one-line YAML flow-mapping roots, one per physical line with no\nseparate trivia lines. It inserts the `---` document-start marker before every\nrecord, including the first.\n\nJSON objects are the common case, but the trigger is based on YAML shape and is\nnot restricted to strict JSON objects.\n\nNormal `--line-width` rules still determine whether each record and its nested\ncollections stay in flow style or expand to block style. Only the unmatched opener is a repair\nfor ill-formed input:\n\n- An unmatched `[` or `{` where a block sequence or mapping begins as a mapping\n  value or sequence item asks Yamark to collapse that one collection to flow\n  style.\n- A physical newline inside a complete flow collection is valid multiline YAML.\n  It asks Yamark to expand that collection to block style. Adjacent forms such as `tags:[` and `tags:{` are not\nlayout hints.\n\nWhen the requested flow form fits the available `--line-width`, Yamark removes\nthe unmatched opener and emits the collection in flow style. Preserves decoded whitespace and comments. |\n| Literal scalars | Preserves by default | Changes a literal scalar only when it is explicitly marked as Markdown or an embedded formatter target. |\n| Quoted scalars with hard newlines | Formats when safe | Can emit literal block style when the YAML value stays unchanged. |\n| Scalars below a mapping key or sequence marker | Formats when safe | Retains the complete entry when preserving a value. Explicit Markdown targets still format; their block content uses deeper indentation when needed to keep the following comment outside the value.\n\n### JSON Lines (JSONL) as YAML streams\n\nPath-aware formatting recognizes a `.yaml` or `.yml` stream made of two or more\nunmarked, one-line YAML flow-mapping roots, one per physical line with no\nseparate trivia lines. Only the unmatched opener is a repair\nfor ill-formed input:\n\n- An unmatched `[` or `{` where a block sequence or mapping begins as a mapping\n  value or sequence item asks Yamark to collapse that one collection to flow\n  style.\n- A physical newline inside a complete flow collection is valid multiline YAML.\n  It asks Yamark to expand that collection to block style. Compact mode\n  suppresses this multiline intent.\n\nThe opener may be on the value line or on the following line after an empty\nmapping value header. Adjacent forms such as `tags:[` and `tags:{` are not\nlayout hints.\n\nWhen the requested flow form fits the available `--line-width`, Yamark removes\nthe unmatched opener and emits the collection in flow style. This page groups settings by behavior; the linked\n[configuration](reference-config.qmd),\n[directive](reference-directives.qmd), and [command-line](cli-help.qmd) pages\ngive the exact syntax for each surface.\n\n## Markdown settings\n\n| Behavior | [Directive](reference-directives.qmd#markdown-targets-and-settings) | [Front matter](#document-markdown-options) | [`yamark.toml`](reference-config.qmd#format) | [Command line](cli-help.qmd#yamark-format) | Default |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Prose wrapping | `wrap=` | `editor_options.markdown.wrap` | `[format].wrap` | `--wrap` | Column 72 |\n| Table widths | `table-widths=` | `editor_options.markdown.table-widths` | `[format].table_widths` | `--table-widths` | `fit` |\n| Canonical spelling | `canonical=` or `canonical` | `editor_options.markdown.canonical` | - | `--canonical` | Off |\n| Footnote definitions | `footnotes=` | `editor_options.markdown.footnotes` | - | `--preserve-footnotes` | Format |\n| Horizontal-rule marker | - | - | `[format].markdown_horizontal_rule` | - | `---` |\n\n### Wrapping values\n\n| Value | Effect |\n| --- | --- |\n| `none` | Do not wrap Markdown prose. |\n| `paragraph` | Put each paragraph on one physical line. |\n| `sentence` | Put each sentence on its own line without column wrapping. |\n| `sentence:<n>` | Put each sentence on its own line and wrap long sentences to column `<n>`. |\n| A positive integer | Wrap prose to that column without forcing sentence boundaries. |\n\n`sentence:<n>` is a Yamark-specific extension. RStudio's visual writer does not\nrecognize the combined value.\n\n### Table widths\n\n`fit` sizes supported pipe, simple, grid, and multiline table columns from\ntheir contents, with consistent padding. It can shrink excessive widths or\nexpand cramped columns. Both modes preserve column alignment and multiline\ncell breaks.\n\n`preserve` retains the source widths while still formatting cell contents.\nFor Pandoc tables, this keeps the borders and gaps that determine widths. For\npipe tables, it keeps separator lengths and row widths, even when the original\nrows are not aligned with one another.\n\nPandoc can use source widths to determine rendered column proportions and\nwrapping. Choose `preserve` when those widths are intentional:\n\n```markdown\n<!-- fmt: table-widths=preserve scope=next -->\n+----------+------------------+\n| Name     | Description      |\n+==========+==================+\n| A        | Short text       |\n+----------+------------------+\n```\n\nUse `scope=file` for a document-wide choice or `scope=from-here` for subsequent\ntables. A later `table-widths=fit scope=from-here` resumes fitting widths.\nWithout an explicit scope, this option follows the usual Markdown directive\ndefault of `scope=file`.\n\nThe setting also works in front matter, `yamark.toml`, and the command line.\nExplicit renderer settings such as Quarto's `tbl-colwidths` remain unchanged.\n`fmt: skip` preserves the entire table when exact source layout matters.\nUnsupported table structures remain unchanged in either mode.\n\n### Canonical and footnote values\n\n`canonical` accepts `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0` in front matter\nand directives. A bare `canonical` directive means `canonical=true`. Canonical\nmode rewrites supported `_emphasis_` and `__strong__` spans as `*emphasis*` and\n`**strong**`. It preserves protected or unsupported spans, including intraword\nunderscores, code spans, link destinations, raw HTML, and template content.\n\nFor `footnotes`, `wrap`, `format`, `true`, `yes`, and `1` format footnote\ndefinitions. `preserve`, `none`, `false`, `no`, and `0` preserve them.\n`--preserve-footnotes` preserves Markdown footnote definitions byte-for-byte.\n\n## YAML settings\n\n| Behavior | Control | Default | Effect |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Structural line width | `--line-width <n>` | 80 | Expands block-renderable flow collections when they exceed the width. Over-width flow collections that cannot be rendered safely in block style may be preserved. Also bounds compact and layout-repair output. |\n| Folded scalar prose width | `--prose-width <n>` | 72 | Wraps eligible folded YAML prose. |\n| Block indentation | `--indent-width <n>` | 2 | Sets indentation for emitted block mappings and sequences. |\n| Compact collections | `--compact`, `[format].compact`, or `fmt: compact` | Off | Collapses eligible block collections to flow style when they fit. |\n| Aligned flow mappings | `fmt: table` or `fmt: compact table` | Off | Aligns a following sequence of compatible flow mappings. The compact form first collapses eligible block rows. |\n\nAll width and indentation values must be positive integers.\n\nCanonical mode also permits limited rewrapping of short existing folded YAML\nprose scalars when their value stays unchanged.\n\n## Execution controls\n\n| Control | Effect |\n| --- | --- |\n| `--diagnostics` | For YAML input, emits trace counters; it also emits notes for skipped or failing optional embedded formatters. |\n| `--skip-embedded-formatters` | Disables external formatters while keeping Yamark's Markdown, YAML, front matter, and recursive Markdown formatting active. |\n| `--config <path>` | Uses one explicit `yamark.toml` for all selected files instead of discovering one per file. |\n\n### Embedded formatter controls\n\n| Need | Control |\n| --- | --- |\n| Select a target | Use a recognized Markdown fence language or a [`fmt: <name>` directive](reference-directives.qmd#templates-and-embedded-formatters). |\n| Register or replace a formatter | Add an [`[embedded.<name>]` table](reference-config.qmd#embedded) to `yamark.toml`. |\n| Disable external formatters for one run | Pass `--skip-embedded-formatters`. |\n| Explain an optional formatter skip | Pass `--diagnostics`. |\n\nWrite, check, diff, and stdin behavior is documented under\n[Command line](cli-help.qmd#modes-output-and-status).\n\n## Document Markdown options\n\nMarkdown front matter can set document-local options under\n`editor_options.markdown`:\n\n```markdown\n---\neditor_options:\n  markdown:\n    wrap: sentence:72\n    canonical: true\n    footnotes: preserve\n    table-widths: preserve\n---\nThis is __strong__. This is _emphasis_.\n```\n\n| Key | Accepted values |\n| --- | --- |\n| `wrap` | `none`, `paragraph`, `sentence`, `sentence:<n>`, or a positive integer column. |\n| `table-widths` | `fit` or `preserve`. |\n| `canonical` | `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. |\n| `footnotes` | `wrap`, `format`, `preserve`, `none`, `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. |\n\nUnknown front-matter keys and unrecognized values are ignored; the\ncorresponding base setting remains active. Invalid `yamark.toml` keys or\ndirective values are errors instead.\n\nThese options apply after the front matter to the Markdown body, recursive\n`markdown` or `md` fences, and Markdown-valued YAML scalars in nested YAML\nregions.\n\nYamark also reads `editor.markdown` for compatibility, but only when\n`editor_options.markdown` is absent. It does not merge the two tables. Git\nfilter subcommands use their own wrapping options and do not read document\noptions.\n\n## Interaction rules\n\nMarkdown settings are applied in this order:\n\n1. Command defaults and config establish the base settings. Explicit `--wrap`\n   and `--table-widths` values override their corresponding `[format]` config\n   values.\n2. Document front matter overrides the corresponding base Markdown settings\n   for the document body and its nested Markdown regions.\n3. Directives then override the corresponding settings within their scope.\n4. `--preserve-footnotes` is the final exception: it preserves footnote\n   definitions even when front matter or a directive requests formatting.\n\nOther interactions:\n\n- `--compact` enables compact mode even if `[format].compact` is `false`. A\n  scoped `fmt: compact=false` directive can disable it for its target, region,\n  or file.\n- `editor_options.markdown` takes the place of the compatibility\n  `editor.markdown` table when both are present; the tables are not merged.\n- Git filter clean and smudge commands use their own Markdown wrapping options.\n  They do not read document Markdown options.\n---\ntitle: Configuration\ndescription: Discovery and the complete yamark.toml schema.\n---\n\nYamark discovers `yamark.toml` from each formatted file's directory upward. It\nuses only the nearest file; it does not merge ancestor configs.\n\nPass `--config path/to/yamark.toml` to use one explicit file for every selected\npath instead. Unknown keys and invalid values are errors.\n\nThe top-level tables are `[format]`, `[template]`, `[embedded]`, and `[paths]`.\n\n## `[format]`\n\n```toml\n[format]\nwrap = \"sentence:88\"\ncompact = true\nmarkdown_horizontal_rule = \"***\"\n```\n\n| Key | Type and values | Effect when present |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `wrap` | String: `none`, `paragraph`, `sentence`, `sentence:<n>`, or a positive integer. | Sets Markdown wrapping. An explicit `--wrap` value overrides it. |\n| `table_widths` | String: `\"fit\"` or `\"preserve\"`. | Sizes Markdown table columns from their contents by default, or retains source widths. An explicit `--table-widths` overrides it; document settings and scoped directives override that base setting. |\n| `compact` | Boolean. | Enables or disables eligible YAML block-to-flow compaction. `--compact` still enables compact mode when this is `false`. |\n| `markdown_horizontal_rule` | String: `\"---\"` or `\"***\"`. | Chooses the marker Yamark emits for normalized Markdown horizontal rules. |\n\nSee [Formatting settings](reference-options.qmd) for built-in defaults and the\nother surfaces that expose these behaviors.\n\n## `[template]`\n\nTemplate delimiters mark regions Yamark must preserve because rendering can\nchange the host language. The defaults are `{{ }}`, `{% %}`, `{# #}`, and\n`<% %>`.\n\n| Key | Type | Effect |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `add_delimiters` | Array of `{ open, close }` tables. | Appends to the delimiters active at this layer, after `replace_delimiters` if both keys are present. |\n| `replace_delimiters` | Array of `{ open, close }` tables. | Replaces the delimiters active at this layer before any additions. |\n\nAdd a delimiter pair:\n\n```toml\n[template]\nadd_delimiters = [\n  { open = \"<<\", close = \">>\" }\n]\n```\n\nReplace the defaults:\n\n```toml\n[template]\nreplace_delimiters = [\n  { open = \"[[\", close = \"]]\" }\n]\n```\n\nEvery entry must contain non-empty `open` and `close` strings.\n\nIn Markdown paragraphs and supported prose containers, including lists and\nblockquotes, a complete single-line expression is one opaque word. Yamark\npreserves every byte inside it and wraps the surrounding prose normally. For\nexample, `{{ render(\"keep   this\") }}` can occupy its own line or exceed the\nrequested width, just like a long word. Function calls, quoted arguments,\nescaped quotes, and nested braces are supported. A closing delimiter inside a\nsingle- or double-quoted argument does not end the expression. For `{#` / `#}`\ncomments, the first literal `#}` ends the token; quotes, apostrophes, and braces\ninside have no special meaning. Yamark only recognizes boundaries; it does not\ninterpret or evaluate template languages.\n\nConfigured openers take precedence over Markdown inline syntax. When several\npairs match an opener, the first complete closing boundary ends the token. File\ndirectives apply to earlier content too, including nested Markdown blocks.\n\nA template-only source line does not preserve placement. With `--wrap sentence`:\n\n<!-- fmt: skip -->\n\n```markdown\nBefore\n{{ render(\"keep   this\") }}\nafter.\n```\n\nbecomes:\n\n```markdown\nBefore {{ render(\"keep   this\") }} after.\n```\n\nWrapping still respects explicit hard breaks, blank lines, and block boundaries.\nUse `fmt: skip`, `fmt: off`/`fmt: on`, or `fmt: skip file` to preserve layout.\nMultiline expressions, templates nested in Markdown links or emphasis, and\notherwise unsupported Markdown blocks retain their existing preservation\npolicy. Template settings do not change how Yamark handles headings, tables,\nhost-language eligibility, or standalone shortcode tokens.\n\n## `[embedded]`\n\nEach child table maps a directive or fence name to a formatter that reads stdin\nand writes stdout. It accepts exactly one key: the required `formatter` key.\n\n```toml\n[embedded.python]\nformatter = \"ruff\"\n\n[embedded.r]\nformatter = \"air\"\n\n[embedded.sql]\nformatter = { command = [\"sqlfmt\", \"--filename\", \"{path}\"], path_suffix = \".sql\" }\n```\n\n`formatter` accepts either a built-in shorthand or a custom formatter table.\nBuilt-in shorthands are:\n\n- `ruff`\n- `air`\n- `mdformat`\n- `prettier-json`, `prettier-jsonc`, and `prettier-json5`\n- `prettier-graphql`\n- `prettier-css`, `prettier-scss`, `prettier-less`, and `prettier-postcss`\n- `prettier-html`\n- `prettier-js`, `prettier-jsx`, `prettier-ts`, and `prettier-tsx`\n\nA custom formatter table requires both `command` and `path_suffix` and accepts\nno other keys:\n\n| Key | Requirement |\n| --- | --- |\n| `command` | A non-empty argv array of strings. It is not a shell command. At least one complete argv item must be `{path}`. |\n| `path_suffix` | A non-empty suffix appended to the synthetic path passed to the formatter. |\n\n`{path}` cannot be embedded inside another argv item.\n\nBuilt-in formatters are optional. A configured formatter is also optional when\nits command's first argv item is exactly `ruff`, `air`, `mdformat`, or\n`prettier`. For either kind, a missing executable or nonzero exit preserves the\ntarget and emits a note only with `--diagnostics`. Any other configured\nformatter treats either condition as an error. A successful process may close\nstdin before reading all input; its output still receives normal validation.\nA successful process that writes to stderr is always an error. Other\nstdin-write errors remain failures.\n\nEmbedded formatter names must be non-empty and trimmed. `skip`, `skip file`,\n`off`, `on`, and `table` are reserved directive names.\n\n## `[paths]`\n\nPath keys are relative to the directory containing `yamark.toml`. This page is\nan exact syntax lookup. For a guided path through YAML, Python, and R examples,\nsee [Directives](directives.qmd).\n\n## Comment forms\n\n| Host | Form | Placement |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Markdown | `<!-- fmt: ... -->` | An own-line HTML comment. |\n| YAML | `# fmt: ...` | An own-line hash comment. `fmt: table` and `fmt: compact table` may also be same-line comments on an empty-valued collection parent; a populated parent is an error. |\n| Python and R | `# fmt: ...` | An own-line hash comment before a supported comment or string target. |\n\n## Scopes\n\n| Scope | Meaning |\n| --- | --- |\n| `scope=next` | Apply to the next supported target. This is the default for target-selecting, compact, table, and embedded-formatter directives. |\n| `scope=from-here` | Apply from the directive until another directive changes the same state. |\n| `scope=file` | Apply throughout the current parsed document or nested region, including supported nodes before the directive. At the top level, that region is the physical file. |\n\nNot every directive accepts every scope. The tables below list the supported\nforms. An unsupported or misspelled explicit scope is an error. Template\ndelimiter directives use the contextual rule described below instead of one\nfixed default.\n\nScopes stop at the current parsed document or nested-region boundary. A\ndirective inside a recursive fence affects that fence, not its Markdown host or\nsibling fences. A `scope=file` directive inside one hashpipe YAML block does not\nspan later blocks. `fmt: skip file` in Markdown front matter is the exception:\nit preserves the outer Markdown document.\n\n## Preserve content\n\n| Directive | Scope | Effect |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `fmt: skip` | Next | Preserve the next supported target. `fmt: skip scope=next` is equivalent. |\n| `fmt: skip file` | File | Preserve the current parsed document or nested region. `fmt: skip scope=file` is equivalent. |\n| `fmt: off` | From here | Preserve content until `fmt: on`, or through the end of Markdown and source regions. `fmt: off scope=from-here` is equivalent. |\n| `fmt: on` | - | Resume formatting after `fmt: off`. The separated form accepts only `true` or `false`.\n\n## Templates and embedded formatters\n\n| Directive | Scope | Effect |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `fmt: template.delimiters \"<<\" \">>\"` | Inferred | Add one non-empty double-quoted delimiter pair using the placement rule below. |\n| `fmt: template.delimiters \"<<\" \">>\" scope=next` | Next | Add the pair to the next supported target. |\n| `fmt: template.delimiters \"<<\" \">>\" scope=from-here` | From here | Add the pair to following supported targets. |\n| `fmt: template.delimiters \"<<\" \">>\" scope=file` | File | Add the pair throughout the current document or nested region. |\n| `fmt: embedded python` | Next | Format the next supported string or YAML literal scalar with the named formatter. |\n| `fmt: python` | Next | Shorthand for `fmt: embedded python`. |\n\nA bare `fmt: template.delimiters` directive uses the next target when placed\ndirectly before one. The example below shows the full tag and comment forms.\n\nA `prompts.yaml` or `agents.yaml` file can use any of these forms. Yamark wraps\nthe selected value as Markdown, choosing folded or literal block style from the\ncontent.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```yaml\nagents:\n  reviewer:\n    instructions: !markdown \"Focus on correctness and tests. Flag any change that lacks a regression test. Prefer concrete suggestions: name the function, name the case.\"\n  summarizer:\n    # fmt: markdown\n    instructions: |\n      You write release notes.\n\n      - One bullet per user-visible change.\n      - No internal refactors.\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```yaml\nagents:\n  reviewer:\n    instructions: !markdown |\n      Focus on correctness and tests. Flag any change that lacks a regression\n      test. Prefer concrete suggestions: name the function, name the case.\n  summarizer:\n    # fmt: markdown\n    instructions: |\n      You write release notes.\n\n      - One bullet per user-visible change.\n      - No internal refactors.\n```\n::::\n\nThe tagged value contains only prose, so Yamark rewraps it as a folded block.\nThe comment-marked value contains a list, so Yamark keeps literal block style\n(`|`) because folding would destroy the line breaks Markdown depends on.\n\n### Source code in YAML\n\nYAML values can also contain source code. Use `# fmt: python`, `# fmt: r`, or\nthe name of another configured formatter before a literal block. When the\nformatter is available, Yamark formats the block and restores its indentation\nin the YAML file.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: python\npreflight: |\n  def check(items):return all(x>0 for x in items)\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: python\npreflight: |\n  def check(items):\n    return all(x > 0 for x in items)\n```\n::::\n\n### YAML scalar presentation\n\nYamark changes scalar spelling only when the parsed YAML value and tag\nstay equivalent. It can simplify safe quoted strings, keep strings that\nwould be misread as booleans, convert hard newlines to literal blocks,\nand fold long prose strings.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```yaml\ntitle: \"hello\"\nboolish: \"true\"\nbody: \"alpha\\nbeta\\n\"\nsummary: \"This package formats YAML front matter and configuration files while preserving semantics, comments, and repository-friendly diffs.\"\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```yaml\ntitle: hello\nboolish: \"true\"\nbody: |\n  alpha\n  beta\nsummary: >-\n  This package formats YAML front matter and configuration files while\n  preserving semantics, comments, and repository-friendly diffs.\n```\n::::\n\n## Markdown links, footnotes, and tables\n\nLong inline links are split at Markdown syntax boundaries. Footnote\ndefinitions wrap under the marker unless the document or CLI asks to\npreserve them.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```markdown\nPlease be mindful of our [code of conduct](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/main/.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) as you interact with other community members.\n\nBody text with a footnote.[^long]\n\n[^long]: This footnote explains that comments were removed because people used comments to hold parsing directives and enough extra words to wrap.\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```markdown\nPlease be mindful of our [code of conduct](\n  https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/main/.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md\n) as you interact with other community members.\n\nBody text with a footnote.[^long]\n\n[^long]: This footnote explains that comments were removed because\n  people used comments to hold parsing directives and enough extra words\n  to wrap.\n```\n::::\n\nSimple GFM pipe tables are aligned by display width. Git clean/smudge filters\nalways use compact pipe-table output.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```markdown\n| package | label |\n|---|---|\n| dplyr | tidy |\n| tidyr | pivoting |\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```markdown\n| package | label    |\n| ------- | -------- |\n| dplyr   | tidy     |\n| tidyr   | pivoting |\n```\n::::\n\n## Markdown in source files\n\n### Hashpipe YAML in source files\n\nConsecutive own-line `#|` comments in Python and R are a YAML block. Yamark\nformats the comment body as YAML, restores the hashpipe prefix, and leaves the\nsurrounding source code unchanged. This recognition is automatic; it does not\nneed a `fmt:` directive.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```r\n#| name: demo\n#| launcher:\n#|  vanilla: true\n#|  default-packages: [base,utils]\n\nmain <- function() NULL\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```r\n#| name: demo\n#| launcher:\n#|   vanilla: true\n#|   default-packages: [base, utils]\n\nmain <- function() NULL\n```\n::::\n\n### Embedded Markdown in Python\n\nWhen a prompt lives next to the code that uses it, Yamark can format the prose\nwithout changing the surrounding Python. Add `# fmt: markdown` before the\nstring:\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```python\n# fmt: markdown\nREVIEW_PROMPT = \"\"\"\n# Review\n\nRead the diff and flag anything that violates the style guide, has obvious correctness issues, or looks untested.\n\n-   Prefer specific suggestions over vague concerns.\n-   Name the function and the case.\n\"\"\"\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```python\n# fmt: markdown\nREVIEW_PROMPT = \"\"\"\n# Review\n\nRead the diff and flag anything that violates the style guide, has\nobvious correctness issues, or looks untested.\n\n- Prefer specific suggestions over vague concerns.\n- Name the function and the case.\n\"\"\"\n```\n::::\n\nPython source outside the marked string is left untouched. Run `ruff format` for\nthat.\n\n### Embedded Markdown in source comments\n\nThe same directive can target a contiguous source comment block. This is useful\nfor generated help text or documentation snippets where a string literal is not\nthe right host.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```python\n# fmt: markdown\n# #   Filters\n#\n# Apply one or more filters. Put the most specific filter first.\n#\n# -   Each filter is a single expression.\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```python\n# fmt: markdown\n# # Filters\n#\n# Apply one or more filters. Put the most specific filter first.\n#\n# - Each filter is a single expression.\n```\n::::\n\n### Embedded Markdown in R\n\nThe same pattern works for R raw strings. It can format package vignettes,\ndocumentation fragments, and Shiny help text kept next to the code that renders\nit.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```r\n# fmt: markdown\nhelp_text <- r\"(\n# Filters\n\nApply one or more filters. Filters are evaluated top-to-bottom; the first match wins, so put the most specific filter first.\n\n-   Each filter is a single expression.\n-   Multiple filters combine with AND.\n)\"\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```r\n# fmt: markdown\nhelp_text <- r\"(\n# Filters\n\nApply one or more filters. Filters are evaluated top-to-bottom; the\nfirst match wins, so put the most specific filter first.\n\n- Each filter is a single expression.\n- Multiple filters combine with AND.\n)\"\n```\n::::\n\n## YAML layout\n\n### JSON Lines as a YAML stream\n\nGive a JSON Lines file containing two or more object records a `.yaml` or\n`.yml` extension, with one record per line, then format it normally. Yamark\ninserts a leading `---` document-start marker before every record, including\nthe first, producing a valid YAML multi-document stream. The example below uses\nrecords from agent runs.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```yaml\n{\"id\":1,\"profile\":{\"name\":\"planner\",\"active\":true}}\n{\"id\":2,\"profile\":{\"name\":\"researcher\",\"active\":true},\"usage\":{\"input_tokens\":640,\"output_tokens\":128}}\n{\"id\":3,\"profile\":{\"name\":\"reviewer\",\"active\":true,\"model\":\"gpt-5\",\"region\":\"us\",\"tools\":[\"search\",\"python\"]},\"events\":[{\"type\":\"tool_call\",\"tools\":[\"search\",\"open\",\"python\",\"write\"]},{\"type\":\"usage\",\"tokens\":{\"input\":900,\"output\":240}},{\"type\":\"completion\",\"status\":\"ok\"}]}\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```yaml\n---\n{id: 1, profile: {name: planner, active: true}}\n---\nid: 2\nprofile: {name: researcher, active: true}\nusage: {input_tokens: 640, output_tokens: 128}\n---\nid: 3\nprofile:\n  name: reviewer\n  active: true\n  model: gpt-5\n  region: us\n  tools: [search, python]\nevents:\n  - {type: tool_call, tools: [search, open, python, write]}\n  - {type: usage, tokens: {input: 900, output: 240}}\n  - {type: completion, status: ok}\n```\n::::\n\nYamark keeps each document as compact as the width allows. The first record\nstays in flow style; the second expands only its root mapping; the third also\nexpands `profile` and `events`. Smaller mappings and sequences remain in flow\nstyle whenever they still fit within `--line-width`. This conversion is for\nobject records, not arbitrary JSON values.\n\n### Aligned flow-mapping tables\n\nA sequence of similar flow mappings can be easier to scan as a table. Mark it\nwith `# fmt: table` and Yamark aligns columns by key:\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: table\n- {name: alpha,type: string,default: [one,two],description: \"Short\"}\n- {name: beta,type: int,default: 0,description: \"Number\"}\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: table\n- {name: alpha, type: string, default: [one, two], description: Short}\n- {name: beta,  type: int,    default: 0,          description: Number}\n```\n::::\n\n### Compact collections\n\nShort, simple block collections can read better as a single flow line.\nEnable `compact = true` in `yamark.toml` (or pass `--compact`) and\nYamark collapses eligible block mappings and sequences that fit the\nstructural width:\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```yaml\ntags:\n  - yaml\n  - markdown\n  - docs\npackage:\n  name: yamark\n  language: rust\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```yaml\ntags: [yaml, markdown, docs]\npackage: {name: yamark, language: rust}\n```\n::::\n\nCollections with comments, aliases, tags, anchors, multiline scalars, or\nblock scalars stay in block style.\n\n### Collapse to flow by typing a bracket\n\nDrop an unmatched `[` or `{` where a block sequence or mapping value starts and\nYamark reads it as a layout hint: collapse this collection onto one line. The\nfile doesn't parse as you typed it, but the intent is obvious - Yamark removes\nthe opener and emits flow style.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```yaml\ntags: [\n  - yaml\n  - markdown\n  - docs\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```yaml\ntags: [yaml, markdown, docs]\n```\n::::\n\nThe opener may also be detached onto the next line after an empty mapping value\nheader:\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```yaml\ntags:\n[\n  - yaml\n  - markdown\n  - docs\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```yaml\ntags: [yaml, markdown, docs]\n```\n::::\n\nAdjacent forms such as `tags:[` and `tags:{` are not repaired as layout hints.\n\nA newline inside an existing flow collection requests the reverse change: expand\nthe collection to block style.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```yaml\n- {a: b,\n   c: d}\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```yaml\n- a: b\n  c: d\n```\n::::\n\nSee [Supported files and syntax -> Layout repair](reference-files.qmd#layout-repair)\nfor the acceptance rules.\n\n## Fenced and nested content\n\n### Recursive Markdown code fences\n\nYAML fences are formatted as YAML. Markdown fences are formatted\nrecursively, so nested YAML inside nested Markdown is formatted too.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n`````markdown\n```yaml\n# fmt: table\n- {name: a,type: int,default: 0}\n- {name: long_name,type: string,default: \"\"}\n```\n\n````markdown\n#   Inner\n\n```yaml\nitems: [a,b]\n```\n````\n`````\n\n**After**\n\n`````markdown\n```yaml\n# fmt: table\n- {name: a,         type: int,    default: 0}\n- {name: long_name, type: string, default: \"\"}\n```\n\n````markdown\n# Inner\n\n```yaml\nitems: [a, b]\n```\n````\n`````\n::::\n\n### Prettier-backed web and data fences\n\nWhen `prettier` is on `PATH`, JSON, JSONC, JSON5, GraphQL, CSS, SCSS, Less,\nPostCSS, HTML, JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, and TSX fenced blocks are handed to\nit. Python and R fences go to Ruff and Air the same way:\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n````markdown\n```json\n{\"name\":\"yamark\",\"tags\":[\"yaml\",\"markdown\",\"formatter\"],\"engines\":{\"node\":\">=18\"}}\n```\n\n```ts\nfunction format(input:string):string{return input.trim()}\n```\n````\n\n**After**\n\n````markdown\n```json\n{\n  \"name\": \"yamark\",\n  \"tags\": [\"yaml\", \"markdown\", \"formatter\"],\n  \"engines\": { \"node\": \">=18\" }\n}\n```\n\n```ts\nfunction format(input: string): string {\n  return input.trim();\n}\n```\n````\n::::\n\nA missing `prettier` leaves the fence unchanged. Smaller mappings and sequences remain in flow\nstyle whenever they still fit within `--line-width`. This conversion is for\nobject records, not arbitrary JSON values.\n\n### Aligned flow-mapping tables\n\nA sequence of similar flow mappings can be easier to scan as a table. Mark it\nwith `# fmt: table` and Yamark aligns columns by key:\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: table\n- {name: alpha,type: string,default: [one,two],description: \"Short\"}\n- {name: beta,type: int,default: 0,description: \"Number\"}\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: table\n- {name: alpha, type: string, default: [one, two], description: Short}\n- {name: beta,  type: int,    default: 0,          description: Number}\n```\n::::\n\n### Compact collections\n\nShort, simple block collections can read better as a single flow line.\nEnable `compact = true` in `yamark.toml` (or pass `--compact`) and\nYamark collapses eligible block mappings and sequences that fit the\nstructural width:\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```yaml\ntags:\n  - yaml\n  - markdown\n  - docs\npackage:\n  name: yamark\n  language: rust\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```yaml\ntags: [yaml, markdown, docs]\npackage: {name: yamark, language: rust}\n```\n::::\n\nCollections with comments, aliases, tags, anchors, multiline scalars, or\nblock scalars stay in block style.\n\n### Collapse to flow by typing a bracket\n\nDrop an unmatched `[` or `{` where a block sequence or mapping value starts and\nYamark reads it as a layout hint: collapse this collection onto one line. The\nfile doesn't parse as you typed it, but the intent is obvious - Yamark removes\nthe opener and emits flow style.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```yaml\ntags: [\n  - yaml\n  - markdown\n  - docs\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```yaml\ntags: [yaml, markdown, docs]\n```\n::::\n\nThe opener may also be detached onto the next line after an empty mapping value\nheader:\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```yaml\ntags:\n[\n  - yaml\n  - markdown\n  - docs\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```yaml\ntags: [yaml, markdown, docs]\n```\n::::\n\nAdjacent forms such as `tags:[` and `tags:{` are not repaired as layout hints.\n\nA newline inside an existing flow collection requests the reverse change: expand\nthe collection to block style.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```yaml\n- {a: b,\n   c: d}\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```yaml\n- a: b\n  c: d\n```\n::::\n\nSee [Supported files and syntax -> Layout repair](reference-files.qmd#layout-repair)\nfor the acceptance rules.\n\n## Fenced and nested content\n\n### Recursive Markdown code fences\n\nYAML fences are formatted as YAML. Markdown fences are formatted\nrecursively, so nested YAML inside nested Markdown is formatted too.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n`````markdown\n```yaml\n# fmt: table\n- {name: a,type: int,default: 0}\n- {name: long_name,type: string,default: \"\"}\n```\n\n````markdown\n#   Inner\n\n```yaml\nitems: [a,b]\n```\n````\n`````\n\n**After**\n\n`````markdown\n```yaml\n# fmt: table\n- {name: a,         type: int,    default: 0}\n- {name: long_name, type: string, default: \"\"}\n```\n\n````markdown\n# Inner\n\n```yaml\nitems: [a, b]\n```\n````\n`````\n::::\n\n### Prettier-backed web and data fences\n\nWhen `prettier` is on `PATH`, JSON, JSONC, JSON5, GraphQL, CSS, SCSS, Less,\nPostCSS, HTML, JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, and TSX fenced blocks are handed to\nit. Python and R fences go to Ruff and Air the same way:\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n````markdown\n```json\n{\"name\":\"yamark\",\"tags\":[\"yaml\",\"markdown\",\"formatter\"],\"engines\":{\"node\":\">=18\"}}\n```\n\n```ts\nfunction format(input:string):string{return input.trim()}\n```\n````\n\n**After**\n\n````markdown\n```json\n{\n  \"name\": \"yamark\",\n  \"tags\": [\"yaml\", \"markdown\", \"formatter\"],\n  \"engines\": { \"node\": \">=18\" }\n}\n```\n\n```ts\nfunction format(input: string): string {\n  return input.trim();\n}\n```\n````\n::::\n\nA missing `prettier` leaves the fence unchanged. Override or disable a\nlanguage with `[embedded.<language>]` in `yamark.toml`, or skip them all with\n`--skip-embedded-formatters`.\n\n---\n\nOnce an example has shown you the behavior, see [Directives](directives.qmd)\nfor how to place those instructions in Markdown, YAML, Python, and R files.\nUse [Reference](reference.qmd) to look up exact directive grammar, formatting\nsettings, supported syntax, and failure behavior.","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01J2wEvxotizCe9ea21FibjC","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

This can keep one-sentence edits\nfocused, but every clone needs local setup and other tools see the\ncolumn-wrapped files. The feature may change or be removed.\n\nThe filter only applies to paths matched by Git attributes.\n\n## Behavior\n\n`clean` runs when content moves from the working tree into the index:\n\n```sh\nyamark git-filter clean --stdin-filename docs/file.md\n```\n\nIt formats Markdown with sentence wrapping.\n\n`smudge` runs when content moves from the index into the working tree:\n\n```sh\nyamark git-filter smudge --stdin-filename docs/file.md --markdown-wrap-at-column 72\n```\n\nIt formats Markdown with column wrapping. Both directions use compact pipe-table\noutput to keep storage diffs small.\n\nUnsupported paths fail. The filter is for Markdown-like files, not YAML or\nsource files.\n\n## VS Code diff preview\n\nCommand-line `git diff` applies the clean filter to the working-tree side, so\nit compares clean content with clean content. VS Code's built-in unstaged\npreview instead reads the clean index blob and the smudged file on disk as\nseparate documents. That comparison can show wrapping changes across the file.\n\nThe Yamark VS Code extension contributes\n`Yamark: Open Filtered Working Tree Diff`. Right-click a modified tracked file\nunder **Changes** and run that command. It reads the index with\n`git cat-file --filters`, which applies the checkout filter, and opens a\nsmudged-to-smudged comparison against the working-tree file.\n\nFor files under **Staged Changes**, use VS Code's normal diff. VS Code reads\nboth HEAD and the index as clean Git blobs, so that comparison is already\nclean-to-clean.\n\nThe Yamark command cannot replace VS Code's default row click or gutter\nmarkers through the public extension API. The underlying VS Code behavior is\ntracked in [microsoft/vscode#302990](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/302990).\n\n## Adopt a repository\n\nFor a shared repository, the maintainer path is:\n\n```sh\ngit switch -c adopt-yamark-filter\nyamark git-filter adopt\ngit diff --cached\ngit commit -m \"Normalize Markdown with yamark Git filter\"\n```\n\n`adopt` requires a clean worktree. It writes shared `filter=yamark-md`\npatterns to `.gitattributes`, installs the local filter driver, normalizes\ntracked Markdown blobs into sentence-per-line storage, stages the normalized\nfiles, and checks the codec invariant:\n\n```text\nclean(smudge(blob)) == blob\n```\n\nUse `--markdown-wrap-at-column <n>` to change the working-tree wrap width. Pass\npaths to adopt only specific Markdown files:\n\n```sh\nyamark git-filter adopt content/blog/post/index.md\n```\n\n## Join a repository\n\nContributors should join only after the adoption commit is present in their\ncheckout:\n\n```sh\ngit pull --ff-only\nyamark git-filter join\n```\n\n`join` refuses when the current branch is behind its upstream. After the branch\nis current, it installs the local filter driver, verifies committed blobs\nround-trip, writes the column-wrapped working-tree view, and leaves\n`git status --porcelain` clean.\n\n## Check in CI\n\nUse `check` in CI to verify committed blobs still satisfy the clean/smudge\ncontract:\n\n```sh\nyamark git-filter check\n```\n\nIt fails if any tracked Markdown file selected by `.gitattributes` violates:\n\n```text\nclean(smudge(blob)) == blob\n```\n\n## Local setup\n\nFor personal experiments in the current repository, run:\n\n```sh\nyamark git-filter setup\n```\n\nThis low-level command configures the filter driver and adds the default\nMarkdown patterns to `.git/info/attributes`. It does not create a shared\nnormalization commit. Pass paths to configure only those paths:\n\n```sh\nyamark git-filter setup content/blog/post/index.md\n```\n\nUse `--repo path/to/repo` when running from outside the repository. Use\n`--markdown-wrap-at-column <n>` to change the working-tree wrap width.\n\nSetup prints the local files and config keys it changed, plus the commands below\nfor undoing or bypassing the filter.\n\nTo configure the same pieces manually, set the filter driver:\n\n```sh\ngit config filter.yamark-md.clean \"yamark git-filter clean --stdin-filename %f\"\ngit config filter.yamark-md.smudge \"yamark git-filter smudge --stdin-filename %f --markdown-wrap-at-column 72\"\ngit config filter.yamark-md.required true\ngit config merge.renormalize true\n```\n\nFor personal use, add attributes to `.git/info/attributes`. For shared project\nstorage, use `yamark git-filter adopt` so the attributes and normalized blobs\nland in the same commit. The shared attributes look like:\n\n```gitattributes\n*.md filter=yamark-md\n*.qmd filter=yamark-md\n*.Rmd filter=yamark-md\n*.rmd filter=yamark-md\n```\n\nIf you use low-level local setup on existing tracked files, normalize the index\nexplicitly:\n\n```sh\ngit add --renormalize .\n```\n\nReview the staged diff before committing the renormalization.\n\n## Undo\n\nTo remove the local setup created by `yamark git-filter setup`, run:\n\n```sh\nyamark git-filter teardown\n```\n\nThis unsets the local filter config and removes simple\n`filter=yamark-md` lines from `.git/info/attributes`. If your repository has\ncommitted `filter=yamark-md` rules in `.gitattributes`, edit that file directly.\n\nTo stage one file exactly as it appears in the working tree without running the\nclean filter for that `git add`, use:\n\n```sh\ngit -c filter.yamark-md.clean=cat add NEWS.md\n```\n\n## Per-file control\n\nGit attributes choose which paths use the filter. Put more specific rules after\nbroad ones:\n\n```gitattributes\n*.md filter=yamark-md\nNEWS.md -filter\n```\n\nUse this when a file should stay out of the clean/smudge flow. The\n+second sentence is the one that actually changed in this commit.\n```\n\nWith the filter, the stored form is sentence-per-line, so the changed sentence\nis the changed line.\n\n```diff\n-Ut enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris.\n+The second sentence is the one that actually changed in this commit.\n```\n\n## Notes\n\nEvery clone that wants the working-tree view needs the `git config` commands.\nThe `.gitattributes` file selects paths, but it does not define the filter\ndriver by itself.\n\nUse a pre-commit hook or CI `yamark format --check` instead when you want the\nrepository storage form to match the working-tree form.\n---\ntitle: Editors\ndescription: Use Yamark from VS Code, Positron, and compatible forks.\n---\n\nThe repository includes a Yamark extension for VS Code, Positron, and compatible\nforks. Use\n`Yamark: Preview Format Document` for Yamark's native file types, or\n`Yamark: View JSON as YAML` for JSON, JSONC, JSON5, JSONL, and NDJSON.\n\n`Yamark: Preview Format Document` runs the same formatting stages as Format\nDocument, including the configured next formatter, but opens the final text\ninstead of applying an edit. `Yamark: View JSON as YAML` sends the current\neditor buffer to `yamark to-yaml` and opens the resulting YAML. The shared attributes look like:\n\n```gitattributes\n*.md filter=yamark-md\n*.qmd filter=yamark-md\n*.Rmd filter=yamark-md\n*.rmd filter=yamark-md\n```\n\nIf you use low-level local setup on existing tracked files, normalize the index\nexplicitly:\n\n```sh\ngit add --renormalize .\n```\n\nReview the staged diff before committing the renormalization.\n\n## Undo\n\nTo remove the local setup created by `yamark git-filter setup`, run:\n\n```sh\nyamark git-filter teardown\n```\n\nThis unsets the local filter config and removes simple\n`filter=yamark-md` lines from `.git/info/attributes`. If your repository has\ncommitted `filter=yamark-md` rules in `.gitattributes`, edit that file directly.\n\nTo stage one file exactly as it appears in the working tree without running the\nclean filter for that `git add`, use:\n\n```sh\ngit -c filter.yamark-md.clean=cat add NEWS.md\n```\n\n## Per-file control\n\nGit attributes choose which paths use the filter. Put more specific rules after\nbroad ones:\n\n```gitattributes\n*.md filter=yamark-md\nNEWS.md -filter\n```\n\nUse this when a file should stay out of the clean/smudge flow. For example, if\n`NEWS.md` should stay column-wrapped in both the working tree and the index,\nexclude it from the filter and use the normal formatter:\n\n```sh\nyamark format --wrap 72 NEWS.md\ngit add NEWS.md\n```\n\nUse `<!-- fmt: skip file -->` inside a Markdown file when the file should still\npass through the filter but Yamark should preserve its contents.\n\n## Diff shape\n\nWithout the filter, editing one sentence inside a wrapped paragraph can modify\nevery physical line in the paragraph.\n\n```diff\n-Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do\n-eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut\n-enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris.\n+Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit, sed do\n+eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua. The\n+second sentence is the one that actually changed in this commit.\n```\n\nWith the filter, the stored form is sentence-per-line, so the changed sentence\nis the changed line.\n\n```diff\n-Ut enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris.\n+The second sentence is the one that actually changed in this commit.\n```\n\n## Notes\n\nEvery clone that wants the working-tree view needs the `git config` commands.\nThe `.gitattributes` file selects paths, but it does not define the filter\ndriver by itself.\n\nUse a pre-commit hook or CI `yamark format --check` instead when you want the\nrepository storage form to match the working-tree form.\n---\ntitle: Editors\ndescription: Use Yamark from VS Code, Positron, and compatible forks.\n---\n\nThe repository includes a Yamark extension for VS Code, Positron, and compatible\nforks. It runs `yamark format --stdin-file-path <file>` for document formatting\nand native formatted previews. It runs\n`yamark to-yaml --stdin-file-path <file>` for JSON-to-YAML views.\n\n## Install\n\nThe extension is not yet published to an extension marketplace. Install the\nYamark command from PyPI, then build and install the extension from a checkout:\n\n```sh\nuv tool install yamark\ncd editors/vscode\nYAMARK_BUNDLE=0 npm run install:local\n```\n\nFor Positron, use `YAMARK_BUNDLE=0 npm run install:positron`. Reload the editor\nafter installation.\n\n## Commands\n\nThe extension contributes:\n\n| Command | Effect |\n| --- | --- |\n| `Yamark: Format Document` | Run the Yamark document formatter for the active file. |\n| `Yamark: Format Selection as Markdown` | Format the active non-empty selection as Markdown only. |\n| `Yamark: Preview Format Document` | Run the same formatting stages as Format Document and open the result as a read-only snapshot. Supports Markdown, R Markdown, Quarto, YAML, Python, and R. |\n| `Yamark: View JSON as YAML` | Project JSON, JSONC, JSON5, JSONL, or NDJSON to formatted YAML in a read-only view. |\n| `Yamark: Open Filtered Working Tree Diff` | Compare an unstaged file with its smudged Git index baseline. |\n| `Yamark: Show Log` | Open the Yamark output channel. |\n\n`Yamark: Format Selection as Markdown` does not run configured native formatter\nchains. It is for prompt text, comments, or Markdown-like prose inside a\nbroader source file.\n\n## Read-only previews\n\nRight-click a supported file in the Explorer or its editor tab. Use\n`Yamark: Preview Format Document` for Yamark's native file types, or\n`Yamark: View JSON as YAML` for JSON, JSONC, JSON5, JSONL, and NDJSON.\n\n`Yamark: Preview Format Document` runs the same formatting stages as Format\nDocument, including the configured next formatter, but opens the final text\ninstead of applying an edit. `Yamark: View JSON as YAML` sends the current\neditor buffer to `yamark to-yaml` and opens the resulting YAML. Both commands\ninclude unsaved source edits in the initial view and do not change the source\nor create a temporary file. JSONL and NDJSON views then follow the source file\non disk and refresh the same read-only view as records are appended. Other\npreviews refresh only when run again.\n\nJSON-family previews use YAML syntax highlighting. JSONC and JSON5 comments\nbecome YAML comments. Each JSONL or NDJSON record becomes one document in a\nYAML stream.\n\nPreview commands do not use `yamark.enabledFileExtensions`. The JSON-to-YAML\nprojection does not run the configured next formatter, apply\n`yamark.extraArguments`, or interpret embedded formatter directives.\nJSON-family files remain excluded from Format Document and format-on-save.\n\n## Git filter diffs\n\nFor a path managed by `filter=yamark-md`, VS Code's built-in unstaged preview\ncan show wrapping changes that are not part of the Git diff. Right-click the\nfile under **Changes** and run `Yamark: Open Filtered Working Tree Diff`.\n\nSee [Git Filter: VS Code diff preview](git-filter.qmd#vs-code-diff-preview) for\nthe clean/smudge details and the limits of this command.\n\n## Executable\n\nThe extension runs `yamark` from `PATH` by default. To use another binary, set\nan explicit executable:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"yamark.executable\": \"/path/to/yamark\"\n}\n```\n\nThe extension can also use a bundled executable under\n`bin/<platform>-<arch>/` when a VSIX package includes one. Enable that path\nwith:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"yamark.useBundledExecutable\": true\n}\n```\n\n`yamark.useBundledExecutable` defaults to `false`, so the extension uses\n`yamark.executable` unless configured otherwise.\n\n## File extensions\n\nBy default Yamark is enabled for Markdown, Quarto, and YAML:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"yamark.enabledFileExtensions\": [\".md\", \".qmd\", \".yaml\", \".yml\"]\n}\n```\n\nOpt into R Markdown, R, and Python by adding extensions:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"yamark.enabledFileExtensions\": [\n    \".md\",\n    \".qmd\",\n    \".yaml\",\n    \".yml\",\n    \".rmd\",\n    \".r\",\n    \".py\"\n  ]\n}\n```\n\nFor `.r` and `.py`, Yamark formats explicitly marked embedded Markdown comment\nblocks and string literals. It does not format surrounding source code unless\nyou configure a second formatter.\n\n## Format on save\n\nSet Yamark as the default formatter for each language it should handle:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"yamark.useBundledExecutable\": false,\n  \"[markdown]\": {\n    \"editor.defaultFormatter\": \"yamark.yamark\",\n    \"editor.formatOnSave\": true\n  },\n  \"[yaml]\": {\n    \"editor.defaultFormatter\": \"yamark.yamark\",\n    \"editor.formatOnSave\": true\n  },\n  \"[quarto]\": {\n    \"editor.defaultFormatter\": \"yamark.yamark\",\n    \"editor.formatOnSave\": true\n  }\n}\n```\n\nManual `Format Document` and save-time formatting both go through the Yamark\nprovider.\n\n## Extra arguments\n\nPass CLI formatter options through `yamark.extraArguments`:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"yamark.extraArguments\": [\"--wrap\", \"sentence\"]\n}\n```\n\nArguments are inserted after `yamark format` and before\n`--stdin-file-path <file>`. They also apply to Preview Format Document because\nthat command uses the same formatting pipeline.\n\n## Formatter chaining\n\nYamark can run one stdin/stdout formatter after itself. This is useful when\nYamark formats embedded Markdown in a Python or R file and Ruff or Air should\nthen format the surrounding source.\n\nThe chain is fixed:\n\n1. Yamark runs first.\n2. If `yamark.runNextFormatter` is true and\n   `yamark.nextFormatterExecutable` is configured, that executable runs on\n   Yamark's output.\n3. The extension returns one combined edit to VS Code.\n\n`yamark.runNextFormatter` defaults to `true`. With no\n`yamark.nextFormatterExecutable`, Yamark runs alone.\n\n```json\n{\n  \"yamark.enabledFileExtensions\": [\".md\", \".qmd\", \".yaml\", \".yml\", \".r\", \".py\"],\n  \"[r]\": {\n    \"editor.defaultFormatter\": \"yamark.yamark\",\n    \"editor.formatOnSave\": true,\n    \"yamark.nextFormatterExecutable\": [\n      \"${extension:posit.air-vscode}/bundled/bin/air${exe}\",\n      \"format\",\n      \"--stdin-file-path\",\n      \"${file}\"\n    ]\n  },\n  \"[python]\": {\n    \"editor.defaultFormatter\": \"yamark.yamark\",\n    \"editor.formatOnSave\": true,\n    \"yamark.nextFormatterExecutable\": [\n      \"${extension:charliermarsh.ruff}/bundled/libs/bin/ruff${exe}\",\n      \"format\",\n      \"--stdin-filename\",\n      \"${file}\",\n      \"-\"\n    ]\n  }\n}\n```\n\n`yamark.nextFormatterExecutable` is an argv array, not a shell string. Put each\nexecutable and argument in its own array element.\n\nPlaceholders:\n\n| Placeholder | Expands to |\n| --- | --- |\n| `${file}` | Absolute path to the active file. |\n| `${fileDirname}` | Absolute directory containing the active file. |\n| `${exe}` | `.exe` on Windows, empty string elsewhere. |\n| `${extension:publisher.name}` | Install path for a VS Code extension, for example `${extension:posit.air-vscode}`. |\n\nYamark does not chain through VS Code formatter commands or provider\nfallthrough because VS Code does not expose a stable API for running another\nformatter second and returning one final save-time edit.\n\n## Logs\n\nOpen `View -> Output -> Yamark`, or run `Yamark: Show Log`. Formatting and\nPreview Format Document logs record the file, Yamark invocation, optional\nfollow-up formatter, changes, and errors. usize;\n                let c = self.peek();\n                let is_seq = c == b'-' && matches!(self.peek_at(1), b' ' | b'\\t' | b'\\n' | 0);\n                let ok = ind > parent || (ctx == Ctx::MapValue && is_seq && ind == parent);\n                if !ok {\n                    self.pos = ls;\n                    let mut n = self.null_node();\n                    n.start = start;\n node.col = col;\n                node.props = props;\n                return Ok(node);\n            }\n        }\n        let mut node = self.parse_block_content(parent, ctx)?;\n        if props.is_some() {\n            node.start = start;\n            node.line = line;\n            node.col = col;\n            node.props = props;\n        }\n        Ok(node)\n    }\n\n    fn null_node(&self) -> Node {\n        Node {\n            start: self.pos,\n            end: self.pos,\n            line: self.line_of(self.pos.min(self.b.len().saturating_sub(1)).max(0)),\n            col: 0,\n            props: None,\n            kind: Kind::Null,\n            comment: None,\n            flow_has_comment: false,\n            end_line: 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Parse block content at the current position (content start, after properties).\n    fn parse_block_content(&mut self, parent: isize, ctx: Ctx) -> PResult<Node> {\n        let start = self.pos;\n        let col = self.col_of(start);\n        let c = self.peek();\n        if c == b'-' && matches!(self.peek_at(1), b' ' | b'\\t' | b'\\n' | 0) {\n            return self.parse_block_seq(col);\n        }\n        if self.parse_block_scalar(parent);\n        }\n        // Possibly an implicit key: look ahead for \"key:\" on this line.\n        if self.implicit_key_ahead() {\n            return self.parse_block_map(col, parent);\n        }\n        if c == b'[' || c == b'{' {\n            let mut n = self.parse_flow_collection()?;\n            n.comment = self.eat_line_rest()?;\n            return Ok(n);\n        }\n        let _ = ctx;\n        let mut n = self.parse_inline_scalar_or_alias(parent, true)?;\n        n.comment = self.eat_line_rest()?;\n        Ok(n)\n    }\n\n    /// Check whether the current line holds an implicit mapping key at the current position.\n    fn implicit_key_ahead(&mut self) -> bool {\n        let save = self.pos;\n        let r = self.try_scan_implicit_key();\n        self.pos = save;\n        r\n    }\n\n    fn try_scan_implicit_key(&mut self) -> bool {\n        let c = self.peek();\n        let ok = if c == b'[' || c == b'{' {\n            self.skip_flow_raw().is_ok()\n        } else if c == b'\"' || c == b'\\'' {\n            match self.scan_quoted_end() {\n                Some(e) => {\n                    // Implicit keys must be single-line.\n                    if self.src[self.pos..e].contains('\\n') {\n                        return false;\n                    }\n                    self.pos = e;\n                    true\n                }\n                None => false,\n            }\n        } else if c == b'*' {\n            while self.pos < self.b.len() && !matches!(self.b[self.pos], b' ' | b'\\t' | b'\\n') && !is_flow_ind(self.b[self.pos]) {\n                self.pos += 1;\n            }\n            true\n        } else if c == b'&' || c == b'!' {\n            // Properties before a key.\n            if self.parse_props().ok().flatten().map(|p| p.newline_after).unwrap_or(true) {\n                return false;\n            }\n            self.skip_inline_ws();\n            return           let mut prev_space = false;\n            while i < le {\n                let ch = self.b[i];\n                if ch == b':' && (i + 1 >= le || matches!(self.b[i + 1], b' ' | b'\\t')) {\n                    self.pos = i;\n                    break;\n                }\n                if ch == b'#' && prev_space {\n                    return false;\n                }\n                prev_space = is_ws(ch);\n                i += 1;\n            }\n            if i >= le {\n                return false;\n            }\n            true\n        };\n        if !ok {\n            return false;\n        }\n        self.skip_inline_ws();\n        self.peek() == b':' && matches!(self.peek_at(1), b' ' | b'\\t' | b'\\n' | 0)\n    }\n\n    fn scan_quoted_end(&self) -> Option<usize> {\n        let q = self.b[self.pos];\n        let mut i = self.pos + 1;\n        while i < self.b.len() {\n            let c = self.b[i];\n            if q == b'\\'' {\n                if c == b'\\'' Some(i + 1);\n                }\n            } else {\n                if c == b'\\\\' {\n                    i += 2;\n                    continue;\n                }\n                if c == b'\"' {\n                    return Some(i + 1);\n                }\n            }\n            i += 1;\n        }\n        None\n    }\n\n    fn skip_flow_raw(&mut self) -> PResult<()> {\n        let mut depth = 0i32;\n        loop {\n            if self.at_eof() {\n                return self.err(\"unterminated flow\");\n            }\n            let c = self.peek();\n            match c {\n                b'[' | b'{' => {\n                    depth += 1;\n                    self.pos += 1;\n                }\n                b']' | b'}' => {\n                    depth -= 1;\n                    self.pos += 1;\n                    if depth == 0 {\n                        return Ok(());\n                    }\n                }\n                b'\"' | b'\\'' => match self.scan_quoted_end() {\n                    Some(e) => self.pos = e,\n                    None => return self.err(\"unterminated quote\"),\n                },\n                b'#' => {\n                    if self.pos > 0 && matches!(self.b[self.pos - 1], b' ' | b'\\t' | b'\\n') {\n                        self.pos = self.line_end(self.pos);\n                    } else {\n                        self.pos += 1;\n                    }\n                }\n                _ => self.pos += 1,\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn parse_block_seq(&mut self, col: usize) -> PResult<Node> {\n        let start = self.pos;\n        let line = self.line_of(start);\n        let mut items = Vec::new();\n        loop {\n            // At '-'\n            let istart = self.pos;\n            let iline = self.line_of(istart);\n            self.pos += 1;\n            let save = self.pos;\n            self.skip_inline_ws();\n            let mut dash_comment = None;\n            let value_same_line;\n        let n = self.skip_trivia_lines();\n                trivia_before_value = n > 0;\n                value_same_line = false;\n            } else {\n                value_same_line = true;\n            }\n            let value = if value_same_line {\n                self.parse_block_node(col as isize, Ctx::SeqItem)?\n            } else {\n                // Content on next lines must be indented                let ind = self.line_indent(ls);\n                    if ind > col {\n                        self.parse_block_node(col as isize, Ctx::SeqItem)?\n                    } else {\n                        self.null_node()\n                    }\n                }\n            };\n            let iend = if matches!(value.kind, Kind::Null) && value.props.is_none() {\n                istart + 1\n            } else {\n                value.end\n            };\n            let end_line = self.line_of(iend.saturating_sub(1).max(istart));\n            items.push(Item {\n                line:     end: iend,\n                end_line,\n            });\n            // Next item?\n            self.skip_trivia_lines();\n            if self.at_eof() {\n                break;\n            }\n parse_block_map(&mut self, col: usize, parent: isize) -> PResult<Node> {\n        let _ = parent;\n        let start = self.pos;\n        let line = self.line_of(start);\n        let mut entries = comment: None,\n            flow_has_comment: false,\n            end_line,\n        })\n    }\n\n    fn parse_implicit_key(&mut self) -> PResult<Node> {\n        let start = self.pos;\n        let    node.start = start;\n            node.col = col;\n            node.props = props;\n        }\n        Ok(node)\n    }\n\n    fn parse_alias(&mut self) -> PResult<Node> {\n        let s =            line,\n            col: self.col_of(s),\n            props: None,\n            kind: Kind::Alias(self.src[s + 1..self.pos].to_string()),\n            comment: None,\n            flow_has_comment: false,\n            end_line: line,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Parse a plain/quoted scalar or alias in block context (value position).\n    fn parse_inline_scalar_or_alias(&mut           return self.parse_quoted(parent);\n        }\n        self.parse_plain_block(parent, block)\n    }\n\n    fn parse_quoted(&mut self, parent: isize) -> PResult<Node> {\n        let s = self.pos;\n        let line = self.line_of(s);\n        let e = match self.scan_quoted_end() {\n            Some(e) => e,\n            None => return self.err(\"unterminated quoted scalar\"),\n        };\n        let raw = &self.src[s..e];\n        // Continuation lines must be indented more than the parent.\n        if raw.contains('\\n') {\n            for (i, l) in raw.split('\\n').enumerate() parse_plain_block(&mut self, parent: isize, _block: bool) -> PResult<Node> {\n        let s = self.pos;\n        let line = self.line_of(s);\n        let c = self.peek();\n        // Indicators that scalar start\");\n        }\n        let mut end = self.scan_plain_line(self.pos)?;\n        let mut lines: Vec<(usize, usize)> = vec![(s, end)];\n        // Continuation lines.\n        let mut p = < self.b.len() && self.b[q] == b'#' {\n                break;\n            }\n            if q >= self.b.len() || self.b[q] != b'\\n' {\n                break;\n            }\n            // Skip         let le = self.line_end(ls);\n                if self.src[ls..le].trim_matches([' ', '\\t']).is_empty() {\n                    blank_lines += 1;\n                    ls = if le < self.b.len() { le + 1 } else { le };\n                } else {\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n            if ls >= self.b.len() {\n                break;\n            }\n        let cs = ls + ind as usize;\n            let mut cs2 = cs;\n            while cs2 < self.b.len() && is_ws(self.b[cs2]) {\n                cs2 += 1;\n            }\n            if self.b[cs2] == b'#' {\n                break;\n            }\n            let le = self.scan_plain_line(cs2)?;\n            // A continuation line that looks like a mapping key is an error.\n            if le < self.b.len() && self.b[le] == b':' {\n                return self.err(\"mapping value in plain scalar\");\n            }\n            let _ = blank_lines;\n            lines.push((cs2, le));\n kind: Kind::Scalar(Scalar {\n                style: ScalarStyle::Plain,\n                start: s,\n                end,\n                value,\n                multiline: lines.len() > 1,\n                block: None,\n            }),\n            comment: None,\n            flow_has_comment: false,\n            end_line,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Scan a plain scalar on one line from `start`; returns end (trailing spaces trimmed).\n    fn scan_plain_line(&self, start: usize) -> PResult<usize> {\n        let le = self.line_end(start);\n        let mut i = start;\n        let mut last_non_ws     }\n        if i < le && self.b[i] == b':' {\n            // \"key: value\" inside a value position.\n            return Err(ParseError { pos: i, msg: \"unexpected mapping value\".into() });\n
