JSON-to-YAML projection has a different contract: it parses a\n35\tJSON-family input and emits formatted YAML for inspection or conversion.\n36\t\n37\tUse `yamark to-yaml --stdin-file-path` to project JSON-family input from stdin\n38\tto formatted YAML on stdout:\n39\t\n40\t```sh\n41\tyamark to-yaml --stdin-file-path data.json < data.json\n42\t```\n43\t\n44\tThe command does not read or write the path. It uses the extension to select\n45\tone exact input grammar:\n46\t\n47\t| Extension | Accepted input |\n48\t| --- | --- |\n49\t| `.json` | Strict JSON. |\n50\t| `.jsonc` | JSON with line comments, block comments, and trailing commas. Other JSON5 syntax is rejected. |\n51\t| `.json5` | JSON5 strings, identifiers, numbers, comments, and trailing commas. |\n52\t| `.jsonl` and `.ndjson` | One strict JSON value per physical line. Blank records are rejected. |\n53\t\n54\tObject member order and duplicate names are preserved. JSON and JSONC keep the\n55\tsource spelling of numbers. JSON5 spellings that YAML would interpret\n56\tdifferently are normalized, including `0X` hexadecimal prefixes, leading or\n57\ttrailing decimal points, unary plus, `Infinity`, and `NaN`. Negative\n58\thexadecimal integers are emitted in decimal because YAML would otherwise treat\n59\tthem as strings.\n60\t\n61\tJSONC and JSON5 comments become YAML comments. JSONL and NDJSON output a YAML\n62\tdocument-start marker before every record. A record may be an object, array, or\n63\tscalar; this does not change how ordinary YAML such as `1\\n2` is interpreted by\n64\t`yamark format`.\n65\t\n66\tString escapes are decoded before YAML emission. Lone UTF-16 surrogate escapes\n67\tare rejected because they do not represent Unicode scalar values. All\n68\tJSON-family inputs reject nesting deeper than 256 levels. JSON5 also rejects\n69\tlegacy numeric escapes such as `\\1`, invalid escaped identifier characters, and\n70\tU+0085 as whitespace. Characters that YAML cannot carry inside a comment are\n71\tshown as visible hexadecimal escapes.\n72\t\n73\tProjection does not scan JSON strings or comments for embedded Markdown or\n74\tformatter directives, and it does not dispatch to Prettier or another embedded\n75\tformatter.\n76\t\n77\t`yamark format` continues to skip JSON-family paths and never rewrites them.\n78\t`Yamark: View JSON as YAML` in VS Code and Positron uses the same JSON-to-YAML\n79\tprojection.\n80\t\n81\t## Markdown\n82\t\n83\t| Construct | Result | Details |\n84\t| --- | --- | --- |\n85\t| Paragraphs | Formats | Wraps by column, paragraph, sentence, or not at all, according to the active Markdown settings. |\n86\t| ATX headings | Formats | Normalizes spacing. Yamark\n362\tinserts a leading `---` document-start marker before every record, including\n363\tthe first, producing a valid YAML multi-document stream. The example below uses\n364\trecords from agent runs.\n365\t\n366\t:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n367\t**Before**\n368\t\n369\t```yaml\n370\t{\"id\":1,\"profile\":{\"name\":\"planner\",\"active\":true}}\n371\t{\"id\":2,\"profile\":{\"name\":\"researcher\",\"active\":true},\"usage\":{\"input_tokens\":640,\"output_tokens\":128}}\n372\t{\"id\":3,\"profile\":{\"name\":\"reviewer\",\"active\":true,\"model\":\"gpt-5\",\"region\":\"us\",\"tools\":[\"search\",\"python\"]},\"events\":[{\"type\":\"tool_call\",\"tools\":[\"search\",\"open\",\"python\",\"write\"]},{\"type\":\"usage\",\"tokens\":{\"input\":900,\"output\":240}},{\"type\":\"completion\",\"status\":\"ok\"}]}\n373\t```\n374\t\n375\t**After**\n376\t\n377\t```yaml\n378\t---\n379\t{id: 1, profile: {name: planner, active: true}}\n380\t---\n381\tid: 2\n382\tprofile: {name: researcher, active: true}\n383\tusage: {input_tokens: 640, output_tokens: 128}\n384\t---\n385\tid: 3\n386\tprofile:\n387\t  name: reviewer\n388\t  active: true\n389\t  model: gpt-5\n390\t  region: us\n391\t  tools: [search, python]\n392\tevents:\n393\t  - {type: tool_call, tools: [search, open, python, write]}\n394\t  - {type: usage, tokens: {input: 900, output: 240}}\n395\t  - {type: completion, status: ok}\n396\t```\n397\t::::\n398\t\n399\tYamark keeps each document as compact as the width allows. The first record\n400\tstays in flow style; the second expands only its root mapping; the third also\n401\texpands `profile` and `events`. Smaller mappings and sequences remain in flow\n402\tstyle whenever they still fit within `--line-width`. This conversion is for\n403\tobject records, not arbitrary JSON values.\n404\t\n405\t### Aligned flow-mapping tables\n406\t\n407\tA sequence of similar flow mappings can be easier to scan as a table. Put a small `fmt:` directive next to\n10\tthe text it controls, then let an editor or repository integration run Yamark.\n11\tBecause directives are comments, the formatting choice stays with the text.\n12\tThe comment marker depends on the file:\n13\t\n14\t| File | Directive comment |\n15\t| --- | --- |\n16\t| Markdown and Quarto | `<!-- fmt: ... -->` |\n17\t| YAML, Python, and R | `# fmt: ...` |\n18\t\n19\tQuarto chunk options use `#|`; for example, `#| fmt: skip`.\n20\t\n21\t## Target the next value or block\n22\t\n23\tMost directives apply to the next supported target. In a YAML file, that target\n24\tis usually a scalar node. In a Python or R file, it is usually a string literal\n25\tor a contiguous source-comment block. The directive does not format the\n26\tsurrounding Python or R source code.\n27\t\n28\t## YAML files\n29\t\n30\tMark a scalar as Markdown and choose sentence wrapping for that scalar:\n31\t\n32\t```yaml\n33\t# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence\n34\tdescription: \"Explain the project in a few clear sentences.\"\n35\tother_value: \"This is ordinary YAML, not Markdown.\"\n36\t```\n37\t\n38\tThe directive attaches to `description`, the next scalar. A tagged scalar is\n39\tanother way to mark Markdown when the setting should travel with the value:\n40\t\n41\t```yaml\n42\tinstructions: !markdown |\n43\t  # Review\n44\t\n45\t  Read the diff and report concrete correctness issues.\n46\t```\n47\t\n48\tUse the same placement for an embedded formatter. Python outside the\n81\tmarked target is left for a Python formatter such as Ruff.\n82\t\n83\tThe same directive can target a Markdown comment block:\n84\t\n85\t```python\n86\t# fmt: markdown\n87\t# # Filters\n88\t#\n89\t# Apply the most specific filter first.\n90\t#\n91\t# - Each filter is a single expression.\n92\t```\n93\t\n94\tFor a non-Markdown embedded language, use its formatter name:\n95\t\n96\t```python\n97\t# fmt: r\n98\tanalysis = \"\"\"\n99\tf <- function(x) x + 1\n100\t\"\"\"\n101\t```\n102\t\n103\t## R files\n104\t\n105\tR uses the same `# fmt:` marker. YAML, Python, and R\n168\tuse the same hash-comment form:\n169\t\n170\t```text\n171\t# fmt: skip file\n172\t```\n173\t\n174\tMarkdown uses an HTML comment:\n175\t\n176\t```markdown\n177\t<!-- fmt: skip file -->\n178\t```\n179\t\n180\tA whole-file skip is useful for generated files or files whose layout is\n181\tintentionally outside Yamark's scope.\n182\t\n183\tMarkdown skip controls retain trailing spaces and line endings in the selected\n184\tcontent, including supported nested Markdown.\n185\t\n186\t## Preserve intentional table widths\n187\t\n188\tYamark normally fits table columns to their contents. Keep a table's authored\n189\twidths while still formatting its contents:\n190\t\n191\t```markdown\n192\t<!-- fmt: table-widths=preserve scope=next -->\n193\t+----------+------------------+\n194\t| Name     | Description      |\n195\t+==========+==================+\n196\t| A        | Short text       |\n197\t+----------+------------------+\n198\t```\n199\t\n200\tUse `scope=file` to preserve widths throughout the document, or\n201\t`scope=from-here` for subsequent tables. A later\n202\t`table-widths=fit scope=from-here` resumes fitting widths. Both modes retain\n203\tcolumn alignment. Fitting widths can change the rendered proportions of\n204\tPandoc tables; preserving widths can retain excessive or cramped padding.\n205\t\n206\tFor Markdown inside YAML, Python, or R, the same option can accompany the\n207\ttarget marker: `# fmt: markdown table-widths=preserve`.\n208\t\n209\t## Set file-specific Markdown options\n210\t\n211\tUse `scope=file` when the file should have a different Markdown policy from the\n212\trepository default:\n213\t\n214\t```markdown\n215\t<!-- fmt: wrap=sentence:72 scope=file -->\n216\t```\n217\t\n218\tThis puts one sentence per line and wraps long sentences at column 72. Other\n219\tfile-wide Markdown options include `canonical=true` and\n220\t`footnotes=preserve`:\n221\t\n222\t```markdown\n223\t<!-- fmt: canonical=true footnotes=preserve scope=file -->\n224\t```\n225\t\n226\tFor a YAML file or a hashpipe YAML stream in Python or R, use the same scope to\n227\tset YAML behavior for the whole file:\n228\t\n229\t```yaml\n230\t# fmt: compact=false scope=file\n231\t```\n232\t\n233\tAn option-only directive such as `# fmt: canonical=true` adjusts the next\n234\talready-marked Markdown scalar. It does not turn an ordinary YAML scalar into a\n235\tMarkdown target:\n236\t\n237\t```yaml\n238\t# fmt: canonical=true\n239\tfirst: !markdown \"This is __strong__ Markdown.\"\n240\tsecond: \"This is ordinary YAML text.\"\n241\t```\n242\t\n243\t## Arrange for Yamark to run automatically\n244\t\n245\tOnce directives are in the files, configure Yamark to run as part of the\n246\tworkflow:\n247\t\n248\t- In an editor, enable format on save. Both modes preserve column alignment and multiline\n40\tcell breaks.\n41\t\n42\t`preserve` retains the source widths while still formatting cell contents.\n43\tFor Pandoc tables, this keeps the borders and gaps that determine widths. A later `table-widths=fit scope=from-here` resumes fitting widths.\n61\tWithout an explicit scope, this option follows the usual Markdown directive\n62\tdefault of `scope=file`.\n63\t\n64\tThe setting also works in front matter, `yamark.toml`, and the command line.\n65\tExplicit renderer settings such as Quarto's `tbl-colwidths` remain unchanged.\n66\t`fmt: skip` preserves the entire table when exact source layout matters.\n67\tUnsupported table structures remain unchanged in either mode.\n68\t\n69\t### Canonical and footnote values\n70\t\n71\t`canonical` accepts `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0` in front matter\n72\tand directives. A bare `canonical` directive means `canonical=true`. Canonical\n73\tmode rewrites supported `_emphasis_` and `__strong__` spans as `*emphasis*` and\n74\t`**strong**`. It preserves protected or unsupported spans, including intraword\n75\tunderscores, code spans, link destinations, raw HTML, and template content.\n76\t\n77\tFor `footnotes`, `wrap`, `format`, `true`, `yes`, and `1` format footnote\n78\tdefinitions. `preserve`, `none`, `false`, `no`, and `0` preserve them.\n79\t`--preserve-footnotes` preserves Markdown footnote definitions byte-for-byte.\n80\t\n81\t## YAML settings\n82\t\n83\t| Behavior | Control | Default | Effect |\n84\t| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n85\t| Structural line width | `--line-width <n>` | 80 | Expands block-renderable flow collections when they exceed the width. Over-width flow collections that cannot be rendered safely in block style may be preserved. Also bounds compact and layout-repair output. |\n86\t| Folded scalar prose width | `--prose-width <n>` | 72 | Wraps eligible folded YAML prose. |\n87\t| Block indentation | `--indent-width <n>` | 2 | Sets indentation for emitted block mappings and sequences. |\n88\t| Compact collections | `--compact`, `[format].compact`, or `fmt: compact` | Off | Collapses eligible block collections to flow style when they fit. |\n89\t| Aligned flow mappings | `fmt: table` or `fmt: compact table` | Off | Aligns a following sequence of compatible flow mappings. The compact form first collapses eligible block rows. |\n90\t\n91\tAll width and indentation values must be positive integers.\n92\t\n93\tCanonical mode also permits limited rewrapping of short existing folded YAML\n94\tprose scalars when their value stays unchanged.\n95\t\n96\t## Execution controls\n97\t\n98\t| Control | Effect |\n99\t| --- | --- |\n100\t| `--diagnostics` | For YAML input, emits trace counters; it also emits notes for skipped or failing optional embedded formatters. |\n101\t| `--skip-embedded-formatters` | Disables external formatters while keeping Yamark's Markdown, YAML, front matter, and recursive Markdown formatting active. |\n102\t| `--config <path>` | Uses one explicit `yamark.toml` for all selected files instead of discovering one per file. |\n103\t\n104\t### Embedded formatter controls\n105\t\n106\t| Need | Control |\n107\t| --- | --- |\n108\t| Select a target | Use a recognized Markdown fence language or a [`fmt: <name>` directive](reference-directives.qmd#templates-and-embedded-formatters). |\n109\t| Register or replace a formatter | Add an [`[embedded.<name>]` table](reference-config.qmd#embedded) to `yamark.toml`. |\n110\t| Disable external formatters for one run | Pass `--skip-embedded-formatters`. |\n111\t| Explain an optional formatter skip | Pass `--diagnostics`. |\n112\t\n113\tWrite, check, diff, and stdin behavior is documented under\n114\t[Command line](cli-help.qmd#modes-output-and-status).\n115\t\n116\t## Document Markdown options\n117\t\n118\tMarkdown front matter can set document-local options under\n119\t`editor_options.markdown`:\n120\t\n121\t```markdown\n122\t---\n123\teditor_options:\n124\t  markdown:\n125\t    wrap: sentence:72\n126\t    canonical: true\n127\t    footnotes: preserve\n128\t    table-widths: preserve\n129\t---\n130\tThis is __strong__. Invalid `yamark.toml` keys or\n142\tdirective values are errors instead.\n143\t\n144\tThese options apply after the front matter to the Markdown body, recursive\n145\t`markdown` or `md` fences, and Markdown-valued YAML scalars in nested YAML\n146\tregions.\n147\t\n148\tYamark also reads `editor.markdown` for compatibility, but only when\n149\t`editor_options.markdown` is absent. JSON-to-YAML projection has a different contract: it parses a\n35\tJSON-family input and emits formatted YAML for inspection or conversion.\n36\t\n37\tUse `yamark to-yaml --stdin-file-path` to project JSON-family input from stdin\n38\tto formatted YAML on stdout:\n39\t\n40\t```sh\n41\tyamark to-yaml --stdin-file-path data.json < data.json\n42\t```\n43\t\n44\tThe command does not read or write the path. JSON5 spellings that YAML would interpret\n56\tdifferently are normalized, including `0X` hexadecimal prefixes, leading or\n57\ttrailing decimal points, unary plus, `Infinity`, and `NaN`. Built-in aliases include `ruff`, `air`, `mdformat`, and the\n176\t`prettier` family.\n177\t\n178\t| Target name or fence language | Built-in formatter |\n179\t| --- | --- |\n180\t| `python`, `ruff` | Ruff |\n181\t| `r`, `air` | Air |\n182\t| `mdformat` | mdformat |\n183\t| `json`, `prettier-json` | Prettier with a `.json` path |\n184\t| `jsonc`, `prettier-jsonc` | Prettier with a `.jsonc` path |\n185\t| `json5`, `prettier-json5` | Prettier with a `.json5` path |\n186\t| `graphql`, `gql`, `graphqls`, `prettier-graphql` | Prettier with a `.graphql` path |\n187\t| `css`, `prettier-css` | Prettier with a `.css` path |\n188\t| `scss`, `prettier-scss` | Prettier with a `.scss` path |\n189\t| `less`, `prettier-less` | Prettier with a `.less` path |\n190\t| `postcss`, `pcss`, `prettier-postcss` | Prettier with a `.pcss` path |\n191\t| `html`, `prettier-html` | Prettier with a `.html` path |\n192\t| `js`, `javascript`, `prettier-js` | Prettier with a `.js` path |\n193\t| `jsx`, `prettier-jsx` | Prettier with a `.jsx` path |\n194\t| `ts`, `typescript`, `prettier-ts` | Prettier with a `.ts` path |\n195\t| `tsx`, `prettier-tsx` | Prettier with a `.tsx` path |\n196\t\n197\tMarkdown fences named `markdown` or `md` are formatted recursively instead of\n198\tusing mdformat. An [`[embedded.<name>]`](reference-config.qmd#embedded) entry\n199\treplaces the built-in mapping for that exact name.\n200\t\n201\tThe default aliases are optional. A configured formatter is also optional when\n202\tits command's first argv item is exactly `ruff`, `air`, `mdformat`, or\n203\t`prettier`. A missing executable or nonzero exit preserves the target for\n204\teither kind. Yamark reports the reason as a note only with `--diagnostics`.\n205\t\n206\tA successful process that writes to stderr is an error. Any other configured\n207\tformatter is strict: a missing executable or nonzero exit is an error. These\n208\tformatter errors happen before Yamark writes the formatted file. See the\n209\t[`[embedded]` schema](reference-config.qmd#embedded) and\n210\t[`--skip-embedded-formatters`](reference-options.qmd#execution-controls).\n211\t\n212\t## Layout repair\n213\t\n214\tYamark recognizes two narrow layout cues. Only the unmatched opener is a repair\n215\tfor ill-formed input:\n216\t\n217\t- An unmatched `[` or `{` where a block sequence or mapping begins as a mapping\n218\t  value or sequence item asks Yamark to collapse that one collection to flow\n219\t  style.\n220\t- A physical newline inside a complete flow collection is valid multiline YAML.\n221\t  It asks Yamark to expand that collection to block style. Compact mode\n222\t  suppresses this multiline intent.\n223\t\n224\tThe opener may be on the value line or on the following line after an empty\n225\tmapping value header. Adjacent forms such as `tags:[` and `tags:{` are not\n226\tlayout hints.\n227\t\n228\tWhen the requested flow form fits the available `--line-width`, Yamark removes\n229\tthe unmatched opener and emits the collection in flow style. Otherwise it\n230\tpreserves the hinted collection as typed. It does not fail solely because the\n231\trequested flow form is too wide, and surrounding YAML may still be formatted.\n232\tThe [layout examples](examples.qmd#collapse-to-flow-by-typing-a-bracket) show\n233\teach accepted gesture before and after formatting.\n234\t\n235\t## Failure behavior\n236\t\n237\tYamark is a formatter, not a general validator. It formats supported regions\n238\tand leaves unsupported regions unchanged when they are not explicitly\n239\ttargeted and it has no safe rewrite.\n240\t\n241\tYamark parses YAML before formatting. For Markdown and Markdown-valued YAML\n242\tscalars, it emits only transformations supported by its parser. Allotment gardens are a particularly interesting case: they are small, intensively managed, and extremely heterogeneous, i.e. two neighbouring plots may differ completely in what is grown and how. Previous work by Baldock et al. (2019) found that allotments supported more bee species per unit area than any other urban land-use type they surveyed! But does this hold in a northern European city with a short growing season? That is the question we set out to answer in the 2023 season.\n\nWe surveyed `r n_distinct(visits$plot_id)` plots in `r n_distinct(visits$site)` allotment sites in Uppsala between May and September. Each plot was visited on average 6.5 times (range 4--9), and each visit consisted of a 15-minute timed observation of a 2 x 2 m quadrat. It formats whole files and embedded content, keeping source readable and changes easy to review. Regions without a supported rewrite stay unchanged.\n\nFor supported embedded code, Yamark can also call Ruff, Air, Prettier, or another configured formatter.\n\nSee the [documentation](https://t-kalinowski.github.io/yamark/) for examples, configuration, editor integrations, and the full syntax reference.\n\n## Install\n\nWith [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) installed, run Yamark directly from [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/yamark/) without a separate install:\n\n```sh\nuvx yamark format config.yaml docs/\n```\n\nThis formats the selected files in place. To install a persistent `yamark` command:\n\n```sh\nuv tool install yamark\n```\n\n## Usage\n\nThe examples below use an installed `yamark` command. To keep running from PyPI without installing it, replace `yamark` with `uvx yamark`.\n\nFormat one or more files or directories in place:\n\n```sh\nyamark format config.yaml docs/\n```\n\nFormat the current directory:\n\n```sh\nyamark format\n```\n\nCheck whether files are already formatted without writing changes:\n\n```sh\nyamark format --check docs/\n```\n\nShow a unified diff without writing changes:\n\n```sh\nyamark format --diff docs/\n```\n\nFormat stdin for editor and CI integrations:\n\n```sh\nyamark format --stdin-file-path config.yaml < config.yaml\n```\n\nConvert JSON-family input from stdin to formatted YAML on stdout:\n\n```sh\nyamark to-yaml --stdin-file-path data.json5 < data.json5\n```\n\nThe path is not read or written. Its suffix selects the exact JSON dialect. This is a conversion, not source formatting.\n\nDirectory traversal skips hidden paths and respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and global Git ignore files by default. Pass a hidden path explicitly to format it.\n\nWhile formatting is enabled, standalone `{{< ... >}}` and `{{% ... %}}` shortcode tokens are preserved, including multiline tokens and quoted arguments. Directive-looking text inside a recognized token is data. Yamark does not match shortcode names or interpret their bodies: Markdown between tokens formats normally. An unterminated token or quote preserves the rest of the enclosing Markdown document or fragment. This does not guarantee rendering equivalence for arbitrary Hugo or Jinja templates.\n\nTo disable body formatting, surround the region with `<!-- fmt: off -->` and `<!-- fmt: on -->`. While formatting is disabled, directives follow the existing linewise policy: a recognized `fmt: on` line resumes formatting even if the surrounding text resembles a shortcode argument, code fence, HTML, or math block.\n\nExplicitly skipped Markdown retains its bytes, including trailing spaces and line endings: `<!-- fmt: skip -->` preserves the next selected node, `<!-- fmt: off -->` preserves the disabled region, and `<!-- fmt: skip file -->` preserves the enclosing Markdown document or fragment. In a YAML file, that target\nis usually a scalar node. In a Python or R file, it is usually a string literal\nor a contiguous source-comment block. The directive does not format the\nsurrounding Python or R source code.\n\n## YAML files\n\nMark a scalar as Markdown and choose sentence wrapping for that scalar:\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence\ndescription: \"Explain the project in a few clear sentences.\"\nother_value: \"This is ordinary YAML, not Markdown.\"\n```\n\nThe directive attaches to `description`, the next scalar. A tagged scalar is\nanother way to mark Markdown when the setting should travel with the value:\n\n```yaml\ninstructions: !markdown |\n  # Review\n\n  Read the diff and report concrete correctness issues.\n```\n\nUse the same placement for an embedded formatter. The formatter name is the\nlanguage after `fmt:`:\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: python\nscript: |\n  def check(items):return all(item > 0 for item in items)\n```\n\nYAML also supports directives on a collection parent when the setting describes\nthe collection rather than a scalar:\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: table\n- {name: alpha, type: string, default: \"\"}\n- {name: beta, type: integer, default: 0}\n```\n\n## Python files\n\nPut `# fmt: markdown` immediately before the string literal or comment block\nthat contains Markdown:\n\n```python\n# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence\nREVIEW_PROMPT = \"\"\"\n# Review\n\nRead the diff and report concrete correctness issues. Prefer specific examples.\n\"\"\"\n```\n\nThe `#` lines inside the string are Markdown content. Python outside the\nmarked target is left for a Python formatter such as Ruff.\n\nThe same directive can target a Markdown comment block:\n\n```python\n# fmt: markdown\n# # Filters\n#\n# Apply the most specific filter first.\n#\n# - Each filter is a single expression.\n```\n\nFor a non-Markdown embedded language, use its formatter name:\n\n```python\n# fmt: r\nanalysis = \"\"\"\nf <- function(x) x + 1\n\"\"\"\n```\n\n## R files\n\nR uses the same `# fmt:` marker. It can target a raw string literal used for a\nvignette, help text, or a Shiny message:\n\n```r\n# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence\nhelp_text <- r\"(\n# Filters\n\nApply the most specific filter first. Explain why a filter matched.\n)\"\n```\n\nIt can also target a contiguous Markdown comment block:\n\n```r\n# fmt: markdown\n# # Filters\n#\n# Apply the most specific filter first.\n#\n# - Each filter is a single expression.\n```\n\nFor source code inside a YAML literal scalar, use the language formatter name\nin the same way as in a YAML file:\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: r\nanalysis: |\n  f <- function(x)x+1\n```\n\n## Control a region or a whole file\n\nThe scope is part of the directive. `next` is the default for target directives.\nUse `from-here` for the rest of a region, and `file` for a document-wide\nsetting:\n\n| Scope | Applies to |\n| --- | --- |\n| `scope=next` | The next supported string, scalar, collection, or comment block. |\n| `scope=from-here` | Supported content from this point until another directive changes the setting. |\n| `scope=file` | The whole file, including supported content before the directive. |\n\nSkip one target:\n\n```yaml\nnormal: [1, 2, 3]\n# fmt: skip\nmanual:\n    -   [ 1,2,3]\n```\n\nPreserve a region and resume formatting afterward:\n\n```markdown\n<!-- fmt: off -->\n#   Keep this heading ##\n\n<!-- fmt: on -->\n```\n\nSkip a whole file by putting the file directive at the top. YAML, Python, and R\nuse the same hash-comment form:\n\n```text\n# fmt: skip file\n```\n\nMarkdown uses an HTML comment:\n\n```markdown\n<!-- fmt: skip file -->\n```\n\nA whole-file skip is useful for generated files or files whose layout is\nintentionally outside Yamark's scope.\n\nMarkdown skip controls retain trailing spaces and line endings in the selected\ncontent, including supported nested Markdown.\n\n## Preserve intentional table widths\n\nYamark normally fits table columns to their contents. Keep a table's authored\nwidths while still formatting its contents:\n\n```markdown\n<!-- fmt: table-widths=preserve scope=next -->\n+----------+------------------+\n| Name     | Description      |\n+==========+==================+\n| A        | Short text       |\n+----------+------------------+\n```\n\nUse `scope=file` to preserve widths throughout the document, or\n`scope=from-here` for subsequent tables. A later\n`table-widths=fit scope=from-here` resumes fitting widths. Both modes retain\ncolumn alignment. Fitting widths can change the rendered proportions of\nPandoc tables; preserving widths can retain excessive or cramped padding.\n\nFor Markdown inside YAML, Python, or R, the same option can accompany the\ntarget marker: `# fmt: markdown table-widths=preserve`.\n\n## Set file-specific Markdown options\n\nUse `scope=file` when the file should have a different Markdown policy from the\nrepository default:\n\n```markdown\n<!-- fmt: wrap=sentence:72 scope=file -->\n```\n\nThis puts one sentence per line and wraps long sentences at column 72. Other\nfile-wide Markdown options include `canonical=true` and\n`footnotes=preserve`:\n\n```markdown\n<!-- fmt: canonical=true footnotes=preserve scope=file -->\n```\n\nFor a YAML file or a hashpipe YAML stream in Python or R, use the same scope to\nset YAML behavior for the whole file:\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: compact=false scope=file\n```\n\nAn option-only directive such as `# fmt: canonical=true` adjusts the next\nalready-marked Markdown scalar. It does not turn an ordinary YAML scalar into a\nMarkdown target:\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: canonical=true\nfirst: !markdown \"This is __strong__ Markdown.\"\nsecond: \"This is ordinary YAML text.\"\n```\n\n## Arrange for Yamark to run automatically\n\nOnce directives are in the files, configure Yamark to run as part of the\nworkflow:\n\n- In an editor, enable format on save. This page is\nan exact syntax lookup. For a guided path through YAML, Python, and R examples,\nsee [Directives](directives.qmd).\n\n## Comment forms\n\n| Host | Form | Placement |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Markdown | `<!-- fmt: ... -->` | An own-line HTML comment. |\n| YAML | `# fmt: ...` | An own-line hash comment. `fmt: table` and `fmt: compact table` may also be same-line comments on an empty-valued collection parent; a populated parent is an error. |\n| Python and R | `# fmt: ...` | An own-line hash comment before a supported comment or string target. |\n\n## Scopes\n\n| Scope | Meaning |\n| --- | --- |\n| `scope=next` | Apply to the next supported target. This is the default for target-selecting, compact, table, and embedded-formatter directives. |\n| `scope=from-here` | Apply from the directive until another directive changes the same state. |\n| `scope=file` | Apply throughout the current parsed document or nested region, including supported nodes before the directive. At the top level, that region is the physical file. |\n\nNot every directive accepts every scope. The tables below list the supported\nforms. An unsupported or misspelled explicit scope is an error. Template\ndelimiter directives use the contextual rule described below instead of one\nfixed default.\n\nScopes stop at the current parsed document or nested-region boundary. A\ndirective inside a recursive fence affects that fence, not its Markdown host or\nsibling fences. A `scope=file` directive inside one hashpipe YAML block does not\nspan later blocks. `fmt: skip file` in Markdown front matter is the exception:\nit preserves the outer Markdown document.\n\n## Preserve content\n\n| Directive | Scope | Effect |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `fmt: skip` | Next | Preserve the next supported target. `fmt: skip scope=next` is equivalent. |\n| `fmt: skip file` | File | Preserve the current parsed document or nested region. `fmt: skip scope=file` is equivalent. |\n| `fmt: off` | From here | Preserve content until `fmt: on`, or through the end of Markdown and source regions. `fmt: off scope=from-here` is equivalent. |\n| `fmt: on` | - | Resume formatting after `fmt: off`. It does not accept an explicit scope. |\n\nThe same control uses the host's comment form:\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: skip\nmanual: [[ 1,2,3], [4,5,6]]\n```\n\n```markdown\n<!-- fmt: off -->\n*   keep\n    this\n    list\n<!-- fmt: on -->\n```\n\nPreserve-control lifecycle checks are host-specific. YAML rejects a targetless\n`skip`, a stray `on`, a nested `off`, and an `off` without a later `on`.\nMarkdown and source regions allow `skip` at the end and let `off` preserve\nthrough the end of the region.\n\n## Markdown targets and settings\n\n| Form | Default scope | Effect |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `fmt: markdown` | Next | Mark the next supported target as Markdown: a Markdown block, including a supported fence; a YAML scalar; or a source string or comment block. |\n| `fmt: markdown wrap=sentence canonical=true` | Next | Mark the next supported target as Markdown and set its options. |\n| `fmt: wrap=sentence` | `scope=next` in YAML; `scope=file` in Markdown or source regions | Change wrapping for an already recognized Markdown region without marking unrelated content. |\n| `fmt: table-widths=preserve` | `scope=next` in YAML; `scope=file` in Markdown or source regions | Preserve widths in supported Markdown tables while formatting contents. Use `scope=next` immediately before one table. |\n| `fmt: canonical` | `scope=next` in YAML; `scope=file` in Markdown or source regions | Enable canonical Markdown spelling. `canonical=true` is equivalent. |\n| `fmt: footnotes=preserve` | `scope=next` in YAML; `scope=file` in Markdown or source regions | Preserve footnote definitions in the affected Markdown. |\n\nOption-only YAML directives tune the next scalar only if it is already marked\nas Markdown:\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: canonical=true\nfirst: !markdown \"This is __strong__.\"\nsecond: \"This is __not__ Markdown.\"\n```\n\nFor `scope=from-here` or `scope=file`, `fmt: markdown` must include at least one\nactual Markdown option. A broad-scope directive changes Markdown settings; it\ndoes not turn every plain scalar into Markdown.\n\nAccepted option values:\n\n| Option | Values |\n| --- | --- |\n| `wrap` | `none`, `paragraph`, `sentence`, `sentence:<n>`, or a positive integer. |\n| `table-widths` | `fit` (the default) or `preserve`. Both preserve alignment. |\n| `canonical` | `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. A bare `canonical` means `true`. |\n| `footnotes` | `wrap`, `format`, `preserve`, `none`, `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. |\n\nFor `footnotes`, `wrap`, `format`, `true`, `yes`, and `1` request formatting;\n`preserve`, `none`, `false`, `no`, and `0` request preservation.\n\n## YAML collections\n\n| Directive | Scope | Effect |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `fmt: compact` | Next | Enable block-to-flow compaction for the next eligible collection. |\n| `fmt: compact false` | Next | Disable compaction for the next eligible collection. `fmt: compact=false` is equivalent. |\n| `fmt: compact scope=from-here` | From here | Enable compaction until another compact directive changes the state. |\n| `fmt: compact=false scope=file` | File | Disable compaction throughout the current YAML document or one source-file hashpipe YAML block. |\n| `fmt: table` | Next | Align the next compatible sequence of flow mappings. |\n| `fmt: compact table` | Next | Collapse eligible block mapping rows before aligning them. `fmt: table compact` and `fmt: table compact=true` are equivalent. |\n\n`fmt: table` accepts only its default next-target scope. Compact directives\naccept `next`, `from-here`, and `file`.\n\n`compact`, `compact=true`, `compact=yes`, `compact=1`, and `compact true`\nenable compaction. `compact=false`, `compact=no`, `compact=0`, and\n`compact false` disable it. The separated form accepts only `true` or `false`.\n\n## Templates and embedded formatters\n\n| Directive | Scope | Effect |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `fmt: template.delimiters \"<<\" \">>\"` | Inferred | Add one non-empty double-quoted delimiter pair using the placement rule below. |\n| `fmt: template.delimiters \"<<\" \">>\" scope=next` | Next | Add the pair to the next supported target. |\n| `fmt: template.delimiters \"<<\" \">>\" scope=from-here` | From here | Add the pair to following supported targets. |\n| `fmt: template.delimiters \"<<\" \">>\" scope=file` | File | Add the pair throughout the current document or nested region. |\n| `fmt: embedded python` | Next | Format the next supported string or YAML literal scalar with the named formatter. |\n| `fmt: python` | Next | Shorthand for `fmt: embedded python`. |\n\nA bare `fmt: template.delimiters` directive uses the next target when placed\ndirectly before one. When blank lines or range boundaries isolate it from\ncontent on both sides, it applies from there onward. The directive requires an\nexplicit scope in every other placement.\n\nDelimiter arguments must be non-empty double-quoted tokens; single quotes are\nnot accepted. Inside a token, `\\\"`, `\\\\`, `\\n`, `\\r`, and `\\t` represent a\ndouble quote, backslash, newline, carriage return, and tab.\n\nEmbedded formatter directives accept only `scope=next`. The name can select a\nbuilt-in alias or an entry from [`[embedded]`](reference-config.qmd#embedded).\n\nYAML can also mark a scalar as Markdown with the `!markdown` or `!md` tag:\n\n```yaml\nbody: !markdown \"A paragraph with [a link](https://example.com).\"\n```\n\n## Source files and fenced chunks\n\n| Host | Directive | Effect |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Python or R comment or string | `fmt: markdown` | Format the next supported comment block or string as Markdown. Surrounding source code stays unchanged. |\n| Python or R string | `fmt: <name>` or `fmt: embedded <name>` | Format the next supported string with the named embedded formatter. Surrounding source code stays unchanged. |\n| Markdown fence | An opening attribute such as `` ```yaml fmt: skip `` | Preserve that fence locally. |\n| Quarto source fence | `#| fmt: skip` anywhere in the initial consecutive `#|` option block | Preserve that chunk locally. |\n\n[Supported files and syntax](reference-files.qmd#python-and-r-source-files)\ndescribes automatic hashpipe YAML recognition. The [Markdown behavior\ntable](reference-files.qmd#markdown) describes Quarto fence-header promotion.\n===========\n---\ntitle: Formatting settings\ndescription: Formatting controls, defaults, accepted values, scopes, and interactions.\n---\n\nStart here when you know which output should change but not where Yamark exposes\nthe control. This page groups settings by behavior; the linked\n[configuration](reference-config.qmd),\n[directive](reference-directives.qmd), and [command-line](cli-help.qmd) pages\ngive the exact syntax for each surface.\n\n## Markdown settings\n\n| Behavior | [Directive](reference-directives.qmd#markdown-targets-and-settings) | [Front matter](#document-markdown-options) | [`yamark.toml`](reference-config.qmd#format) | [Command line](cli-help.qmd#yamark-format) | Default |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Prose wrapping | `wrap=` | `editor_options.markdown.wrap` | `[format].wrap` | `--wrap` | Column 72 |\n| Table widths | `table-widths=` | `editor_options.markdown.table-widths` | `[format].table_widths` | `--table-widths` | `fit` |\n| Canonical spelling | `canonical=` or `canonical` | `editor_options.markdown.canonical` | - | `--canonical` | Off |\n| Footnote definitions | `footnotes=` | `editor_options.markdown.footnotes` | - | `--preserve-footnotes` | Format |\n| Horizontal-rule marker | - | - | `[format].markdown_horizontal_rule` | - | `---` |\n\n### Wrapping values\n\n| Value | Effect |\n| --- | --- |\n| `none` | Do not wrap Markdown prose. |\n| `paragraph` | Put each paragraph on one physical line. |\n| `sentence` | Put each sentence on its own line without column wrapping. |\n| `sentence:<n>` | Put each sentence on its own line and wrap long sentences to column `<n>`. |\n| A positive integer | Wrap prose to that column without forcing sentence boundaries. |\n\n`sentence:<n>` is a Yamark-specific extension. RStudio's visual writer does not\nrecognize the combined value.\n\n### Table widths\n\n`fit` sizes supported pipe, simple, grid, and multiline table columns from\ntheir contents, with consistent padding. It can shrink excessive widths or\nexpand cramped columns. Both modes preserve column alignment and multiline\ncell breaks.\n\n`preserve` retains the source widths while still formatting cell contents.\nFor Pandoc tables, this keeps the borders and gaps that determine widths. For\npipe tables, it keeps separator lengths and row widths, even when the original\nrows are not aligned with one another.\n\nPandoc can use source widths to determine rendered column proportions and\nwrapping. Choose `preserve` when those widths are intentional:\n\n```markdown\n<!-- fmt: table-widths=preserve scope=next -->\n+----------+------------------+\n| Name     | Description      |\n+==========+==================+\n| A        | Short text       |\n+----------+------------------+\n```\n\nUse `scope=file` for a document-wide choice or `scope=from-here` for subsequent\ntables. A later `table-widths=fit scope=from-here` resumes fitting widths.\nWithout an explicit scope, this option follows the usual Markdown directive\ndefault of `scope=file`.\n\nThe setting also works in front matter, `yamark.toml`, and the command line.\nExplicit renderer settings such as Quarto's `tbl-colwidths` remain unchanged.\n`fmt: skip` preserves the entire table when exact source layout matters.\nUnsupported table structures remain unchanged in either mode.\n\n### Canonical and footnote values\n\n`canonical` accepts `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0` in front matter\nand directives. A bare `canonical` directive means `canonical=true`. Canonical\nmode rewrites supported `_emphasis_` and `__strong__` spans as `*emphasis*` and\n`**strong**`. It preserves protected or unsupported spans, including intraword\nunderscores, code spans, link destinations, raw HTML, and template content.\n\nFor `footnotes`, `wrap`, `format`, `true`, `yes`, and `1` format footnote\ndefinitions. `preserve`, `none`, `false`, `no`, and `0` preserve them.\n`--preserve-footnotes` preserves Markdown footnote definitions byte-for-byte.\n\n## YAML settings\n\n| Behavior | Control | Default | Effect |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Structural line width | `--line-width <n>` | 80 | Expands block-renderable flow collections when they exceed the width. Over-width flow collections that cannot be rendered safely in block style may be preserved. Also bounds compact and layout-repair output. |\n| Folded scalar prose width | `--prose-width <n>` | 72 | Wraps eligible folded YAML prose. |\n| Block indentation | `--indent-width <n>` | 2 | Sets indentation for emitted block mappings and sequences. |\n| Compact collections | `--compact`, `[format].compact`, or `fmt: compact` | Off | Collapses eligible block collections to flow style when they fit. |\n| Aligned flow mappings | `fmt: table` or `fmt: compact table` | Off | Aligns a following sequence of compatible flow mappings. This is _emphasis_.\n```\n\n| Key | Accepted values |\n| --- | --- |\n| `wrap` | `none`, `paragraph`, `sentence`, `sentence:<n>`, or a positive integer column. |\n| `table-widths` | `fit` or `preserve`. |\n| `canonical` | `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. |\n| `footnotes` | `wrap`, `format`, `preserve`, `none`, `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. |\n\nUnknown front-matter keys and unrecognized values are ignored; the\ncorresponding base setting remains active. JSON-to-YAML projection has a different contract: it parses a\nJSON-family input and emits formatted YAML for inspection or conversion.\n\nUse `yamark to-yaml --stdin-file-path` to project JSON-family input from stdin\nto formatted YAML on stdout:\n\n```sh\nyamark to-yaml --stdin-file-path data.json < data.json\n```\n\nThe command does not read or write the path. It uses the extension to select\none exact input grammar:\n\n| Extension | Accepted input |\n| --- | --- |\n| `.json` | Strict JSON. |\n| `.jsonc` | JSON with line comments, block comments, and trailing commas. Other JSON5 syntax is rejected. |\n| `.json5` | JSON5 strings, identifiers, numbers, comments, and trailing commas. |\n| `.jsonl` and `.ndjson` | One strict JSON value per physical line. Blank records are rejected. |\n\nObject member order and duplicate names are preserved. JSON and JSONC keep the\nsource spelling of numbers. JSON5 spellings that YAML would interpret\ndifferently are normalized, including `0X` hexadecimal prefixes, leading or\ntrailing decimal points, unary plus, `Infinity`, and `NaN`. Negative\nhexadecimal integers are emitted in decimal because YAML would otherwise treat\nthem as strings.\n\nJSONC and JSON5 comments become YAML comments. Unknown keys and invalid values are errors.\n\nThe top-level tables are `[format]`, `[template]`, `[embedded]`, and `[paths]`.\n\n## `[format]`\n\n```toml\n[format]\nwrap = \"sentence:88\"\ncompact = true\nmarkdown_horizontal_rule = \"***\"\n```\n\n| Key | Type and values | Effect when present |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `wrap` | String: `none`, `paragraph`, `sentence`, `sentence:<n>`, or a positive integer. | Sets Markdown wrapping. An explicit `--wrap` value overrides it. |\n| `table_widths` | String: `\"fit\"` or `\"preserve\"`. | Sizes Markdown table columns from their contents by default, or retains source widths. An explicit `--table-widths` overrides it; document settings and scoped directives override that base setting. |\n| `compact` | Boolean. | Enables or disables eligible YAML block-to-flow compaction. `--compact` still enables compact mode when this is `false`. |\n| `markdown_horizontal_rule` | String: `\"---\"` or `\"***\"`. | Chooses the marker Yamark emits for normalized Markdown horizontal rules. |\n\nSee [Formatting settings](reference-options.qmd) for built-in defaults and the\nother surfaces that expose these behaviors.\n\n## `[template]`\n\nTemplate delimiters mark regions Yamark must preserve because rendering can\nchange the host language. The defaults are `{{ }}`, `{% %}`, `{# #}`, and\n`<% %>`.\n\n| Key | Type | Effect |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `add_delimiters` | Array of `{ open, close }` tables. | Appends to the delimiters active at this layer, after `replace_delimiters` if both keys are present. |\n| `replace_delimiters` | Array of `{ open, close }` tables. | Replaces the delimiters active at this layer before any additions. |\n\nAdd a delimiter pair:\n\n```toml\n[template]\nadd_delimiters = [\n  { open = \"<<\", close = \">>\" }\n]\n```\n\nReplace the defaults:\n\n```toml\n[template]\nreplace_delimiters = [\n  { open = \"[[\", close = \"]]\" }\n]\n```\n\nEvery entry must contain non-empty `open` and `close` strings.\n\nIn Markdown paragraphs and supported prose containers, including lists and\nblockquotes, a complete single-line expression is one opaque word. Yamark\npreserves every byte inside it and wraps the surrounding prose normally. For\nexample, `{{ render(\"keep   this\") }}` can occupy its own line or exceed the\nrequested width, just like a long word. Function calls, quoted arguments,\nescaped quotes, and nested braces are supported. A closing delimiter inside a\nsingle- or double-quoted argument does not end the expression. For `{#` / `#}`\ncomments, the first literal `#}` ends the token; quotes, apostrophes, and braces\ninside have no special meaning. Yamark only recognizes boundaries; it does not\ninterpret or evaluate template languages.\n\nConfigured openers take precedence over Markdown inline syntax. When several\npairs match an opener, the first complete closing boundary ends the token. File\ndirectives apply to earlier content too, including nested Markdown blocks.\n\nA template-only source line does not preserve placement. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Ch8kV9apUNPMwkbdbR2sS","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01LWvfDJLmzyh5HaWv2CkVcv","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/tmp/corpus4/b/changelog.md","content":"serosurv changelog\n==================\n\nAll notable changes to **serosurv** are documented in this file. We loosely follow [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/ \"Keep a Changelog 1.1.0\") and [semantic versioning][semver], although _honestly_ the 0.3.0 release broke the API without a major version bump (sorry to everyone whose scripts depended on the old two-vector interface of `seroprev()`; see the migration notes under 0.3.0).   \nDates are in ISO 8601 format and refer to the day the release was tagged, not the day it reached our r-universe.\n\n## [Unreleased] ##\n\n### Added\n* `adjust_prevalence()` gains `method = \"bayes\"`, which fits the hierarchical model of Gelman and Carpenter[^gc2020] so that the uncertainty in test sensitivity and specificity is propagated from the validation studies instead of being treated as known constants. Needs **cmdstanr** (>= 0.7.0), which is now listed under `Suggests`.\n* New example data `sero_toy`: a simulated serosurvey of 1,200 participants in 8 districts with a known true prevalence, mainly for teaching.\n+ `plot_prevalence()` can facet by any grouping variable via `facet_by =`.\n\n### Changed\n- The default interval for *unadjusted* prevalence is now Wilson instead of Wald.  Wald intervals behave badly near 0 and 1, which is exactly where most serosurveys early in an outbreak live.\n- Minimum R version is now 4.1, because we use the native pipe `|>` internally.\n\n### Fixed\n- `rogan_gladen()` no longer silently returns values outside $[0, 1]$; estimates are truncated to the unit interval and a warning is raised (#41, thanks to K. Asante for the report).\n- Column names containing underscores (age\\_group\\_5y and friends) were mangled in `plot_prevalence()` legends. \n\n## [0.4.1] - 2024-03-18 ##\n\nBug-fix release. If you used `weights =` together with `by =` in 0.4.0, **please re-run your analyses**: stratum weights were recycled in the wrong order whenever the grouping variable was a factor whose levels were not in alphabetical order.\n\n### Fixed\n\n1) Stratum weights are now matched by name, not by position (#38).\n2) `seroprev()` printed \"NaN%\" for strata without positives; it now prints `0.0%` together with the exact (Clopper–Pearson) upper bound.\n3) The vignettes build without internet access (the district shapefile now ships in `inst/extdata`).\n\nEffect of the fix on the bundled `sero_toy` data, adjusted prevalence in %:\n\n| District | 0.4.0 (wrong) | 0.4.1 |true value|\n|:--|--:|--:|:-:|\n| North | 12.4 | 8.1 | 8.0 |\n| Lakeside | 3.9| 6.6 |6.5|\n|Old Town |  21.0 | 20.7 | 21.2 |\n| *all districts* | 11.8 | 11.8 | 11.9 |\n\n## [0.4.0] - 2024-01-29\n\n### Added\n\n* Post-stratification: `seroprev(..., poststrat = census_df)` reweights the sample to known population margins (age group &times; sex &times; district). Census margins for the three study countries are included as `census_ke`, `census_ug` and `census_tz`.\n* Support for **multiple assays** per sample:\n    * `combine_assays(rule = \"both\")` – positive only if both assays are positive\n    * `combine_assays(rule = \"either\")`\n    * `combine_assays(rule = \"sequential\")` – the second assay is only run on samples that were positive on the first, which is the usual confirmatory algorithm in the field labs\n\n  Sensitivity and specificity of the combined algorithm are derived assuming conditional independence of the assays, which is optimistic. See `vignette(\"assay-dependence\")`.\n\n### Changed\n\n* `seroprev()` returns a tibble with class `serosurv_est` instead of a plain list.\\\n  Code that used `res$estimate` keeps working, code that used `res[[1]]` does not.\n* Arguments renamed for consistency with **epiR**:\n\n  - `sens` → `se`\n  - `spec` → `sp`\n  - `n_val` → `n_validation`\n\n### Deprecated\n\n* `seroprev_old()`, the pre-0.3 interface. It will be removed in 0.5.0 – *really* this time.\n\n* * *\n\n## [0.3.0] - 2023-06-02\n\nThe version used for the analyses in our 2023 paper in __Epidemiology & Infection__. To reproduce those results exactly, install it with\n\n    remotes::install_github(\"ecoepi-lab/serosurv@v0.3.0\")\n\n### Changed\n\n- **Breaking:** `seroprev()` takes a data frame plus column names instead of two vectors.\n- The Rogan–Gladen correction is applied by default whenever `se` and `sp` are supplied:\n$$\n\\hat{\\pi}_{RG} = \\frac{\\hat{p} + \\widehat{Sp} - 1}{\\widehat{Se} + \\widehat{Sp} - 1}\n$$\n  with the delta-method variance of Reiczigel et al. (2010).\n\n#### Migrating from 0.2.x\n\n1. Replace `seroprev(x, n)` with `seroprev(df, positive = x, total = n)`.\n2. If you grouped results with `split()` + `lapply()`, use `by = ` instead.\n\nIf you also used test adjustment:\n\n3. Pass `se` and `sp` explicitly; the old global option `serosurv.assay` is ignored.\n4. Check that your validation sample sizes are in `n_validation`, otherwise the intervals will be too narrow.\n\n### Removed\n\n- The **rjags** backend. JAGS is painful to install on the Windows laptops in the field office and nobody was using it anyway.\n\n___\n\n## [0.2.0] - 2022-11-14\n\n- First version shared outside the group.\n- Functions: `seroprev()`, `rogan_gladen()`, `plot_prevalence()`.\n- Project-level settings can be stored in a `serosurv.yml` next to the `.Rproj` file, e.g.\n\n  ```yaml\n  assay:   {name: \"Wantai HEV IgG\", se: 0.98, sp: 0.995}\n  ci_method: \"wilson\"\n  strata: [district,age_group]\n  ```\n\n## 0.1.0 - 2022-05-03 #\n\nInternal release for the Kisumu field team.  \nNo changelog was kept for this one, sorry!\n\n- - -\n\n<p align=\"right\"><sub>Maintainers: Asha Mwangi &amp; Peter Lindgren &middot; release checklist in <code>RELEASING.md</code></sub></p>\n\n[^gc2020]: Gelman, A. and Carpenter, B. It started as part of Lena's PhD and is now used by about a dozen people in three departments, so please read this page before opening a pull request -- it saves time for everybody, including you.  \n\n> **TL;DR**\n> 1. Open an issue first for anything bigger than a typo.\n> 2. Work on a branch, never directly on `main`.\n> 3. Run the test dataset (`make test`) before you ask for a review.\n\nContents:\n\n* [Reporting problems](#reporting-problems)\n* [Setting up a development environment](#setting-up)\n* [Code style](#code-style)\n+ [Data policy](#data-policy) &larr; please read this one even if you skip everything else\n* [Pull requests](#pull-requests)\n\nReporting problems\n------------------\n\nBefore filing an issue please have a look at the [FAQ](docs/faq.md \"Frequently asked questions\") and at the closed issues, a surprising number of problems turn out to be caused by an outdated SILVA download. When you do open an issue, include\n\n- the exact command you ran,\n- your `config/config.yaml` (remove any paths that reveal sample or participant IDs!),\n- the **complete** log of the failing rule, which Snakemake writes to `logs/<rule>/<sample>.log`, and\n- the output of `snakemake --version` and `mamba list -n ampliseq-lite`.\n\nWe triage issues on Monday mornings at lab meeting and label them as follows:\n\n|label|meaning|who usually picks it up|\n|---|:---|---|\n| `bug` | wrong results or a crash | maintainers |\n|`good first issue`|small and well defined| anyone :) |\n| `taxonomy-db` | needs a new or updated reference database (SILVA, UNITE, GTDB) | Lena or Sam |\n| `wontfix` | out of scope, e.g. shotgun metagenomics (use nf-core/mag for that) | – |\n\n## Setting up {#setting-up}\n\nYou need [mamba](https://mamba.readthedocs.io/ \"mamba documentation\") (or conda >= 23.10, which uses the libmamba solver by default) and git. On the department cluster both are available after `module load mamba`.\n\n1) Fork and clone the repository:\n\n   ```bash\n   git clone git@github.com:<your-user>/ampliseq-lite.git\n   cd ampliseq-lite\n   ```\n\n2) Create the development environment. It contains snakemake, snakefmt, pytest and pre-commit on top of the runtime dependencies:\n\n   ```bash\n   mamba env create -f envs/dev.yaml\n   mamba activate ampliseq-dev\n   pre-commit install\n   ```\n3) Run the small test dataset (6 mock-community samples, about two minutes on a laptop):\n\n        make test\n\n   If this fails on a fresh clone, that is a bug -- please tell us!\n\n### A minimal config for development\n\nPoint the pipeline at the test data with a small config file. Keys are case-sensitive and the pipeline does _not_ warn about unknown keys yet (see #57), so a typo in `max_ee` silently gives you the default:\n\n```yaml\nsamples:   \"tests/data/samples.tsv\"\nprimers:\n    forward: GTGYCAGCMGCCGCGGTAA      # 515F (Parada)\n    reverse: \"GGACTACNVGGGTWTCTAAT\"   # 806R (Apprill)\ntrim: {min_length: 200, max_ee: [2,2], trunc_q: 2}\ntaxonomy:\n  database: silva-138.1\n  min_confidence: 0.8\nthreads: 4\n```\n\nThe expected-error filter discards a read when $\\sum_i 10^{-Q_i/10}$ exceeds `max_ee`, where $Q_i$ is the Phred quality score at position $i$.\n\n## Code style\n\n* Snakefiles are formatted with **snakefmt**, Python scripts with **ruff** and R scripts with **styler**. `pre-commit` runs all three, so normally you don't have to think about it.\n* One rule per output type. Rules that call R or Python should use the `script:` directive and not `shell: \"Rscript ...\"`, so the `snakemake` object is available inside the script.\n* Every rule needs `log:`, `conda:` and `benchmark:` directives. A rule without a log file __will__ be rejected in review; we have lost too many days to silent failures on the cluster.\n* Name rules with verbs: `trim_primers`, `learn_errors`, `assign_taxonomy`.   Not `step3b`.\n\nA typical rule:\n\n```python\nrule assign_taxonomy:\n    input:\n        seqs=\"results/asv/asv_seqs.fasta\",\n        db=config[\"taxonomy\"][\"database_path\"],\n    output:\n        \"results/taxonomy/asv_taxonomy.tsv\",\n    log:\n        \"logs/assign_taxonomy.log\",\n    benchmark:\n        \"benchmarks/assign_taxonomy.tsv\"\n    conda:\n        \"../envs/dada2.yaml\"\n    threads: 8\n    script:\n        \"../scripts/assign_taxonomy.R\"\n```\n\nIf a run hangs on the cluster, press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd> **once** and wait; Snakemake removes incomplete output files before it exits.\n\n### Commit messages and the changelog\n\nWrite a short summary line (max. ~60 characters) in the imperative mood, a blank line, then details if needed. Reference issues with `Fixes #12`. Good summary lines look like\n\n    Add UNITE 9.0 database download rule\n    Fix sample sheet parsing when sample IDs contain dots\n\nUser-visible changes also get an entry under *Unreleased* in `CHANGELOG.md`, in this form:\n\n```markdown\n### Fixed\n* `trim_primers` no longer drops reads whose primer starts with a degenerate base (#61).\n+ The taxonomy table now has one column per rank instead of a single `;`-separated string, which makes it much easier to read into phyloseq\n```\n\n## Data policy\n\n<div class=\"warning\" markdown=\"1\">\n**Never commit sequencing reads, sample metadata containing participant information, or anything from the `restricted/` share.** Some projects (the infant gut cohort in particular) include human-associated samples covered by an ethics approval that does not allow sharing outside the university network.\n</div>\n\nIf you accidentally commit something sensitive, __do not__ just delete it in a new commit -- it stays in the history. Tell Lena or Sam right away and we will rewrite the history and rotate whatever needs rotating. Nobody will be angry, it has happened before[^history].\n\nTest data in `tests/data/` are subsampled from public mock communities ([ZymoBIOMICS][zymo]) and are fine to share.\n\nPull requests\n-------------\n\nBefore requesting a review, tick these off in the PR description:\n\n- [ ] `make test` passes locally\n- [ ] new rules have `log:`, `conda:` and `benchmark:`\n- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` has an entry under *Unreleased*\n- [x] you have read this document\n\nReviews are usually done within a week. During the field season (May–August) it can take longer because half the group is out sampling lakes; ping us in the `#ampliseq` Slack channel if nothing happens.\n\n***\n\n### Authorship ###\n\nPeople who contribute substantially to the pipeline (new modules, major bug fixes, rewriting the docs) are invited as co-authors on the pipeline paper, with roles described using the [CRediT taxonomy][credit]. Smaller contributions are acknowledged in `AUTHORS.md`. If you think you should be on the list and aren't, just say so -- seriously.\n\n[^history]: Twice, actually. Removed `TrackingClient#getShipment(id, callback)` and all other callback overloads. Use the promise-returning variants.\n2. `Shipment.status` is now a string union (`\"created\" | \"in_transit\" | \"out_for_delivery\" | \"delivered\" | \"exception\" | \"returned\"`) instead of a numeric enum, so `status === 3` comparisons must be updated.\n3. The default `baseUrl` changed from `https://tracking.acme-corp.example/api/v3` to `https://tracking.acme-corp.example/api/v4`. The v3 API will be switched off on 2027-03-31.\n    * If you pin `baseUrl` explicitly, nothing changes for you.\n    * If you rely on the default, test against v4 in staging first: the `eta` field moved into `delivery.eta`.\n\nMigration example:\n\n```diff\n-import { TrackingClient, ShipmentStatus } from \"@acme/shipment-tracking-sdk\";\n-client.getShipment(id, (err, shipment) => {\n-  if (shipment.status === ShipmentStatus.Delivered) markDone(shipment);\n-});\n+import { TrackingClient } from \"@acme/shipment-tracking-sdk\";\n+const shipment = await client.shipments.get(id);\n+if (shipment.status === \"delivered\") markDone(shipment);\n```\n\n<details>\n<summary>Full list of removed exports</summary>\n\n| Export | Replacement | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `ShipmentStatus` (enum) | string union `ShipmentStatus` | type-only export now |\n| `createLegacyClient()` | `new TrackingClient()` |  |\n| `TrackingError.code` (number) | `TrackingError.reason` | e.g. `\"RATE_LIMITED\"`|\n| `withRetries(fn, n)` | `retry` option | moved into client options \\| per request |\n\n</details>\n\n### Changed\n- The default request timeout is now 10 s (was 30 s).   Long-polling calls keep their own 55 s timeout.\n- `User-Agent` now includes the calling service name when `serviceName` is set, e.g. `shipment-tracking-sdk/5.0.0 (returns-portal)`. This makes the tracking team's dashboards a lot more useful, so _please_ set it.\n-  Bundle size dropped from 41 kB to 17 kB (min+gzip) after removing `axios`.   \n\n### Deprecated\n* `client.carriers.list({ includeInactive })` -- use `client.carriers.search()` instead; `includeInactive` will be removed in 6.0.\n\n### Internal\n1) Migrated the build from Rollup to tsup; the published package layout is unchanged.\n2) CI now runs the contract tests against the tracking API's Pact broker on every merge request.\n   1) Provider verification runs nightly instead of per commit.\n   2) A failing verification blocks the release job, not the merge request.\n\n***\n\n## [4.9.2] - 2026-09-23\n\n### Fixed\n- The pagination cursor was not URL-encoded, which broke `listShipments()` for depots whose ID contains a `+` (only `AT-VIE+01` in practice).\n- Fixed a memory leak in `watch()` when the server closed the connection with HTTP 204\\\n  (thanks to the returns-portal team for the heap snapshot).\n\n## [4.9.1] - 2026-08-30\n### Security\n- Bumped `undici` to 6.19.8 to address CVE-2026-31337[^cve]. Please read it once end to end before opening your first merge request -- it will save you and your reviewers a few round trips.\n\n> [!IMPORTANT]\n> Never paste real card numbers (PANs), CVCs or track data into issues, merge requests, test fixtures or Slack, not even \"just once\" for debugging.  Use the test cards listed in [`docs/test-cards.md`](docs/test-cards.md) instead.\n> If it happens anyway, follow the [PAN exposure runbook][pan-runbook] **immediately**.\n\n**Contents**\n\n1) [Ground rules](#ground-rules)\n2) [Setting up your environment](#setting-up-your-environment)\n3) [Branches and commits](#branches-and-commits)\n4) [Merge requests and reviews](#merge-requests-and-reviews)\n5) [Releasing](#releasing)\n\n## Ground rules\n\n* Every change goes through a merge request with at least **two approvals**, one of them from a [code owner](CODEOWNERS \"Who owns what\").\n* No direct pushes to `main` or `release/*` -- the branches are protected, and Compliance reviews the audit log every quarter.\n+ Keep merge requests small. A good rule of thumb is fewer than 400 changed lines, excluding generated code and test fixtures.\n* Changes that touch cryptography, tokenisation or key handling need an additional review from `@payments-security`.\n\n## Setting up your environment\n\nYou will need:\n\n- JDK 21 (Temurin) -- `sdk install java 21.0.5-tem`\n- Docker Desktop or Colima with at least 6 GB of memory\n\n- access to the `payments-dev` Vault namespace (request it in ServiceNow, catalogue item _Developer Vault Access_)\n\nThen:\n\n1. Clone the repository and install the git hooks:\n\n   ```bash\n   git clone git@git.acme-corp.example:payments/payments-gateway.git\n   cd payments-gateway && ./scripts/install-hooks.sh\n   ```\n\n2. Start the dependencies (Postgres, Redis and the PSP simulator) with `docker compose up -d`.\n3. Run the service with the `local` profile:\n\n        ./gradlew bootRun --args='--spring.profiles.active=local'\n\n4. Open <http://localhost:8080/swagger-ui.html> and send a test authorization with the Visa test card `4111 1111 1111 1111`.\n\nIf `docker compose` hangs on the PSP simulator under macOS, stop it with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd> and restart Colima with more memory: `colima start --memory 8`.\n\n## Branches and commits\n\nWe use short-lived feature branches off `main`. Release branches are cut by the release manager every second Tuesday, and hotfix branches are cut from the release branch they fix.\n\n<!-- fmt: off -->\n    main ──●────●────●─────────●────●──▶\n            \\         \\       /\n             feat/PAY-1234   release/2026.23 ──●── hotfix/PAY-1301   \n<!-- fmt: on -->\n\nCommit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/ \"Conventional Commits 1.0.0\"), with the Jira key as the scope:\n\n```text\nfeat(PAY-1234): support network tokens for Mastercard MDES\n\nNetwork tokens are requested lazily on the first recurring charge.\nRefs: PAY-1190\n```\n\n| Type | When to use | Shows up in release notes? |\n|:-----|:------------|:--:|\n| `feat` | new behaviour visible to merchants or internal consumers | yes |\n| `fix` | bug fix | yes |\n| `perf` | performance improvement without a behaviour change | yes|\n| `refactor` / `chore` / `test` | everything else | no |\n\n## Merge requests and reviews\n\nBefore you assign reviewers, make sure that:\n\n- [ ] the pipeline is green, including the `pci-static-analysis` job\n- [x] new endpoints are documented in `openapi/gateway.yaml`\n- [ ] database migrations are backwards compatible (expand / contract, see [ADR-0031][adr-31])\n- [ ] logs do not contain cardholder data; run `./gradlew checkLogRedaction` to be sure\n\nUse this template for the description (GitLab pre-fills it from `.gitlab/merge_request_templates/default.md`):\n\n````markdown\n##  What\n\nShort summary of the change.   Link the Jira ticket: PAY-0000\n\n## Why\n*  context, links to incidents or ADRs\n\n## How to test\n1. step one\n1. step two\n\n## Risk\n- [ ] touches card data  \n- [ ] needs a feature flag\n````\n\nReviewers should respond within **one working day**. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Ch8kar6GGBWF5uAWPbsQa","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Dh6B1bP9Ljtyz1YyvTvhRE","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/tmp/corpus4/a/readme.md","content":"<p align=\"center\">\n  <img src=\"docs/assets/platformctl-logo.svg\" alt=\"platformctl logo\" width=\"160\">\n</p>\n\n# platformctl\n[![pipeline status](https://git.acme-corp.example/platform/platformctl/badges/main/pipeline.svg)](https://git.acme-corp.example/platform/platformctl/-/commits/main) [![coverage report](https://git.acme-corp.example/platform/platformctl/badges/main/coverage.svg \"Line coverage on main\")](https://git.acme-corp.example/platform/platformctl/-/graphs/main/charts) [![classification: internal](https://img.shields.io/badge/classification-internal-orange)][classification]\n\n`platformctl` is the command-line front door to the **Acme Internal Developer Platform** (IDP).  It provisions everything a new service needs on the golden path -- a Kubernetes namespace with sane defaults, a managed Postgres database, Kafka topics with ACLs, Vault policies, a Backstage catalog entry and the CI templates -- from a single `service.yaml` that lives next to your code.\n\n> [!NOTE]\n> `platformctl` replaces the old `svc-bootstrap` Jenkins job, which will be switched off on **31 January 2027**.  See the [migration guide](docs/migrating-from-svc-bootstrap.md \"Migrating from svc-bootstrap\") if you still have services that were created with it.\n\n## Contents ##\n\n* [Installation](#installation)\n* [Quick start](#quick-start)\n* [The service.yaml file](#the-serviceyaml-file)\n    * [Tiers](#tiers)\n* [Commands](#commands)\n* [Configuration](#configuration)\n* [FAQ](#faq)\n\n## Installation\n\nOn a managed laptop the CLI is already installed by the _Developer Workstation_ profile and kept up to date by Jamf.  Otherwise:\n\n1. Make sure you are on the corporate VPN or in an office network.\n2. Install it from the internal Homebrew tap:\n   ```console\n   $ brew tap acme/internal https://git.acme-corp.example/platform/homebrew-internal.git\n   $ brew install platformctl\n   ```\n3. Log in once.  The token is cached in your OS keychain and refreshed automatically:\n\n       platformctl login --sso\n\nLinux users can download a static binary from the [releases page][releases] instead. Windows is supported through WSL2 only.\n\n## Quick start\n\n```sh\nplatformctl init --template java-service --name parcel-label-printer --team team-logistics-edge\nplatformctl plan\nplatformctl apply\n```\n\n`init` writes a `service.yaml` similar to this one:\n\n```yaml\napiVersion: platform.acme-corp.example/v1\nkind: Service\nmetadata:\n    name: parcel-label-printer\n    owner:   team-logistics-edge\n    tier: \"2\"\n    tags: [logistics,printing ,  edge]\nspec:\n  runtime: {language: java, version: 21}\n  database: {engine: postgres, size: small, extensions: [pgcrypto, \"pg_partman\"], backups: {retention_days: 14, pitr: false}}\n  kafka:\n    topics:\n    - name: label.print.requested.v1\n      partitions: 6\n      retention: \"7d\"\n    - {name: label.print.completed.v1, partitions: 6, retention: 7d}\n  expose: [ http ]\n```\n\nThe service.yaml file\n---------------------\n\nEvery field is documented in the [schema reference](docs/schema.md).  The ones people ask about most:\n\n+ `metadata.owner` must be a team that exists in Backstage; personal owners are __not__ accepted.\n+ `metadata.tier` controls the defaults for replicas, PodDisruptionBudgets and alerting (see [Tiers](#tiers)).\n+ `spec.database.size` maps to a CloudNativePG instance class: `small` = 2 vCPU / 4 GiB, `medium` = 4 vCPU / 16 GiB, `large` = 8 vCPU / 32 GiB.\n\n### Tiers\n\n| Tier | Example | Min. replicas | Paging | Change approval |\n|:---:|---|--:|:--|---|\n| 1 | payments-gateway, checkout | 3 | 24/7, 5 min | CAB |\n| 2 | parcel tracking, pricing | 2 | business hours | team lead |\n| 3 | internal tools, batch jobs | 1 | none | none|\n\n## Commands\n\n| Command | What it does |\n|---|---|\n| `platformctl init` | Scaffolds `service.yaml`, `.gitlab-ci.yml` and a `catalog-info.yaml` from a template |\n| `platformctl plan` | Shows what would change, much like `terraform plan` \\| `less` |\n| `platformctl apply` | Applies the plan. Tier 1 services need an approved change ticket: `--change CHG0041234` |\n| `platformctl destroy` | Tears everything down. Databases are snapshotted first and the snapshot is kept for 35 days |\n\nPress <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd> during `apply` to abort; resources that were already created are rolled back unless you pass `--keep-partial`.\n\n## Configuration\n\nSettings are read from, in order of precedence:   \ncommand-line flags, environment variables, `~/.config/platformctl/config.yaml` and finally the defaults compiled into the binary.\n\nVariable | Default | Description\n--- | --- | ---\n`PLATFORMCTL_API` | `https://idp.acme-corp.example/api` | IDP API endpoint\n`PLATFORMCTL_CONTEXT` | `prod` | One of `dev`, `staging`, `prod`\n`PLATFORMCTL_NO_COLOR` | unset | Disable ANSI colours (also honours `NO_COLOR`)\n\n<details>\n<summary><b>Example config file</b></summary>\n\n```yaml\ncontext:   staging\napi: https://idp.staging.acme-corp.example/api\ndefaults: {team: team-logistics-edge, template: java-service}\n```\n\n</details>\n\n## FAQ\n\n**Why not just use Terraform directly?**  \nYou can, and the platform team does exactly that under the hood.  But most product teams do not want to own 1,500 lines of HCL per service, keep provider versions in sync or remember that a tier 1 database needs point-in-time recovery enabled. `platformctl` encodes those decisions so that you do not have to.\n\n**Can I adopt an existing service?**\\\nYes: `platformctl adopt --name <service>` imports existing resources into the IDP state.  Expect a few manual fixes; the import report lists them.\n\n**Something is broken. Who do I talk to?**  \nPost in `#platform-help` with the output of `platformctl doctor`.  For outages use the `@platform-oncall` handle -- it pages whoever is on call.\n\n* * *\n\nArchitecture\n------------\n\n![High-level architecture: platformctl talks to the IDP API, which drives Crossplane, Vault and Backstage](docs/assets/architecture.png \"platformctl architecture\")\n\nThe CLI is a thin client.  All provisioning logic lives in the IDP API (`platform/idp-api`), which reconciles the desired state through Crossplane compositions[^xp]. The regression affected all card schemes, but it was most visible for Mastercard transactions routed via the U.K. acquirer (see Fig. 2). Approximately 18,400 authorizations (about 1.7% of attempts in the window) timed out, and an estimated EUR 1.1m of checkout value was lost or delayed. No card data was exposed, and no duplicate captures were found during reconciliation the next morning.\n\nDr. Okafor's team first suspected the new 3-D Secure challenge flow, i.e. the change that shipped in release v4.18.0 that morning; however, the timing did not match. The root cause turned out to be connection-pool exhaustion in the HSM proxy, a component whose pooling code had not been touched since 2009. It was triggered by a routine certificate rotation on the HSM cluster, which made every TLS handshake about four times slower (see Sec. 3.2 for details).\n\n## Timeline\n\nAll times are CET. The timeline was reconstructed from PagerDuty, the `#inc-2026-1103` Slack channel and the gateway's audit log; where those sources disagree, the audit log wins.\n\n| Time | Event |\n|---|---|\n| 13:40 | p99 latency crosses the 800 ms SLO threshold. |\n| 13:52 | First page to the payments on-call (Mr. Lindqvist). |\n| 14:20 | Incident declared Sev-2; comms lead assigned. |\n| 15:31 | HSM proxy pool size raised from 64 to 256 via config flag. |\n| 16:05 | p99 back below 450 ms; monitoring continues. |\n\n## Impact\n\n```{r latency-plot, fig.cap=\"p99 authorization latency by acquirer on 3 November 2026. The shaded band is the incident window. Note the log scale.\", fig.width=9, fig.height=4}\nplot_latency(auth, by = \"acquirer\", log_y = TRUE, highlight = c(params$window_start, params$window_end))\n```\n\nThe effect differed considerably by acquirer and scheme (Fig. 1 vs. Fig. 2). Visa transactions through the EU acquirer saw a moderate increase, e.g. from 380 ms to roughly 900 ms at p99, whereas Mastercard through the U.K. acquirer exceeded the 2 s client timeout for long stretches. In total, `r format(sum(auth$timed_out), big.mark = \",\")` authorizations timed out. The merchants most affected were large ticketing customers running flash sales, which have little tolerance for retries...\n\n```{r}\n#| label: tbl-impact\n#| tbl-cap: \"Impact by card scheme. Counts are approx. and exclude client-side retries.\"\nimpact_table(auth) |> knitr::kable(digits = 1)\n```\n\nSome customers retried aggressively. This is _expected_ behaviour, and our client libraries back off exponentially (cf. the retry policy in Sec. 4 of the integration guide). However, at least one large merchant (No. 7 in the internal ranking) uses a custom integration that retries immediately, which roughly tripled its request volume during the incident. Did the retries make things worse? Probably, but only marginally: they added about 6% to the load on the HSM proxy.\n\n## Root cause\n\nThe HSM proxy keeps a fixed-size pool of TLS connections to the hardware security modules. When the HSM cluster's certificate was rotated at 13:35, all pooled connections were closed and re-established at once. With the new 4096-bit key, each handshake took approx. 180 ms instead of 45 ms. Because the pool size (64) had been tuned years ago for a much lower request rate, requests queued behind the handshakes and the latency cascaded through the gateway.\n\n> \"We had a runbook for HSM certificate rotation, but it assumed the proxy would reconnect lazily. It does not. It reconnects everything at once.\" -- Mr. Lindqvist, in the incident channel at 15:12\n\nSeveral factors contributed:\n\n1. The rotation was scheduled during business hours (14:00 is our lowest-traffic hour on weekdays, but only for EU merchants).\n2. The proxy's pool metrics were not on any dashboard. They were only exposed via JMX, i.e. invisible to Grafana.\n3. The canary for the rotation checked HSM health, not end-to-end authorization latency. It passed.\n\nThis is a well-known failure pattern for connection pools under synchronized reconnects [@nygard2018release, pp. 112-118; @kleppmann2017designing]. Similar incidents have been described at other payment providers, e.g. in a 2019 talk by Dr. Chen et al. on \"thundering herds\" in HSM fleets [-@chen2019herds].\n\n## Action items\n\n* **Pool sizing.** Make the pool size adaptive, with a floor of 128. Owner: payments-core. Due 2026-12-15.\n* **Staggered reconnects.** Reconnect at most 10% of the pool per second after a rotation. This should have been the default all along.\n* **Dashboards.** Export the pool metrics to Prometheus and add them to the _Gateway Golden Signals_ dashboard.\n* __Rotation runbook.__ Move HSM certificate rotations to the 03:00-05:00 window, and add an end-to-end latency check to the canary.\n\nThe estimated cost of the action items is approx. 3 engineer-weeks. Given that a similar rotation is scheduled for Q1 2027, we recommend completing at least the first two items before then. Questions should go to Dr. Okafor or to the #payments-core channel.\n\n## Appendix: method\n\nLatency percentiles were computed per minute from the gateway's request logs (n = `r nrow(auth)` requests in the window, plus a 14-day baseline). We used the t-digest implementation in the **tdigest** package [@dunning2019tdigest] with compression 200, which keeps the relative error at p99 below 0.5% for our volumes. The baseline is the median of the same minute-of-day across the previous 14 days, excl. public holidays (e.g. 1 Nov.).[^holidays]\n\n[^holidays]: All Saints' Day (1 Nov.) is a public holiday in several German states. Traffic on that day is not representative. We therefore excluded it from the baseline.\n\n```{r appendix-session, echo=TRUE, results=\"markup\", comment=\"\"}\nsessionInfo()\n```\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5291,"cache_read_input_tokens":157330,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":5291,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":"toolu_013nYV1A9z7RKwdKLnhFSPe6","agent_id":"a904cbf21a591ed04","session_id":"0e7cfb1b-67a4-4c6e-bc49-6d823e4685c0","uuid":"10298a74-c3eb-4f31-a59b-062052c7fde5","timestamp":"2026-11-17T15:41:17.308Z","request_id":"req_011Ch8kdQYhVoxwhmnbWybfA","subagent_type":"general-purpose","task_description":"Write realistic test corpus A"}
