Please skim this before opening a big PR, it'll save us both time.\"\n---\n\n# Contributing to teacup #\n\nFirst off: thanks for even opening this file! :tea: teacup is a one-person hobby project (hi, I'm Rosa) that somehow turned into a thing a few hundred people use for their blogs, and every bug report, typo fix, theme and PR genuinely helps. That said, I work on this in the evenings and at weekends, so please be patient if I don't reply for a week or two; it's not personal, I promise.  \nSmall PRs get merged faster than big ones. If you want to do something big, open an issue first so we can talk about it *before* you sink a weekend into it.\n\nGetting set up\n==============\n\nYou need:\n\n+ Go 1.22 or newer\n+ `make` (on Windows use WSL, or just run the commands from the `Makefile` by hand)\n+ optionally [`watchexec`](https://github.com/watchexec/watchexec \"watchexec on GitHub\") for `make watch`\n\nThen:\n\n1) fork the repo and clone your fork\n2) `make build` — this produces `./bin/teacup`\n3) `make test` — runs the unit tests *and* the golden-file tests in `testdata/sites/`\n4) `./bin/teacup serve ./examples/blog` and open http://localhost:1313\n\nIf step 3 fails on a fresh clone, that's a bug. Please tell me!\n\n## Project layout\n\n```text\ncmd/teacup/          CLI entry point (cobra)\ninternal/build/      the actual site builder\ninternal/markdown/   goldmark setup + our extensions (callouts, footnotes, heading ids)\ninternal/theme/      template loading; the default theme is in internal/theme/default/\ntestdata/sites/      golden-file tests, each folder is a tiny site + its expected output\n```\n\n### Golden-file tests\n\nEach folder under `testdata/sites/` has a `site/` and an `expected/` directory. The test builds `site/` and diffs the output against `expected/`. When you change the output on purpose, regenerate the expected files with:\n\n    UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./internal/build/...\n\nand then **look at the diff** before committing it. I have merged broken golden files before because I didn't look. Everything happens locally, nothing gets uploaded anywhere, and it never deletes a file unless you explicitly pass `--delete-dupes` **and** confirm. I wrote this because my \"Retro\" folder had grown to 40 GB of `Super Mario World (USA) (1).zip`, `smw_final_FINAL.sfc` and friends, and every existing tool either wanted a GUI, Windows, or both.\n\n[![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-mkdocs-blue)](https://kitokafor.github.io/romsort/) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/pypi/dm/romsort)](https://pypistats.org/packages/romsort)\n\n> **Note**  \n> romsort only works with ROMs you dumped yourself or are otherwise legally allowed to have. It never downloads ROMs and never will, so please don't open issues asking for that.\n\n## Features ##\n\n* Matches files by CRC32/SHA-1 against DAT files, so the filename doesn't matter at all\n* Renames to the canonical No-Intro / Redump name\n+ Sorts into per-system folders (`snes/`, `megadrive/`, `psx/` ...)\n+ **1G1R** mode: keeps one game per title, preferring your region order (`--regions EUR,USA,JPN`)\n- Handles `.zip` and `.7z` archives, and multi-track `.cue`/`.bin` sets\n- Dry-run by default :sunglasses: — you have to pass `--apply` to actually move anything\n\nInstallation\n------------\n\n```bash\npipx install romsort\n# or, if you like living on the edge\npipx install git+https://github.com/kitokafor/romsort\n```\n\nNeeds Python 3.10 or newer. 7z support needs `py7zr`, which is an optional extra: `pipx install \"romsort[7z]\"`.\n\n## Usage\n\n    romsort scan ~/Roms/unsorted --dat-dir ~/Roms/dats\n    romsort sort ~/Roms/unsorted ~/Roms/sorted --apply\n\nThe first command only reads; it prints a report of what it found and what it *would* do.  The second one actually moves files.   \nHere's what the output looks like on a small folder:\n\n~~~console\n$ romsort scan ./unsorted --dat-dir ./dats\nloaded 14 DAT files (38,212 entries)\nmatched   212 / 230 files\nunknown    18 files  (see romsort-unknown.txt)\ndupes       9 files  (same SHA-1, different names)\n~~~\n\n### Commands\n\n| command | what it does | safe? |\n|---|---|:---:|\n| `scan` | hash everything, match against the DATs, print a report | :white_check_mark: |\n| `sort` | move/rename matched files into `DEST/<system>/` | only with `--apply` |\n| `dedupe` | find duplicates, optionally delete them | :warning: with `--delete-dupes` |\n|`dat update`|download the latest DATs from your configured sources|:white_check_mark:|\n\n### Config file\n\nromsort looks for `~/.config/romsort/config.yaml`. Every option can also be passed on the command line, the config file just saves typing. Files whose name ends in \\_old or starts with \\# are skipped, which is a leftover from my own folder structure and will probably become an option at some point.\n\n```yaml\n# ~/.config/romsort/config.yaml\ndat_dir: ~/Roms/dats\nregions: [EUR, USA,JPN]\none_game_one_rom:   true\nsystems:\n    snes: {dat: \"Nintendo - Super Nintendo Entertainment System\", folder: snes}\n    md:   {dat: \"Sega - Mega Drive - Genesis\", folder: megadrive}\n    psx:\n      dat: Sony - PlayStation\n      folder: psx\n      prefer: [cue, chd]\nignore:\n- \"*.txt\"\n- '*.nfo'\n- \"[BIOS]*\"\n```\n\n## FAQ\n\n**Q: Why are some of my files \"unknown\"?**  \nUsually one of these:\n\n1) it's a bad dump or a hack (hacks aren't in No-Intro, by design)\n2) it has a header the DAT doesn't expect. romsort strips iNES and SMC headers automatically, but not every weird copier header out there\n3) you don't have the DAT for that system yet\n\n**Q: Can it convert `.bin`/`.cue` to `.chd`?**\\\nNo, use `chdman` for that. romsort will happily sort the `.chd` files afterwards though.\n\n**Q: Does it work on Windows?**  \nProbably? I don't have a Windows machine to test on. For example, to widen the fuzzy window for a PSP that is known to settle late and to silence the on-call mention:\n\n```yaml\nmatching:\n    fuzzy_window_days:   3\nnotify: {mention_on_exceptions: []}\n```\n\nUnknown top-level keys are rejected with exit code `1`, so typos do not go unnoticed.\n\"\"\"\n\n# fmt: markdown\n# ## Matching rules\n#\n# Matching runs in passes, from the most to the least specific.   A line matched in an earlier pass is never reconsidered, which keeps the result deterministic even when a PSP sends duplicate references.\n#\n# 1. **Exact** -- the PSP reference equals the ledger posting's `external_ref`.\n# 2. **Fuzzy** -- same merchant, currency and amount, value date within `fuzzy_window_days` days.\n#    Ties go to the earliest ledger posting.\n# 3. **Batch** -- for PSPs that settle in aggregate (looking at you, SEPA direct debit), compare per-merchant daily totals instead of individual lines.\n#\n# Anything left over becomes a row in `recon.exceptions` with reason `UNMATCHED`.\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass SettlementLine:\n    psp: str\n    psp_reference: str\n    merchant_id: str\n    currency: str\n    amount_minor: int\n    value_date: dt.date\n    fee_minor: int = 0\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass ReconResult:\n    matched: list[tuple[SettlementLine, str]] = field(default_factory=list)\n    unmatched: list[SettlementLine] = field(default_factory=list)\n\n    @property\n    def exit_code(self) -> int:\n        return 3 if self.unmatched else 0\n\n    def totals_by_currency(self) -> dict[str, tuple[int, int]]:\n        totals: dict[str, list[int]] = defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0])\n        for line, _ in self.matched:\n            totals[line.currency][0] += line.amount_minor\n            totals[line.currency][1] += line.fee_minor\n        return {cur: (net, fees) for cur, (net, fees) in sorted(totals.items())}\n\n\ndef load_config(path: Path | None) -> dict:\n    config = yaml.safe_load(DEFAULT_CONFIG_YAML)\n    if path is None:\n        return config\n    override = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")) or {}\n    unknown = set(override) - {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Ch8kjXRreRvCe96tao9N7","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_0178ycPsCFpQhSY4VLLdMNZU","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/tmp/corpus4/b/quarto_report.qmd","content":"---\ntitle:  \"Drought shocks and school enrolment in rural Ethiopia\"\nsubtitle: 'Evidence from the Ethiopia Socioeconomic Survey, 2011–2016'\nauthor:\n    - name: \"Hanna Tesfaye\"\n      orcid: 0000-0002-1825-0097\n      email: hanna.tesfaye@aau.example.edu\n      affiliations: [{name: \"Department of Economics, Addis Ababa University\"}]\n      corresponding: true\n    - name: Jonas Weber\n      affiliations:\n        - name: Kiel Institute for the World Economy\n          city: Kiel\ndate: last-modified\ndate-format: \"D MMMM YYYY\"\nabstract: \"We combine three waves of the Ethiopia Socioeconomic Survey (ESS) with gridded rainfall data to estimate how drought shocks affect primary school enrolment. A one standard deviation shortfall in growing-season rainfall reduces enrolment of children aged 7–14 by about 3 percentage points, with larger effects for girls and for households that do not receive transfers from the Productive Safety Net Programme.\"\nkeywords: [drought, education,  \"human capital\", Ethiopia,panel data]\nbibliography: references.bib\ncsl: \"chicago-author-date.csl\"\nlink-citations: true\nformat:\n  html:\n    toc: true\n    toc-depth: 3\n    code-fold: true\n    code-tools: true\n    embed-resources: true\n    theme: [cosmo, custom.scss]\n  pdf:\n    documentclass: scrartcl\n    geometry: [\"margin=2.5cm\", \"a4paper\"]\n    keep-tex: true\n    include-in-header:\n      text: |\n        \\usepackage{booktabs}\n        \\usepackage{siunitx}\nexecute:\n  echo: false\n  warning: false\n  message: false\ncrossref:\n  fig-prefix: Figure\n  tbl-prefix:   Table\n  eq-prefix: Equation\nknitr:\n  opts_chunk:\n    dev: \"ragg_png\"\n    fig.align: 'center'\n---\n\n```{r}\n#| label: setup\n#| include: false\nlibrary(tidyverse)\nlibrary(fixest)\nlibrary(modelsummary)\nlibrary(sf)\n\npanel  <- read_rds(here::here(\"data\", \"ess_panel_children.rds\"))\nkebele <- read_rds(here::here(\"data\", \"spi3_kebele.rds\"))\nn_hh   <- n_distinct(panel$household_id)\n```\n\n## Introduction {#sec-intro}\n\nEthiopia's agricultural economy remains highly exposed to rainfall variability: roughly 85% of households depend on rain-fed crop production, and the 2015/16 El Niño drought was the worst in fifty years [@fews2016; @dercon2004, p. 312]. A large literature documents the consequences of such shocks for consumption and child nutrition [@dercon2005; @hoddinott2006], but the evidence on schooling is mixed. Children may be withdrawn from school to work on the farm or to save on fees, or, conversely, enrolment may *increase* in a bad year because the opportunity cost of children's time falls [@jacoby1997; @shah2017].\n\nThis paper uses three waves of the Ethiopia Socioeconomic Survey (ESS) to estimate the effect of growing-season rainfall shocks on primary school enrolment. Our sample contains `r nrow(panel)` child-year observations from `{r} n_hh` households. We find that drought reduces enrolment, and that the effect is concentrated among girls and among households outside the Productive Safety Net Programme (PSNP)[^psnp].\n\n[^psnp]: The PSNP is a public works and cash/food transfer programme introduced in 2005. It currently covers around 8 million people in chronically food-insecure woredas; see @gilligan2009 for an early evaluation of its effects on food security and asset accumulation.\n\n::: {.callout-note collapse=\"true\"}\n## Replication material\nAll code is in the `analysis/` folder of the replication package. The ESS microdata cannot be redistributed, but can be downloaded free of charge from the [World Bank Microdata Library](https://microdata.worldbank.org/index.php/catalog/lsms \"LSMS-ISA catalogue\") after registration. Run `targets::tar_make()` to rebuild everything.\n:::\n\n## Data {#sec-data}\n\n### Survey data\n\nThe ESS is part of the Living Standards Measurement Study -- Integrated Surveys on Agriculture (LSMS-ISA). We use the 2011/12, 2013/14 and 2015/16 waves, which follow the same rural households. The outcome is a dummy for current enrolment of children aged 7--14 at the time of the interview.\n\n### Rainfall\n\nRainfall comes from CHIRPS v2.0 [@funk2015], a 0.05° gridded product blending satellite estimates with station data. For each kebele we compute the Standardised Precipitation Index for the *kiremt* (main rainy) season, June to September:\n\n$$\n\\text{SPI}_{kt} = \\Phi^{-1}\\!\\left( G_k(R_{kt}) \\right)\n$$ {#eq-spi}\n\nwhere $G_k$ is the gamma distribution fitted to 1981–2010 kiremt rainfall in kebele $k$ and $\\Phi$ is the standard normal CDF. Following convention, a season with $\\text{SPI}_{kt} < -1$ counts as a drought.\n\n![Kiremt SPI by kebele in 2015. Darker colours are drier; dots mark ESS enumeration areas.](figures/spi_map_2015.png){#fig-map fig-alt=\"Choropleth map of Ethiopia showing the standardised precipitation index for the 2015 kiremt season, with the driest areas in the north-east (Afar and eastern Amhara) and enumeration areas shown as black dots.\" width=\"80%\"}\n\n@fig-map shows that the 2015 drought was concentrated in the north-east, in Afar, eastern Amhara and parts of Oromia, i.e. in areas where the PSNP was already active.\n\n```{r}\n#| label: tbl-balance\n#| tbl-cap: \"Descriptive statistics by drought exposure, pooled sample\"\n#| tbl-colwidths: [40,20,20,20]\npanel |>\n  mutate(drought = if_else(spi3 < -1, \"Drought\", \"No drought\")) |>\n  select(drought, enrolled, age, female, hh_size, head_female, log_cons, psnp) |>\n  datasummary_balance(~drought, data = _, dinm = TRUE, fmt = 3)\n```\n\n@tbl-balance compares children in kebeles with and without a drought in the survey year. Drought-affected households are poorer and more likely to be PSNP beneficiaries, which is why all specifications include child fixed effects.\n\n## Empirical strategy\n\nWe estimate a linear probability model with child and region-by-year fixed effects:\n\n$$\nE_{ikt} = \\beta\\,\\text{SPI}_{kt} + \\gamma' X_{ikt} + \\alpha_i + \\delta_{r(k)t} + \\varepsilon_{ikt}\n$$ {#eq-main}\n\nStandard errors are clustered by kebele, the level at which the shock varies [@abadie2023]. The key terms are defined as follows.\n\nDrought\n:   A kiremt season with $\\text{SPI}_{kt} < -1$, i.e. roughly the driest 16% of seasons in the reference period.\n\nPSNP household\n: A household that reported receiving PSNP transfers (cash or food) in the 12 months before the interview.  Public works participants and direct-support beneficiaries are pooled.\n\nEnrolled\n:  The child currently attends primary or lower-secondary school according to the household roster. We do not observe actual attendance, which probably responds more strongly to shocks than enrolment does.\n\n## Results\n\n::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n### Pooled\n\n```{r}\n#| label: tbl-main\n#| tbl-cap: \"Effect of rainfall shocks on enrolment (linear probability model)\"\nmodels <- list(\n  \"(1)\" = feols(enrolled ~ spi3 | child_id + region^year, data = panel, cluster = ~kebele_id),\n  \"(2)\" = feols(enrolled ~ spi3 + hh_size + head_female + log_cons | child_id + region^year, data = panel, cluster = ~kebele_id),\n  \"(3)\" = feols(enrolled ~ drought | child_id + region^year, data = panel, cluster = ~kebele_id)\n)\nmodelsummary(models, stars = TRUE, gof_map = c(\"nobs\", \"r.squared.within\"))\n```\n\n### By sex and PSNP status\n\n```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5, echo=FALSE, fig.cap=\"Effect of a one-SD rainfall shortfall on enrolment by subgroup, with 95% confidence intervals.\"}\nhet <- feols(enrolled ~ spi3 | child_id + region^year, data = panel, cluster = ~kebele_id, split = ~interaction(female, psnp))\ncoefplot(het)\n```\n\n### Robustness\n\n1. Dropping the 2015/16 wave, in which attrition was highest.\n2. Using the continuous rainfall deviation in mm instead of the SPI.\n3. Adding woreda-specific linear trends.\n4. Restricting the sample to children who were enrolled in the first wave.\n\nAll four leave the main coefficient between [-0.034 and -0.026]{.mark}; see Appendix A.\n\n:::\n\n```{r}\n#| label: fig-event\n#| fig-cap: \"Enrolment around the 2015 drought\"\n#| fig-subcap:\n#|   - \"Drought-affected kebeles\"\n#|   - 'Other kebeles'\n#| layout-ncol: 2\n#| fig-alt: \"Two line charts of enrolment rates by survey wave. Enrolment falls in 2015/16 in drought-affected kebeles but not elsewhere.\"\nfor (g in c(TRUE, FALSE)) {\n  p <- panel |> filter(drought_2015 == g) |> count(wave, wt = enrolled / n()) |> ggplot(aes(wave, n)) + geom_line() + geom_point()\n  print(p)\n}\n```\n\nThe estimates in @tbl-main imply that a one-SD shortfall reduces enrolment by about 3 percentage points, roughly a tenth of the gap between the poorest and richest consumption quintile. @fig-event suggests that this is not driven by pre-existing trends.\n\n::: {.callout-warning}\n## Attrition\nAbout 9% of the households interviewed in 2011/12 could not be re-interviewed in 2015/16, and attrition was higher in drought-affected zones. If the households that left were those hit hardest, our estimates are biased towards zero. Bounds following @lee2009 are reported in Appendix B[^bounds].\n:::\n\n:::: {.columns}\n\n::: {.column width=\"60%\"}\nGirls' enrolment drops by 4.1 percentage points, boys' by 1.9. The difference is significant at the 5% level, consistent with households protecting the education of the child with the higher expected labour market return [cf. @jensen2010].\n:::\n\n::: {.column width=\"40%\"}\n> \"When the rains failed, my daughter stayed home to fetch water.\"\n>\n> --- Mother of three, South Wollo (qualitative module, 2016)\n:::\n\n::::\n\n## Conclusion\n\nRainfall shocks have measurable consequences for human capital accumulation in rural Ethiopia, and the PSNP appears to shield households from the worst of them. If you are a reviewer: hello! Everything you need to reproduce the figures and tables of the manuscript is in this repository, and the whole pipeline runs in about 25 minutes on a recent laptop (most of that time is spent fitting the hierarchical models in Stan).   \n\nThe repository is organised as a [research compendium](https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.2017.1375986 \"Marwick, Boettiger & Mullen (2018)\"), i.e. an R-package-like structure in which the analysis code, the data and the manuscript live together and are versioned together.\n\n## Contents ##\n\n```\n.\n├── data-raw/        # survey sheets as entered by the dive teams (do not edit!)\n├── data/            # cleaned data, created by data-raw/clean_surveys.R\n├── R/               # functions used by the targets pipeline\n├── analysis/\n│   ├── _targets.R\n│   ├── config.yml\n│   └── manuscript.qmd\n└── renv.lock\n```\n\n## Getting started\n\nYou need R (>= 4.2), a working C++ toolchain for **cmdstanr**, and roughly 4 GB of free disk space.\n\n1) Clone the repository and open `caribbean-reef-fish.Rproj` in RStudio.\n2) Restore the package library:\n    ```r\n    install.packages(\"renv\")\n    renv::restore()\n    cmdstanr::install_cmdstan(version = \"2.34.1\")\n    ```\n3) Run the pipeline:\n\n    ```r\n    targets::tar_make()\n    ```\n\n   Results end up in `analysis/outputs/`, and the manuscript is rendered to `analysis/manuscript.html`.\n\nSteps 2 and 3 also work from a terminal:\n\n    Rscript -e 'renv::restore(prompt = FALSE)'\n    Rscript -e 'targets::tar_make()'\n\nIf `renv::restore()` fails while compiling **sf** on macOS, install GDAL with Homebrew first (`brew install gdal`) and try again.\\\nOn Windows, use the binary packages from CRAN instead (see [this renv issue][renv-win]).\n\n## Data\n\nThe main file is `data/fish_counts.csv`, one row per species per transect per survey. Columns:\n\n| column | type | description |\n|--------|:----:|-------------|\n| `survey_id` | chr | `<island>-<site>-<yyyymmdd>`, e.g. `BON-012-20150611` |\n| `transect` | int | 1–4; each transect is 30 m × 2 m (belt transect, 60 m²)|\n| `species` | chr | valid name according to WoRMS, see `data/species_list.csv` |\n| `length_cm` |dbl| total length, visually estimated in 5 cm classes and recorded as the class midpoint |\n| `count` | int | number of individuals |\n| `depth_m` | dbl | mean transect depth   |\n\nSpecies marked with an asterisk (\\*) in `species_list.csv` were only identified to genus before 2014.\n\nBiomass is calculated from length with the usual allometric relationship $W = aL^b$, using species-specific $a$ and $b$ from FishBase[^fishbase] (fallback: genus averages). Densities are expressed per 100 m², so for transect $j$ with area $A_j$\n\n$$\nD_{sj} = \\frac{100}{A_j} \\sum_{k} n_{sjk}\n$$\n\nwhere $n_{sjk}$ is the count of species $s$ in length class $k$.\n\n### Settings\n\nA few choices (which islands, which years, the Stan sampler settings) live in `analysis/config.yml` rather than in the code. The defaults reproduce the paper:\n\n```yaml\ndefault:\n  islands: [BON,CUR,ARU]\n  years:   {from: 2009, to: 2023}\n  exclude_sites: [\"CUR-031\"]   # destroyed by the 2019 coastal works\n  stan:\n      chains: 4\n      iter_warmup: 1000\n      iter_sampling: 1000\n      adapt_delta: 0.99\nquick:\n  stan: {chains: 2, iter_warmup: 300, iter_sampling: 300}\n```\n\nUse the `quick` profile for testing (`Sys.setenv(R_CONFIG_ACTIVE = \"quick\")`); its results are _not_ suitable for inference!\n\n## Survey protocol (short version) ##\n\nEvery site was surveyed once a year between May and July by two divers:\n\n* four 30 m belt transects at 10 m depth, laid parallel to the reef crest\n    * diver 1 counts all non-cryptic fish within 1 m either side of the tape\n    * diver 2 follows ~3 m behind and records lionfish (*Pterois volitans* / *P. miles*) and cryptic species\n* benthic cover from photo-quadrats every 2 m (analysed separately, see [reef-benthos][benthos])\n+ water temperature from the dive computer\n\nSurveys before 2012 used 25 m transects; these are rescaled in `R/standardise_effort.R`. The 2020 season was cancelled \\(COVID-19\\) and the 2017 data for Aruba are incomplete because of boat problems.\n\nHow to cite\n-----------\n\n> Ramírez, L., Okafor, C. & Thompson, J. (2024). Zieliński\"\ndate: \"`r format(Sys.Date(), '%d %B %Y')`\"\noutput:\n  bookdown::html_document2:\n    toc: yes\n    toc_float: true\n    number_sections: true\n    fig_caption: yes\n  bookdown::word_document2: default\nbibliography: [ticks.bib, packages.bib]\ncsl: parasites-and-vectors.csl\nlink-citations: yes\neditor_options:\n  markdown:\n    wrap: sentence\n    canonical: true\n  chunk_output_type: console\n---\n\n```{r setup, include=FALSE}\nknitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 300)\nlibrary(tidyverse)\nlibrary(glmmTMB)\nlibrary(DHARMa)\nlibrary(here)\ndrags <- read_csv(here(\"data\", \"drag_sampling_2022_2023.csv\"))\nsites <- read_csv(here(\"data\", \"sites.csv\"))\nn_sites <- nrow(sites)\n```\n\n# Introduction\n\nTick-borne encephalitis (TBE) and Lyme borreliosis are the two most important vector-borne diseases in central Europe, and both are transmitted mainly by nymphs of the castor bean tick, *Ixodes ricinus* (L.). In the Czech Republic the number of notified TBE cases has fluctuated between approx. 400 and 900 per year since the mid-1990s, with a record 847 cases reported in 2020. Over the same period ticks have been found at increasingly high altitudes, e.g. up to 1,300 m a.s.l. in the Krkonoše mountains [@Danielova2006; @Materna2008]. Is this upward shift a consequence of climate warming, of changes in host populations, or simply of more sampling effort at high altitudes? The answer matters for public health, because mountain areas are popular with hikers and vaccination coverage in the Czech population is still only about 30%.\n\nSeveral studies have described altitudinal patterns in tick abundance [@Jouda2004; @Gilbert2010; see also @Medlock2013, pp. 12--15], but most of them sampled only a few sites, and many used a single visit per site and year. Gilbert et al. (2010) concluded that \"the upper altitudinal limit of *I. ricinus* is set by the length of the season in which questing is possible.\" Jouda et al. (2004) found the opposite pattern in one of their three years (cf. Fig. 2 in @Jouda2004), which they attributed to an unusually dry summer. We therefore ask three questions: (i) how does the density of questing nymphs change with altitude; (ii) is this relationship modified by microclimate, i.e. by the saturation deficit at ground level; and (iii) does it differ between years? The two study years were very different. 2022 was among the driest years on record, whereas the spring of 2023 was the wettest since 1961. Prof. Hönig (pers. comm.) called this contrast \"almost a natural experiment\". We agree, with some caveats (see Discussion).\n\n# Methods\n\n## Study area\n\nThe study was carried out in the Šumava National Park (SW Czech Republic) and its foothills under permit No. 2021/451 of the park administration. We selected `r n_sites` sites along four transects running from the Vltava valley (ca. 450 m a.s.l.) to the main ridge near Mt. Plechý (approx. 1,250 m a.s.l.); site characteristics are listed in Table \\@ref(tab:sites). All sites were in mixed or coniferous forest with a herb layer dominated by *Vaccinium myrtillus*, *Oxalis acetosella* or grasses (*Calamagrostis* spp., *Deschampsia flexuosa*). Sites were at least 500 m apart. Mean annual temperature ranges from 7.5 °C at the lowest to 3.9 °C at the highest site.\n\n## Tick sampling\n\nQuesting ticks were collected by dragging a 1 m² white flannel cloth over the vegetation along 10 transects of 10 m per site (i.e. 100 m² per visit), checking the cloth after every 10 m. Each site was visited once a month from April to October in 2022 and 2023, always between 9:00 and 13:00 and never within 24 h of rain. All ticks were stored in 70% ethanol and identified to species and stage under a stereomicroscope using the key of Estrada-Peña et al. (2017). Larvae were counted but not analysed further. At each visit we measured air temperature and relative humidity 5 cm above the ground with a handheld meter and calculated the saturation deficit (SD) following Randolph & Storey (1999):\n\n$$\nSD = \\left(1 - \\frac{RH}{100}\\right) \\cdot 4.9463 \\cdot e^{0.0621\\,T}\n$$\n\nwhere $RH$ is relative humidity in % and $T$ is temperature in °C.\n\n<!-- fmt: off -->\n**Field protocol card (laminated version)**\n1. Drag 10 × 10 m. Check cloth after each 10 m.\n2. Ticks → 70% EtOH, one tube per drag.\n3. Record T and RH at 5 cm. Do NOT sample within 24 h of rain!\n<!-- fmt: on -->\n\n## Statistical analysis\n\nNymph counts per visit were modelled with negative binomial GLMMs [`glmmTMB`, @Brooks2017] with altitude (scaled), SD, year and the altitude × year interaction as fixed effects, and site and month as random intercepts. Was a zero-inflated model necessary? We compared models with and without a zero-inflation component by AIC; the ZI model was not supported (ΔAIC = 1.8). Residuals were checked with DHARMa [@Hartig2022], which showed no overdispersion (dispersion test, p = 0.41). All analyses were done in R version `r getRversion()`.\n\n```{r model}\nm_nb <- glmmTMB(nymphs ~ scale(altitude) * factor(year) + sd_hpa + (1 | site) + (1 | month), family = nbinom2, data = drags)\nm_zi <- update(m_nb, ziformula = ~1)\nsim <- simulateResiduals(m_nb, n = 1000)\n```\n\n# Results\n\nIn total we collected 6,482 ticks, of which 5,911 (91.2%) were *I. ricinus* nymphs. Adults made up approx. 4% of the catch, and only 9 *Dermacentor reticulatus* were found, all at the two lowest sites. Nymph density declined steeply with altitude in both years (Fig. \\@ref(fig:fig-altitude)), from a mean of 42.3 nymphs per 100 m² below 600 m to 3.1 per 100 m² above 1,000 m. The decline was steeper in 2022 than in 2023 (altitude × year interaction: z = 2.87, p = 0.004). Did nymphs simply quest less in the dry year? Partly: saturation deficit had a strong negative effect on counts (Table \\@ref(tab:model-table)), but the altitude effect remained after accounting for it.\n\n```{r fig-altitude, fig.cap=\"Mean density of questing *I. ricinus* nymphs per 100 m² against site altitude in 2022 (open circles) and 2023 (filled circles). Lines show model predictions with 95% confidence bands.\", fig.width=7, fig.height=4}\ndrags |>\n  group_by(site, year) |>\n  summarise(altitude = first(altitude), density = mean(nymphs), .groups = \"drop\") |>\n  ggplot(aes(altitude, density, shape = factor(year))) +\n  geom_point(size = 2) +\n  scale_shape_manual(values = c(1, 16), name = NULL) +\n  labs(x = \"Altitude (m a.s.l.)\", y = expression(\"Nymphs per 100 m\"^2))\n```\n\nThree further results are worth mentioning:\n\n- No nymphs were found above 1,150 m a.s.l. in 2022. In 2023 nymphs were found at all but one site, incl. the highest one (1,248 m).\n- The seasonal peak shifted from May at low sites to July at high sites. This is consistent with Materna et al. (2008) for the Krkonoše mts.\n- Larvae were extremely aggregated, e.g. 312 of 1,040 larvae came from a single drag in Aug. 2023.\n\n| Altitude band | Sites | Nymphs/100 m² (2022) | Nymphs/100 m² (2023) |\n|:---|---:|---:|---:|\n| < 600 m | 6 | 45.1 | 39.6 |\n| 600–900 m |8| 18.7 | 24.0 |\n| 900–1,100 m | 6 | 2.2 | 7.9 |\n| > 1,100 m | 4 | 0.0 | 1.4 |\n\n```{r model-table}\n#| tab.cap: \"Fixed effects of the negative binomial GLMM. Estimates are on the log scale.\"\nbroom.mixed::tidy(m_nb, effects = \"fixed\") |>\n  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = \"Fixed effects of the negative binomial GLMM. Estimates are on the log scale.\")\n```\n\n# Discussion\n\nOur results support the view that the altitudinal limit of *I. ricinus* is not fixed but moves from year to year. In the wet year 2023, nymphs were found ca. 100 m higher than in 2022. Is the upward shift reported in the literature then an artefact? Not necessarily: a series of mild, wet years would produce exactly the pattern described by Daniel et al. (2003) and Materna et al. (2008). However, we cannot exclude that host density also changed; roe deer (*Capreolus capreolus*) numbers in the park increased by approx. 20% between 2015 and 2022 according to the park administration (unpubl. data)[^deer]. The so-called \"edge effect\", i.e. higher tick densities near forest edges, was not examined here!\n\n> Very windy, the cloth kept flipping over. Probably underestimates density at site 17.\n> --- field notebook, 14 June 2022\n\nTwo limitations should be kept in mind. First, drag sampling measures questing activity, not absolute abundance, and activity depends on weather (2022 vs. 2023 being an extreme example). Second, with only two years we cannot separate a trend from inter-annual variation. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01DycXc4fAMxdi6THFkGPD6u","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Yamark\n2\t\n3\tYamark is a fast formatter for YAML and Markdown. It formats whole files and embedded content, keeping source readable and changes easy to review. Regions without a supported rewrite stay unchanged.\n4\t\n5\tFor supported embedded code, Yamark can also call Ruff, Air, Prettier, or another configured formatter.\n6\t\n7\tSee the [documentation](https://t-kalinowski.github.io/yamark/) for examples, configuration, editor integrations, and the full syntax reference.\n8\t\n9\t## Install\n10\t\n11\tWith [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) installed, run Yamark directly from [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/yamark/) without a separate install:\n12\t\n13\t```sh\n14\tuvx yamark format config.yaml docs/\n15\t```\n16\t\n17\tThis formats the selected files in place. To install a persistent `yamark` command:\n18\t\n19\t```sh\n20\tuv tool install yamark\n21\t```\n22\t\n23\t## Usage\n24\t\n25\tThe examples below use an installed `yamark` command. To keep running from PyPI without installing it, replace `yamark` with `uvx yamark`.\n26\t\n27\tFormat one or more files or directories in place:\n28\t\n29\t```sh\n30\tyamark format config.yaml docs/\n31\t```\n32\t\n33\tFormat the current directory:\n34\t\n35\t```sh\n36\tyamark format\n37\t```\n38\t\n39\tCheck whether files are already formatted without writing changes:\n40\t\n41\t```sh\n42\tyamark format --check docs/\n43\t```\n44\t\n45\tShow a unified diff without writing changes:\n46\t\n47\t```sh\n48\tyamark format --diff docs/\n49\t```\n50\t\n51\tFormat stdin for editor and CI integrations:\n52\t\n53\t```sh\n54\tyamark format --stdin-file-path config.yaml < config.yaml\n55\t```\n56\t\n57\tConvert JSON-family input from stdin to formatted YAML on stdout:\n58\t\n59\t```sh\n60\tyamark to-yaml --stdin-file-path data.json5 < data.json5\n61\t```\n62\t\n63\tThe path is not read or written. Its suffix selects the exact JSON dialect. This is a conversion, not source formatting.\n64\t\n65\tDirectory traversal skips hidden paths and respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and global Git ignore files by default. Pass a hidden path explicitly to format it.\n66\t\n67\tWhile formatting is enabled, standalone `{{< ... >}}` and `{{% ... %}}` shortcode tokens are preserved, including multiline tokens and quoted arguments. Directive-looking text inside a recognized token is data. Yamark does not match shortcode names or interpret their bodies: Markdown between tokens formats normally. An unterminated token or quote preserves the rest of the enclosing Markdown document or fragment. This does not guarantee rendering equivalence for arbitrary Hugo or Jinja templates.\n68\t\n69\tTo disable body formatting, surround the region with `<!-- fmt: off -->` and `<!-- fmt: on -->`. While formatting is disabled, directives follow the existing linewise policy: a recognized `fmt: on` line resumes formatting even if the surrounding text resembles a shortcode argument, code fence, HTML, or math block.\n70\t\n71\tExplicitly skipped Markdown retains its bytes, including trailing spaces and line endings: `<!-- fmt: skip -->` preserves the next selected node, `<!-- fmt: off -->` preserves the disabled region, and `<!-- fmt: skip file -->` preserves the enclosing Markdown document or fragment. In a YAML file, that target\n24\tis usually a scalar node. In a Python or R file, it is usually a string literal\n25\tor a contiguous source-comment block. The directive does not format the\n26\tsurrounding Python or R source code.\n27\t\n28\t## YAML files\n29\t\n30\tMark a scalar as Markdown and choose sentence wrapping for that scalar:\n31\t\n32\t```yaml\n33\t# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence\n34\tdescription: \"Explain the project in a few clear sentences.\"\n35\tother_value: \"This is ordinary YAML, not Markdown.\"\n36\t```\n37\t\n38\tThe directive attaches to `description`, the next scalar. YAML, Python, and R\n168\tuse the same hash-comment form:\n169\t\n170\t```text\n171\t# fmt: skip file\n172\t```\n173\t\n174\tMarkdown uses an HTML comment:\n175\t\n176\t```markdown\n177\t<!-- fmt: skip file -->\n178\t```\n179\t\n180\tA whole-file skip is useful for generated files or files whose layout is\n181\tintentionally outside Yamark's scope.\n182\t\n183\tMarkdown skip controls retain trailing spaces and line endings in the selected\n184\tcontent, including supported nested Markdown.\n185\t\n186\t## Preserve intentional table widths\n187\t\n188\tYamark normally fits table columns to their contents. A later\n202\t`table-widths=fit scope=from-here` resumes fitting widths. Both modes retain\n203\tcolumn alignment. Fitting widths can change the rendered proportions of\n204\tPandoc tables; preserving widths can retain excessive or cramped padding.\n205\t\n206\tFor Markdown inside YAML, Python, or R, the same option can accompany the\n207\ttarget marker: `# fmt: markdown table-widths=preserve`.\n208\t\n209\t## Set file-specific Markdown options\n210\t\n211\tUse `scope=file` when the file should have a different Markdown policy from the\n212\trepository default:\n213\t\n214\t```markdown\n215\t<!-- fmt: wrap=sentence:72 scope=file -->\n216\t```\n217\t\n218\tThis puts one sentence per line and wraps long sentences at column 72. Keep local exceptions in directives so they stay beside the\n262\tcontent they explain.\n263\t\n264\tFor example, a repository can choose sentence-per-line Markdown and compact\n265\tYAML collections by default:\n266\t\n267\t```toml\n268\t[format]\n269\twrap = \"sentence:88\"\n270\tcompact = true\n271\t```\n272\t\n273\tYamark discovers `yamark.toml` from each formatted file's directory upward.\n274\tUse the [Configuration reference](reference-config.qmd) for the full\n275\t`[format]`, `[template]`, `[embedded]`, and `[paths]` schema.\n276\t\n277\t## For one-off runs\n278\t\n279\tCommand-line options are useful for trying a policy, checking files in CI, or\n280\toverriding a repository default for one invocation:\n281\t\n282\t```sh\n283\tyamark format --wrap sentence:72 docs/\n284\tyamark format --compact config.yaml\n285\tyamark format --check docs/\n286\t```\n287\t\n288\tUse the [Directive syntax reference](reference-directives.qmd) for every\n289\taccepted form, scope, and value.\n290\t\n291\tUse the [Command-line reference](cli-help.qmd) for the accepted arguments and\n292\t[Usage](usage.qmd) for installation and common commands.\n293\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":"toolu_01Nhtp7phpCBs6fPGDZU4ker","agent_id":"aaa892d4096df6e64","session_id":"0e7cfb1b-67a4-4c6e-bc49-6d823e4685c0","uuid":"8fc53c8f-821d-4531-94e1-83b668f71ff7","timestamp":"2026-11-17T16:36:33.800Z","tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01BrS2AZmoKG5qG4iDuosheF","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}],"subagent_type":"general-purpose","task_description":"Write realistic test corpus D"}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_011f9LJ7U2zKXDk1pe59tQy3","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t---\n2\t# fmt: skip file\n3\ttitle: Directive syntax\n4\tdescription: Exact fmt comment forms, targets, scopes, values, and effects.\n5\t---\n6\t\n7\t<!-- fmt: skip file -->\n8\t\n9\tDirectives are comments whose trimmed content starts with `fmt:`. This page is\n10\tan exact syntax lookup. For a guided path through YAML, Python, and R examples,\n11\tsee [Directives](directives.qmd).\n12\t\n13\t## Comment forms\n14\t\n15\t| Host | Form | Placement |\n16\t| --- | --- | --- |\n17\t| Markdown | `<!-- fmt: ... -->` | An own-line HTML comment. |\n18\t| YAML | `# fmt: ...` | An own-line hash comment. `fmt: table` and `fmt: compact table` may also be same-line comments on an empty-valued collection parent; a populated parent is an error. |\n19\t| Python and R | `# fmt: ...` | An own-line hash comment before a supported comment or string target. |\n20\t\n21\t## Scopes\n22\t\n23\t| Scope | Meaning |\n24\t| --- | --- |\n25\t| `scope=next` | Apply to the next supported target. This is the default for target-selecting, compact, table, and embedded-formatter directives. |\n26\t| `scope=from-here` | Apply from the directive until another directive changes the same state. |\n27\t| `scope=file` | Apply throughout the current parsed document or nested region, including supported nodes before the directive. At the top level, that region is the physical file. |\n28\t\n29\tNot every directive accepts every scope. The tables below list the supported\n30\tforms. An unsupported or misspelled explicit scope is an error. Template\n31\tdelimiter directives use the contextual rule described below instead of one\n32\tfixed default.\n33\t\n34\tScopes stop at the current parsed document or nested-region boundary. A\n35\tdirective inside a recursive fence affects that fence, not its Markdown host or\n36\tsibling fences. A `scope=file` directive inside one hashpipe YAML block does not\n37\tspan later blocks. `fmt: skip file` in Markdown front matter is the exception:\n38\tit preserves the outer Markdown document.\n39\t\n40\t## Preserve content\n41\t\n42\t| Directive | Scope | Effect |\n43\t| --- | --- | --- |\n44\t| `fmt: skip` | Next | Preserve the next supported target. `fmt: skip scope=next` is equivalent. |\n45\t| `fmt: skip file` | File | Preserve the current parsed document or nested region. `fmt: skip scope=file` is equivalent. |\n46\t| `fmt: off` | From here | Preserve content until `fmt: on`, or through the end of Markdown and source regions. `fmt: off scope=from-here` is equivalent. |\n47\t| `fmt: on` | - | Resume formatting after `fmt: off`. It does not accept an explicit scope. |\n48\t\n49\tThe same control uses the host's comment form:\n50\t\n51\t```yaml\n52\t# fmt: skip\n53\tmanual: [[ 1,2,3], [4,5,6]]\n54\t```\n55\t\n56\t```markdown\n57\t<!-- fmt: off -->\n58\t*   keep\n59\t    this\n60\t    list\n61\t<!-- fmt: on -->\n62\t```\n63\t\n64\tPreserve-control lifecycle checks are host-specific. YAML rejects a targetless\n65\t`skip`, a stray `on`, a nested `off`, and an `off` without a later `on`.\n66\tMarkdown and source regions allow `skip` at the end and let `off` preserve\n67\tthrough the end of the region.\n68\t\n69\t## Markdown targets and settings\n70\t\n71\t| Form | Default scope | Effect |\n72\t| --- | --- | --- |\n73\t| `fmt: markdown` | Next | Mark the next supported target as Markdown: a Markdown block, including a supported fence; a YAML scalar; or a source string or comment block. |\n74\t| `fmt: markdown wrap=sentence canonical=true` | Next | Mark the next supported target as Markdown and set its options. |\n75\t| `fmt: wrap=sentence` | `scope=next` in YAML; `scope=file` in Markdown or source regions | Change wrapping for an already recognized Markdown region without marking unrelated content. |\n76\t| `fmt: table-widths=preserve` | `scope=next` in YAML; `scope=file` in Markdown or source regions | Preserve widths in supported Markdown tables while formatting contents. Use `scope=next` immediately before one table. |\n77\t| `fmt: canonical` | `scope=next` in YAML; `scope=file` in Markdown or source regions | Enable canonical Markdown spelling. `canonical=true` is equivalent. |\n78\t| `fmt: footnotes=preserve` | `scope=next` in YAML; `scope=file` in Markdown or source regions | Preserve footnote definitions in the affected Markdown. |\n79\t\n80\tOption-only YAML directives tune the next scalar only if it is already marked\n81\tas Markdown:\n82\t\n83\t```yaml\n84\t# fmt: canonical=true\n85\tfirst: !markdown \"This is __strong__.\"\n86\tsecond: \"This is __not__ Markdown.\"\n87\t```\n88\t\n89\tFor `scope=from-here` or `scope=file`, `fmt: markdown` must include at least one\n90\tactual Markdown option. A broad-scope directive changes Markdown settings; it\n91\tdoes not turn every plain scalar into Markdown.\n92\t\n93\tAccepted option values:\n94\t\n95\t| Option | Values |\n96\t| --- | --- |\n97\t| `wrap` | `none`, `paragraph`, `sentence`, `sentence:<n>`, or a positive integer. |\n98\t| `table-widths` | `fit` (the default) or `preserve`. Both preserve alignment. |\n99\t| `canonical` | `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. A bare `canonical` means `true`. |\n100\t| `footnotes` | `wrap`, `format`, `preserve`, `none`, `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. |\n101\t\n102\tFor `footnotes`, `wrap`, `format`, `true`, `yes`, and `1` request formatting;\n103\t`preserve`, `none`, `false`, `no`, and `0` request preservation.\n104\t\n105\t## YAML collections\n106\t\n107\t| Directive | Scope | Effect |\n108\t| --- | --- | --- |\n109\t| `fmt: compact` | Next | Enable block-to-flow compaction for the next eligible collection. |\n110\t| `fmt: compact false` | Next | Disable compaction for the next eligible collection. `fmt: compact=false` is equivalent. |\n111\t| `fmt: compact scope=from-here` | From here | Enable compaction until another compact directive changes the state. |\n112\t| `fmt: compact=false scope=file` | File | Disable compaction throughout the current YAML document or one source-file hashpipe YAML block. |\n113\t| `fmt: table` | Next | Align the next compatible sequence of flow mappings. |\n114\t| `fmt: compact table` | Next | Collapse eligible block mapping rows before aligning them. `fmt: table compact` and `fmt: table compact=true` are equivalent. |\n115\t\n116\t`fmt: table` accepts only its default next-target scope. Compact directives\n117\taccept `next`, `from-here`, and `file`.\n118\t\n119\t`compact`, `compact=true`, `compact=yes`, `compact=1`, and `compact true`\n120\tenable compaction. `compact=false`, `compact=no`, `compact=0`, and\n121\t`compact false` disable it. The separated form accepts only `true` or `false`.\n122\t\n123\t## Templates and embedded formatters\n124\t\n125\t| Directive | Scope | Effect |\n126\t| --- | --- | --- |\n127\t| `fmt: template.delimiters \"<<\" \">>\"` | Inferred | Add one non-empty double-quoted delimiter pair using the placement rule below. |\n128\t| `fmt: template.delimiters \"<<\" \">>\" scope=next` | Next | Add the pair to the next supported target. |\n129\t| `fmt: template.delimiters \"<<\" \">>\" scope=from-here` | From here | Add the pair to following supported targets. |\n130\t| `fmt: template.delimiters \"<<\" \">>\" scope=file` | File | Add the pair throughout the current document or nested region. |\n131\t| `fmt: embedded python` | Next | Format the next supported string or YAML literal scalar with the named formatter. |\n132\t| `fmt: python` | Next | Shorthand for `fmt: embedded python`. |\n133\t\n134\tA bare `fmt: template.delimiters` directive uses the next target when placed\n135\tdirectly before one. When blank lines or range boundaries isolate it from\n136\tcontent on both sides, it applies from there onward. The directive requires an\n137\texplicit scope in every other placement.\n138\t\n139\tDelimiter arguments must be non-empty double-quoted tokens; single quotes are\n140\tnot accepted. Inside a token, `\\\"`, `\\\\`, `\\n`, `\\r`, and `\\t` represent a\n141\tdouble quote, backslash, newline, carriage return, and tab.\n142\t\n143\tEmbedded formatter directives accept only `scope=next`. The name can select a\n144\tbuilt-in alias or an entry from [`[embedded]`](reference-config.qmd#embedded).\n145\t\n146\tYAML can also mark a scalar as Markdown with the `!markdown` or `!md` tag:\n147\t\n148\t```yaml\n149\tbody: !markdown \"A paragraph with [a link](https://example.com).\"\n150\t```\n151\t\n152\t## Source files and fenced chunks\n153\t\n154\t| Host | Directive | Effect |\n155\t| --- | --- | --- |\n156\t| Python or R comment or string | `fmt: markdown` | Format the next supported comment block or string as Markdown. Both modes preserve column alignment and multiline\n40\tcell breaks.\n41\t\n42\t`preserve` retains the source widths while still formatting cell contents.\n43\tFor Pandoc tables, this keeps the borders and gaps that determine widths. For\n44\tpipe tables, it keeps separator lengths and row widths, even when the original\n45\trows are not aligned with one another.\n46\t\n47\tPandoc can use source widths to determine rendered column proportions and\n48\twrapping. Choose `preserve` when those widths are intentional:\n49\t\n50\t```markdown\n51\t<!-- fmt: table-widths=preserve scope=next -->\n52\t+----------+------------------+\n53\t| Name     | Description      |\n54\t+==========+==================+\n55\t| A        | Short text       |\n56\t+----------+------------------+\n57\t```\n58\t\n59\tUse `scope=file` for a document-wide choice or `scope=from-here` for subsequent\n60\ttables. A later `table-widths=fit scope=from-here` resumes fitting widths.\n61\tWithout an explicit scope, this option follows the usual Markdown directive\n62\tdefault of `scope=file`.\n63\t\n64\tThe setting also works in front matter, `yamark.toml`, and the command line.\n65\tExplicit renderer settings such as Quarto's `tbl-colwidths` remain unchanged.\n66\t`fmt: skip` preserves the entire table when exact source layout matters.\n67\tUnsupported table structures remain unchanged in either mode.\n68\t\n69\t### Canonical and footnote values\n70\t\n71\t`canonical` accepts `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0` in front matter\n72\tand directives. A bare `canonical` directive means `canonical=true`. Canonical\n73\tmode rewrites supported `_emphasis_` and `__strong__` spans as `*emphasis*` and\n74\t`**strong**`. It preserves protected or unsupported spans, including intraword\n75\tunderscores, code spans, link destinations, raw HTML, and template content.\n76\t\n77\tFor `footnotes`, `wrap`, `format`, `true`, `yes`, and `1` format footnote\n78\tdefinitions. `preserve`, `none`, `false`, `no`, and `0` preserve them.\n79\t`--preserve-footnotes` preserves Markdown footnote definitions byte-for-byte.\n80\t\n81\t## YAML settings\n82\t\n83\t| Behavior | Control | Default | Effect |\n84\t| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n85\t| Structural line width | `--line-width <n>` | 80 | Expands block-renderable flow collections when they exceed the width. Over-width flow collections that cannot be rendered safely in block style may be preserved. Also bounds compact and layout-repair output. |\n86\t| Folded scalar prose width | `--prose-width <n>` | 72 | Wraps eligible folded YAML prose. |\n87\t| Block indentation | `--indent-width <n>` | 2 | Sets indentation for emitted block mappings and sequences. |\n88\t| Compact collections | `--compact`, `[format].compact`, or `fmt: compact` | Off | Collapses eligible block collections to flow style when they fit. |\n89\t| Aligned flow mappings | `fmt: table` or `fmt: compact table` | Off | Aligns a following sequence of compatible flow mappings. The compact form first collapses eligible block rows. |\n90\t\n91\tAll width and indentation values must be positive integers.\n92\t\n93\tCanonical mode also permits limited rewrapping of short existing folded YAML\n94\tprose scalars when their value stays unchanged.\n95\t\n96\t## Execution controls\n97\t\n98\t| Control | Effect |\n99\t| --- | --- |\n100\t| `--diagnostics` | For YAML input, emits trace counters; it also emits notes for skipped or failing optional embedded formatters. |\n101\t| `--skip-embedded-formatters` | Disables external formatters while keeping Yamark's Markdown, YAML, front matter, and recursive Markdown formatting active. |\n102\t| `--config <path>` | Uses one explicit `yamark.toml` for all selected files instead of discovering one per file. |\n103\t\n104\t### Embedded formatter controls\n105\t\n106\t| Need | Control |\n107\t| --- | --- |\n108\t| Select a target | Use a recognized Markdown fence language or a [`fmt: <name>` directive](reference-directives.qmd#templates-and-embedded-formatters). |\n109\t| Register or replace a formatter | Add an [`[embedded.<name>]` table](reference-config.qmd#embedded) to `yamark.toml`. |\n110\t| Disable external formatters for one run | Pass `--skip-embedded-formatters`. |\n111\t| Explain an optional formatter skip | Pass `--diagnostics`. |\n112\t\n113\tWrite, check, diff, and stdin behavior is documented under\n114\t[Command line](cli-help.qmd#modes-output-and-status).\n115\t\n116\t## Document Markdown options\n117\t\n118\tMarkdown front matter can set document-local options under\n119\t`editor_options.markdown`:\n120\t\n121\t```markdown\n122\t---\n123\teditor_options:\n124\t  markdown:\n125\t    wrap: sentence:72\n126\t    canonical: true\n127\t    footnotes: preserve\n128\t    table-widths: preserve\n129\t---\n130\tThis is __strong__. This is _emphasis_.\n131\t```\n132\t\n133\t| Key | Accepted values |\n134\t| --- | --- |\n135\t| `wrap` | `none`, `paragraph`, `sentence`, `sentence:<n>`, or a positive integer column. |\n136\t| `table-widths` | `fit` or `preserve`. |\n137\t| `canonical` | `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. |\n138\t| `footnotes` | `wrap`, `format`, `preserve`, `none`, `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. |\n139\t\n140\tUnknown front-matter keys and unrecognized values are ignored; the\n141\tcorresponding base setting remains active. Invalid `yamark.toml` keys or\n142\tdirective values are errors instead.\n143\t\n144\tThese options apply after the front matter to the Markdown body, recursive\n145\t`markdown` or `md` fences, and Markdown-valued YAML scalars in nested YAML\n146\tregions.\n147\t\n148\tYamark also reads `editor.markdown` for compatibility, but only when\n149\t`editor_options.markdown` is absent. Git\n150\tfilter subcommands use their own wrapping options and do not read document\n151\toptions.\n152\t\n153\t## Interaction rules\n154\t\n155\tMarkdown settings are applied in this order:\n156\t\n157\t1. Yamark\n362\tinserts a leading `---` document-start marker before every record, including\n363\tthe first, producing a valid YAML multi-document stream. The example below uses\n364\trecords from agent runs.\n365\t\n366\t:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n367\t**Before**\n368\t\n369\t```yaml\n370\t{\"id\":1,\"profile\":{\"name\":\"planner\",\"active\":true}}\n371\t{\"id\":2,\"profile\":{\"name\":\"researcher\",\"active\":true},\"usage\":{\"input_tokens\":640,\"output_tokens\":128}}\n372\t{\"id\":3,\"profile\":{\"name\":\"reviewer\",\"active\":true,\"model\":\"gpt-5\",\"region\":\"us\",\"tools\":[\"search\",\"python\"]},\"events\":[{\"type\":\"tool_call\",\"tools\":[\"search\",\"open\",\"python\",\"write\"]},{\"type\":\"usage\",\"tokens\":{\"input\":900,\"output\":240}},{\"type\":\"completion\",\"status\":\"ok\"}]}\n373\t```\n374\t\n375\t**After**\n376\t\n377\t```yaml\n378\t---\n379\t{id: 1, profile: {name: planner, active: true}}\n380\t---\n381\tid: 2\n382\tprofile: {name: researcher, active: true}\n383\tusage: {input_tokens: 640, output_tokens: 128}\n384\t---\n385\tid: 3\n386\tprofile:\n387\t  name: reviewer\n388\t  active: true\n389\t  model: gpt-5\n390\t  region: us\n391\t  tools: [search, python]\n392\tevents:\n393\t  - {type: tool_call, tools: [search, open, python, write]}\n394\t  - {type: usage, tokens: {input: 900, output: 240}}\n395\t  - {type: completion, status: ok}\n396\t```\n397\t::::\n398\t\n399\tYamark keeps each document as compact as the width allows. Smaller mappings and sequences remain in flow\n402\tstyle whenever they still fit within `--line-width`. This conversion is for\n403\tobject records, not arbitrary JSON values.\n404\t\n405\t### Aligned flow-mapping tables\n406\t\n407\tA sequence of similar flow mappings can be easier to scan as a table. Mark it\n408\twith `# fmt: table` and Yamark aligns columns by key:\n409\t\n410\t:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n411\t**Before**\n412\t\n413\t```yaml\n414\t# fmt: table\n415\t- {name: alpha,type: string,default: [one,two],description: \"Short\"}\n416\t- {name: beta,type: int,default: 0,description: \"Number\"}\n417\t```\n418\t\n419\t**After**\n420\t\n421\t```yaml\n422\t# fmt: table\n423\t- {name: alpha, type: string, default: [one, two], description: Short}\n424\t- {name: beta,  type: int,    default: 0,          description: Number}\n425\t```\n426\t::::\n427\t\n428\t### Compact collections\n429\t\n430\tShort, simple block collections can read better as a single flow line.\n431\tEnable `compact = true` in `yamark.toml` (or pass `--compact`) and\n432\tYamark collapses eligible block mappings and sequences that fit the\n433\tstructural width:\n434\t\n435\t:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n436\t**Before**\n437\t\n438\t```yaml\n439\ttags:\n440\t  - yaml\n441\t  - markdown\n442\t  - docs\n443\tpackage:\n444\t  name: yamark\n445\t  language: rust\n446\t```\n447\t\n448\t**After**\n449\t\n450\t```yaml\n451\ttags: [yaml, markdown, docs]\n452\tpackage: {name: yamark, language: rust}\n453\t```\n454\t::::\n455\t\n456\tCollections with comments, aliases, tags, anchors, multiline scalars, or\n457\tblock scalars stay in block style.\n458\t\n459\t### Collapse to flow by typing a bracket\n460\t\n461\tDrop an unmatched `[` or `{` where a block sequence or mapping value starts and\n462\tYamark reads it as a layout hint: collapse this collection onto one line. The\n463\tfile doesn't parse as you typed it, but the intent is obvious - Yamark removes\n464\tthe opener and emits flow style.\n465\t\n466\t:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n467\t**Before**\n468\t\n469\t```yaml\n470\ttags: [\n471\t  - yaml\n472\t  - markdown\n473\t  - docs\n474\t```\n475\t\n476\t**After**\n477\t\n478\t```yaml\n479\ttags: [yaml, markdown, docs]\n480\t```\n481\t::::\n482\t\n483\tThe opener may also be detached onto the next line after an empty mapping value\n484\theader:\n485\t\n486\t:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n487\t**Before**\n488\t\n489\t```yaml\n490\ttags:\n491\t[\n492\t  - yaml\n493\t  - markdown\n494\t  - docs\n495\t```\n496\t\n497\t**After**\n498\t\n499\t```yaml\n500\ttags: [yaml, markdown, docs]\n501\t```\n502\t::::\n503\t\n504\tAdjacent forms such as `tags:[` and `tags:{` are not repaired as layout hints.\n505\t\n506\tA newline inside an existing flow collection requests the reverse change: expand\n507\tthe collection to block style.\n508\t\n509\t:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n510\t**Before**\n511\t\n512\t```yaml\n513\t- {a: b,\n514\t   c: d}\n515\t```\n516\t\n517\t**After**\n518\t\n519\t```yaml\n520\t- a: b\n521\t  c: d\n522\t```\n523\t::::\n524\t\n525\tSee [Supported files and syntax -> Layout repair](reference-files.qmd#layout-repair)\n526\tfor the acceptance rules.\n527\t\n528\t## Fenced and nested content\n529\t\n530\t### Recursive Markdown code fences\n531\t\n532\tYAML fences are formatted as YAML. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01MEoWMYty45tvprwgCCfa7K","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Yamark\n2\t\n3\tYamark is a fast formatter for YAML and Markdown. It formats whole files and embedded content, keeping source readable and changes easy to review. Regions without a supported rewrite stay unchanged.\n4\t\n5\tFor supported embedded code, Yamark can also call Ruff, Air, Prettier, or another configured formatter.\n6\t\n7\tSee the [documentation](https://t-kalinowski.github.io/yamark/) for examples, configuration, editor integrations, and the full syntax reference.\n8\t\n9\t## Install\n10\t\n11\tWith [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) installed, run Yamark directly from [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/yamark/) without a separate install:\n12\t\n13\t```sh\n14\tuvx yamark format config.yaml docs/\n15\t```\n16\t\n17\tThis formats the selected files in place. To install a persistent `yamark` command:\n18\t\n19\t```sh\n20\tuv tool install yamark\n21\t```\n22\t\n23\t## Usage\n24\t\n25\tThe examples below use an installed `yamark` command. To keep running from PyPI without installing it, replace `yamark` with `uvx yamark`.\n26\t\n27\tFormat one or more files or directories in place:\n28\t\n29\t```sh\n30\tyamark format config.yaml docs/\n31\t```\n32\t\n33\tFormat the current directory:\n34\t\n35\t```sh\n36\tyamark format\n37\t```\n38\t\n39\tCheck whether files are already formatted without writing changes:\n40\t\n41\t```sh\n42\tyamark format --check docs/\n43\t```\n44\t\n45\tShow a unified diff without writing changes:\n46\t\n47\t```sh\n48\tyamark format --diff docs/\n49\t```\n50\t\n51\tFormat stdin for editor and CI integrations:\n52\t\n53\t```sh\n54\tyamark format --stdin-file-path config.yaml < config.yaml\n55\t```\n56\t\n57\tConvert JSON-family input from stdin to formatted YAML on stdout:\n58\t\n59\t```sh\n60\tyamark to-yaml --stdin-file-path data.json5 < data.json5\n61\t```\n62\t\n63\tThe path is not read or written. Its suffix selects the exact JSON dialect. This is a conversion, not source formatting.\n64\t\n65\tDirectory traversal skips hidden paths and respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and global Git ignore files by default. Pass a hidden path explicitly to format it.\n66\t\n67\tWhile formatting is enabled, standalone `{{< ... >}}` and `{{% ... %}}` shortcode tokens are preserved, including multiline tokens and quoted arguments. Directive-looking text inside a recognized token is data. Yamark does not match shortcode names or interpret their bodies: Markdown between tokens formats normally. An unterminated token or quote preserves the rest of the enclosing Markdown document or fragment. This does not guarantee rendering equivalence for arbitrary Hugo or Jinja templates.\n68\t\n69\tTo disable body formatting, surround the region with `<!-- fmt: off -->` and `<!-- fmt: on -->`. While formatting is disabled, directives follow the existing linewise policy: a recognized `fmt: on` line resumes formatting even if the surrounding text resembles a shortcode argument, code fence, HTML, or math block.\n70\t\n71\tExplicitly skipped Markdown retains its bytes, including trailing spaces and line endings: `<!-- fmt: skip -->` preserves the next selected node, `<!-- fmt: off -->` preserves the disabled region, and `<!-- fmt: skip file -->` preserves the enclosing Markdown document or fragment. This protection survives supported nesting in Markdown fences and divs; surrounding Markdown still formats.\n72\t\n73\t## Editor integrations\n74\t\n75\tThe VS Code and Positron formatter extension lives in `editors/vscode/`. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_013YEkwTUqrpCKU9CX9Uzeno","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t---\n2\t# fmt: skip file\n3\ttitle: Directives\n4\tdescription: Tell Yamark what to format, skip, preserve, or configure from inside the file.\n5\t---\n6\t\n7\t<!-- fmt: skip file -->\n8\t\n9\tThe source file is the primary interface. Put a small `fmt:` directive next to\n10\tthe text it controls, then let an editor or repository integration run Yamark.\n11\tBecause directives are comments, the formatting choice stays with the text.\n12\tThe comment marker depends on the file:\n13\t\n14\t| File | Directive comment |\n15\t| --- | --- |\n16\t| Markdown and Quarto | `<!-- fmt: ... -->` |\n17\t| YAML, Python, and R | `# fmt: ...` |\n18\t\n19\tQuarto chunk options use `#|`; for example, `#| fmt: skip`.\n20\t\n21\t## Target the next value or block\n22\t\n23\tMost directives apply to the next supported target. In a YAML file, that target\n24\tis usually a scalar node. In a Python or R file, it is usually a string literal\n25\tor a contiguous source-comment block. The directive does not format the\n26\tsurrounding Python or R source code.\n27\t\n28\t## YAML files\n29\t\n30\tMark a scalar as Markdown and choose sentence wrapping for that scalar:\n31\t\n32\t```yaml\n33\t# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence\n34\tdescription: \"Explain the project in a few clear sentences.\"\n35\tother_value: \"This is ordinary YAML, not Markdown.\"\n36\t```\n37\t\n38\tThe directive attaches to `description`, the next scalar. A tagged scalar is\n39\tanother way to mark Markdown when the setting should travel with the value:\n40\t\n41\t```yaml\n42\tinstructions: !markdown |\n43\t  # Review\n44\t\n45\t  Read the diff and report concrete correctness issues.\n46\t```\n47\t\n48\tUse the same placement for an embedded formatter. The formatter name is the\n49\tlanguage after `fmt:`:\n50\t\n51\t```yaml\n52\t# fmt: python\n53\tscript: |\n54\t  def check(items):return all(item > 0 for item in items)\n55\t```\n56\t\n57\tYAML also supports directives on a collection parent when the setting describes\n58\tthe collection rather than a scalar:\n59\t\n60\t```yaml\n61\t# fmt: table\n62\t- {name: alpha, type: string, default: \"\"}\n63\t- {name: beta, type: integer, default: 0}\n64\t```\n65\t\n66\t## Python files\n67\t\n68\tPut `# fmt: markdown` immediately before the string literal or comment block\n69\tthat contains Markdown:\n70\t\n71\t```python\n72\t# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence\n73\tREVIEW_PROMPT = \"\"\"\n74\t# Review\n75\t\n76\tRead the diff and report concrete correctness issues. Prefer specific examples.\n77\t\"\"\"\n78\t```\n79\t\n80\tThe `#` lines inside the string are Markdown content. Python outside the\n81\tmarked target is left for a Python formatter such as Ruff.\n82\t\n83\tThe same directive can target a Markdown comment block:\n84\t\n85\t```python\n86\t# fmt: markdown\n87\t# # Filters\n88\t#\n89\t# Apply the most specific filter first.\n90\t#\n91\t# - Each filter is a single expression.\n92\t```\n93\t\n94\tFor a non-Markdown embedded language, use its formatter name:\n95\t\n96\t```python\n97\t# fmt: r\n98\tanalysis = \"\"\"\n99\tf <- function(x) x + 1\n100\t\"\"\"\n101\t```\n102\t\n103\t## R files\n104\t\n105\tR uses the same `# fmt:` marker. It can target a raw string literal used for a\n106\tvignette, help text, or a Shiny message:\n107\t\n108\t```r\n109\t# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence\n110\thelp_text <- r\"(\n111\t# Filters\n112\t\n113\tApply the most specific filter first. Explain why a filter matched.\n114\t)\"\n115\t```\n116\t\n117\tIt can also target a contiguous Markdown comment block:\n118\t\n119\t```r\n120\t# fmt: markdown\n121\t# # Filters\n122\t#\n123\t# Apply the most specific filter first.\n124\t#\n125\t# - Each filter is a single expression.\n126\t```\n127\t\n128\tFor source code inside a YAML literal scalar, use the language formatter name\n129\tin the same way as in a YAML file:\n130\t\n131\t```yaml\n132\t# fmt: r\n133\tanalysis: |\n134\t  f <- function(x)x+1\n135\t```\n136\t\n137\t## Control a region or a whole file\n138\t\n139\tThe scope is part of the directive. `next` is the default for target directives.\n140\tUse `from-here` for the rest of a region, and `file` for a document-wide\n141\tsetting:\n142\t\n143\t| Scope | Applies to |\n144\t| --- | --- |\n145\t| `scope=next` | The next supported string, scalar, collection, or comment block. |\n146\t| `scope=from-here` | Supported content from this point until another directive changes the setting. |\n147\t| `scope=file` | The whole file, including supported content before the directive. |\n148\t\n149\tSkip one target:\n150\t\n151\t```yaml\n152\tnormal: [1, 2, 3]\n153\t# fmt: skip\n154\tmanual:\n155\t    -   [ 1,2,3]\n156\t```\n157\t\n158\tPreserve a region and resume formatting afterward:\n159\t\n160\t```markdown\n161\t<!-- fmt: off -->\n162\t#   Keep this heading ##\n163\t\n164\t<!-- fmt: on -->\n165\t```\n166\t\n167\tSkip a whole file by putting the file directive at the top. YAML, Python, and R\n168\tuse the same hash-comment form:\n169\t\n170\t```text\n171\t# fmt: skip file\n172\t```\n173\t\n174\tMarkdown uses an HTML comment:\n175\t\n176\t```markdown\n177\t<!-- fmt: skip file -->\n178\t```\n179\t\n180\tA whole-file skip is useful for generated files or files whose layout is\n181\tintentionally outside Yamark's scope.\n182\t\n183\tMarkdown skip controls retain trailing spaces and line endings in the selected\n184\tcontent, including supported nested Markdown.\n185\t\n186\t## Preserve intentional table widths\n187\t\n188\tYamark normally fits table columns to their contents. Keep a table's authored\n189\twidths while still formatting its contents:\n190\t\n191\t```markdown\n192\t<!-- fmt: table-widths=preserve scope=next -->\n193\t+----------+------------------+\n194\t| Name     | Description      |\n195\t+==========+==================+\n196\t| A        | Short text       |\n197\t+----------+------------------+\n198\t```\n199\t\n200\tUse `scope=file` to preserve widths throughout the document, or\n201\t`scope=from-here` for subsequent tables. A later\n202\t`table-widths=fit scope=from-here` resumes fitting widths. Both modes retain\n203\tcolumn alignment. Fitting widths can change the rendered proportions of\n204\tPandoc tables; preserving widths can retain excessive or cramped padding.\n205\t\n206\tFor Markdown inside YAML, Python, or R, the same option can accompany the\n207\ttarget marker: `# fmt: markdown table-widths=preserve`.\n208\t\n209\t## Set file-specific Markdown options\n210\t\n211\tUse `scope=file` when the file should have a different Markdown policy from the\n212\trepository default:\n213\t\n214\t```markdown\n215\t<!-- fmt: wrap=sentence:72 scope=file -->\n216\t```\n217\t\n218\tThis puts one sentence per line and wraps long sentences at column 72. Other\n219\tfile-wide Markdown options include `canonical=true` and\n220\t`footnotes=preserve`:\n221\t\n222\t```markdown\n223\t<!-- fmt: canonical=true footnotes=preserve scope=file -->\n224\t```\n225\t\n226\tFor a YAML file or a hashpipe YAML stream in Python or R, use the same scope to\n227\tset YAML behavior for the whole file:\n228\t\n229\t```yaml\n230\t# fmt: compact=false scope=file\n231\t```\n232\t\n233\tAn option-only directive such as `# fmt: canonical=true` adjusts the next\n234\talready-marked Markdown scalar. It does not turn an ordinary YAML scalar into a\n235\tMarkdown target:\n236\t\n237\t```yaml\n238\t# fmt: canonical=true\n239\tfirst: !markdown \"This is __strong__ Markdown.\"\n240\tsecond: \"This is ordinary YAML text.\"\n241\t```\n242\t\n243\t## Arrange for Yamark to run automatically\n244\t\n245\tOnce directives are in the files, configure Yamark to run as part of the\n246\tworkflow:\n247\t\n248\t- In an editor, enable format on save. The [Editors](editors.qmd) page shows\n249\t  the VS Code and Positron settings. This is the most direct way to see a\n250\t  directive take effect while editing.\n251\t- In a pre-commit hook, run `yamark format`. In CI, use\n252\t  `yamark format --check` to verify files without changing them.\n253\t\n254\tThe experimental [Git Filter](git-filter.qmd) serves a narrower workflow: it\n255\tstores selected Markdown files sentence-per-line while keeping the working tree\n256\tcolumn-wrapped.\n257\t\n258\t## When a repository default is better\n259\t\n260\tUse `yamark.toml` for settings that should apply broadly rather than to one\n261\tpiece of text. Keep local exceptions in directives so they stay beside the\n262\tcontent they explain.\n263\t\n264\tFor example, a repository can choose sentence-per-line Markdown and compact\n265\tYAML collections by default:\n266\t\n267\t```toml\n268\t[format]\n269\twrap = \"sentence:88\"\n270\tcompact = true\n271\t```\n272\t\n273\tYamark discovers `yamark.toml` from each formatted file's directory upward.\n274\tUse the [Configuration reference](reference-config.qmd) for the full\n275\t`[format]`, `[template]`, `[embedded]`, and `[paths]` schema.\n276\t\n277\t## For one-off runs\n278\t\n279\tCommand-line options are useful for trying a policy, checking files in CI, or\n280\toverriding a repository default for one invocation:\n281\t\n282\t```sh\n283\tyamark format --wrap sentence:72 docs/\n284\tyamark format --compact config.yaml\n285\tyamark format --check docs/\n286\t```\n287\t\n288\tUse the [Directive syntax reference](reference-directives.qmd) for every\n289\taccepted form, scope, and value.\n290\t\n291\tUse the [Command-line reference](cli-help.qmd) for the accepted arguments and\n292\t[Usage](usage.qmd) for installation and common commands.\n293\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":"toolu_012TVaAcbC3M6kTMPUD5ooJG","agent_id":"a8421a8d761b8e04c","session_id":"0e7cfb1b-67a4-4c6e-bc49-6d823e4685c0","uuid":"114182bf-0da2-4569-90fe-98c21b4bcdf2","timestamp":"2026-11-17T16:36:53.441Z","tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_013YEkwTUqrpCKU9CX9Uzeno","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}],"subagent_type":"general-purpose","task_description":"Write realistic test corpus E"}

For a guided path through YAML, Python, and R examples,\n11\tsee [Directives](directives.qmd).\n12\t\n13\t## Comment forms\n14\t\n15\t| Host | Form | Placement |\n16\t| --- | --- | --- |\n17\t| Markdown | `<!-- fmt: ... -->` | An own-line HTML comment. |\n18\t| YAML | `# fmt: ...` | An own-line hash comment. `fmt: table` and `fmt: compact table` may also be same-line comments on an empty-valued collection parent; a populated parent is an error. |\n19\t| Python and R | `# fmt: ...` | An own-line hash comment before a supported comment or string target. |\n20\t\n21\t## Scopes\n22\t\n23\t| Scope | Meaning |\n24\t| --- | --- |\n25\t| `scope=next` | Apply to the next supported target. This is the default for target-selecting, compact, table, and embedded-formatter directives. |\n26\t| `scope=from-here` | Apply from the directive until another directive changes the same state. |\n27\t| `scope=file` | Apply throughout the current parsed document or nested region, including supported nodes before the directive. At the top level, that region is the physical file. |\n28\t\n29\tNot every directive accepts every scope. The tables below list the supported\n30\tforms. An unsupported or misspelled explicit scope is an error. Template\n31\tdelimiter directives use the contextual rule described below instead of one\n32\tfixed default.\n33\t\n34\tScopes stop at the current parsed document or nested-region boundary. A\n35\tdirective inside a recursive fence affects that fence, not its Markdown host or\n36\tsibling fences. A `scope=file` directive inside one hashpipe YAML block does not\n37\tspan later blocks. `fmt: skip file` in Markdown front matter is the exception:\n38\tit preserves the outer Markdown document.\n39\t\n40\t## Preserve content\n41\t\n42\t| Directive | Scope | Effect |\n43\t| --- | --- | --- |\n44\t| `fmt: skip` | Next | Preserve the next supported target. `fmt: skip scope=next` is equivalent. |\n45\t| `fmt: skip file` | File | Preserve the current parsed document or nested region. `fmt: skip scope=file` is equivalent. |\n46\t| `fmt: off` | From here | Preserve content until `fmt: on`, or through the end of Markdown and source regions. `fmt: off scope=from-here` is equivalent. |\n47\t| `fmt: on` | - | Resume formatting after `fmt: off`. It does not accept an explicit scope. |\n48\t\n49\tThe same control uses the host's comment form:\n50\t\n51\t```yaml\n52\t# fmt: skip\n53\tmanual: [[ 1,2,3], [4,5,6]]\n54\t```\n55\t\n56\t```markdown\n57\t<!-- fmt: off -->\n58\t*   keep\n59\t    this\n60\t    list\n61\t<!-- fmt: on -->\n62\t```\n63\t\n64\tPreserve-control lifecycle checks are host-specific. YAML rejects a targetless\n65\t`skip`, a stray `on`, a nested `off`, and an `off` without a later `on`.\n66\tMarkdown and source regions allow `skip` at the end and let `off` preserve\n67\tthrough the end of the region.\n68\t\n69\t## Markdown targets and settings\n70\t\n71\t| Form | Default scope | Effect |\n72\t| --- | --- | --- |\n73\t| `fmt: markdown` | Next | Mark the next supported target as Markdown: a Markdown block, including a supported fence; a YAML scalar; or a source string or comment block. |\n74\t| `fmt: markdown wrap=sentence canonical=true` | Next | Mark the next supported target as Markdown and set its options. |\n75\t| `fmt: wrap=sentence` | `scope=next` in YAML; `scope=file` in Markdown or source regions | Change wrapping for an already recognized Markdown region without marking unrelated content. |\n76\t| `fmt: table-widths=preserve` | `scope=next` in YAML; `scope=file` in Markdown or source regions | Preserve widths in supported Markdown tables while formatting contents. A broad-scope directive changes Markdown settings; it\n91\tdoes not turn every plain scalar into Markdown.\n92\t\n93\tAccepted option values:\n94\t\n95\t| Option | Values |\n96\t| --- | --- |\n97\t| `wrap` | `none`, `paragraph`, `sentence`, `sentence:<n>`, or a positive integer. |\n98\t| `table-widths` | `fit` (the default) or `preserve`. Both preserve alignment. |\n99\t| `canonical` | `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. A bare `canonical` means `true`. |\n100\t| `footnotes` | `wrap`, `format`, `preserve`, `none`, `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. |\n101\t\n102\tFor `footnotes`, `wrap`, `format`, `true`, `yes`, and `1` request formatting;\n103\t`preserve`, `none`, `false`, `no`, and `0` request preservation.\n104\t\n105\t## YAML collections\n106\t\n107\t| Directive | Scope | Effect |\n108\t| --- | --- | --- |\n109\t| `fmt: compact` | Next | Enable block-to-flow compaction for the next eligible collection. |\n110\t| `fmt: compact false` | Next | Disable compaction for the next eligible collection. `fmt: compact=false` is equivalent. |\n111\t| `fmt: compact scope=from-here` | From here | Enable compaction until another compact directive changes the state. |\n112\t| `fmt: compact=false scope=file` | File | Disable compaction throughout the current YAML document or one source-file hashpipe YAML block. |\n113\t| `fmt: table` | Next | Align the next compatible sequence of flow mappings. |\n114\t| `fmt: compact table` | Next | Collapse eligible block mapping rows before aligning them. `fmt: table compact` and `fmt: table compact=true` are equivalent. |\n115\t\n116\t`fmt: table` accepts only its default next-target scope. Compact directives\n117\taccept `next`, `from-here`, and `file`.\n118\t\n119\t`compact`, `compact=true`, `compact=yes`, `compact=1`, and `compact true`\n120\tenable compaction. `compact=false`, `compact=no`, `compact=0`, and\n121\t`compact false` disable it. The separated form accepts only `true` or `false`.\n122\t\n123\t## Templates and embedded formatters\n124\t\n125\t| Directive | Scope | Effect |\n126\t| --- | --- | --- |\n127\t| `fmt: template.delimiters \"<<\" \">>\"` | Inferred | Add one non-empty double-quoted delimiter pair using the placement rule below. |\n128\t| `fmt: template.delimiters \"<<\" \">>\" scope=next` | Next | Add the pair to the next supported target. |\n129\t| `fmt: template.delimiters \"<<\" \">>\" scope=from-here` | From here | Add the pair to following supported targets. |\n130\t| `fmt: template.delimiters \"<<\" \">>\" scope=file` | File | Add the pair throughout the current document or nested region. |\n131\t| `fmt: embedded python` | Next | Format the next supported string or YAML literal scalar with the named formatter. |\n132\t| `fmt: python` | Next | Shorthand for `fmt: embedded python`. |\n133\t\n134\tA bare `fmt: template.delimiters` directive uses the next target when placed\n135\tdirectly before one. Normal formatting does not select these files. |\n18\t| Markdown fences named `yaml`, `yml`, `markdown`, or `md` | YAML, or recursively formatted Markdown. | Automatic unless the fence is locally skipped. |\n19\t| Markdown source fences | Python, R, JSON, GraphQL, CSS, HTML, JavaScript, TypeScript, and related aliases. | Delegated when a matching embedded formatter is available. |\n20\t| YAML scalars tagged `!markdown` or `!md` | The scalar value as Markdown. | Explicit tag. |\n21\t| YAML scalars following `# fmt: markdown` | The scalar value as Markdown. | Explicit directive. |\n22\t| YAML literal scalars following `# fmt: <name>` or `# fmt: embedded <name>` | The scalar value through a built-in or configured embedded formatter. | Explicit directive. |\n23\t\n24\tExtension matching is ASCII case-insensitive.
