Wie viele Beobachtungen fehlen? Entfernt diese mit `drop_na()` und begründet in einem Satz, warum das hier vertretbar ist. Erstellt anschließend ein Histogramm der Differenzen (Abb. 1).\n2. Formuliert die Hypothesen $H_0\\colon \\mu_D = 0$ und $H_1\\colon \\mu_D \\neq 0$ in Worten. Achtung: Es geht um die *Differenz* je Person, nicht um zwei unabhängige Gruppen! Warum ist das wichtig?\n3. Führt einen gepaarten $t$-Test zum Niveau $\\alpha = 0{,}05$ durch. Gebt die Teststatistik, die Freiheitsgrade und den $p$-Wert an. Ein Ergebnis wie „p = 0.000“ ist keine gültige Angabe; schreibt stattdessen $p < 0{,}001$.\n4. Prof. Koch behauptet: „Der Effekt ist signifikant, also ist er auch wichtig.“ Stimmt das? Diskutiert die Aussage mit Hilfe der Effektstärke $d = \\bar{d}/s_d$ (vgl. Skript, Kap. 5, S. 42).\n5. **Bonus (2 P.):** Wiederholt den Test mit einem Wilcoxon-Vorzeichen-Rang-Test. Ändert sich eure Schlussfolgerung? Wenn ja, warum?\nTipp: `wilcox.test(..., paired = TRUE)`. Lest vorher die Hilfeseite, insbesondere den Abschnitt „Details“.\n\nZur Erinnerung: Die Teststatistik des gepaarten $t$-Tests lautet\n\n$$\nT = \\frac{\\bar{d}}{s_d / \\sqrt{n}} \\sim t_{n-1} \\quad \\text{unter } H_0 .\n$$\n\nBei n = 30 Paaren hat die Verteilung also 29 Freiheitsgrade. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Ch8rj7eaDZbArWyCBM39E","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01CNnGcsKHWfrX9aSWd5Lj57","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/tmp/corpus5/e/rmarkdown_sentence_wrap.Rmd","content":"---\ntitle: \"EXP-117: batched GraphQL queries on checkout -- A/B readout\"\nauthor: \"Growth Eng x Platform SRE\"\ndate: \"`r format(Sys.Date(), '%d %B %Y')`\"\noutput:\n  html_document:\n    toc: true\n    toc_float: TRUE\n    code_folding: hide\n    df_print: paged\nparams:\n    exp_id: \"EXP-117\"\n    alpha: 0.05\n    mde:   0.01\neditor_options:\n  markdown:\n    wrap: sentence\n    canonical: true\n  chunk_output_type: console\n---\n\n```{r setup, include=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=4, dpi=150}\nlibrary(data.table)\nlibrary(ggplot2)\nexp <- fread(here::here(\"data\", \"exp117_assignments.csv\"))\nn_control <- exp[arm == \"control\", uniqueN(user_id)]\nn_treat <- exp[arm == \"treatment\", uniqueN(user_id)]\n```\n\n## TL;DR\n\nWe tested whether batching the three checkout queries (cart, shipping options, payment methods) into one persisted GraphQL operation reduces checkout abandonment. It does! Conversion in the treatment arm was 4.71% vs. 4.56% in control, a relative lift of 3.2%. The result is significant at the pre-registered alpha of `r params$alpha` (p = 0.012, two-sided) and the direction is the same in all three regions (see Sec. 4). We recommend shipping to 100% behind the existing flag `checkout.batched-queries` and deleting the flag after two weeks.\n\n## Background\n\nCheckout makes three round-trips to the gateway before the \"Pay\" button becomes active. On mobile networks in ap-southeast-2 that is approx. 900 ms of extra latency at the median and roughly 2.1 s at the p90. Product had a hunch that this mattered; the platform team had a hunch that it didn't, i.e. that users wait anyway. One reviewer called the whole thing \"premature optimization.\" This experiment was meant to settle the question (and, frankly, the argument).\n\nThe design follows the usual playbook (cf. the experimentation guide, p. 4): user-level randomization via flagd's `fractional` operator, a 50/50 split, and a fixed horizon of 14 days from a power analysis for an MDE of `r scales::percent(params$mde)` relative.\nDr. Okafor reviewed the analysis plan before launch on Oct. 2. We did not peek... well, we peeked once, on day 3, because the dashboard was public. We did _not_ act on it.\n\n## Data\n\n```{r load}\n#| echo:    false\n#| cache: TRUE\n#| dependson: [ \"setup\" ]\norders <- fread(here::here(\"data\", \"exp117_orders.csv\"))\nconv <- merge(exp, orders[, .(converted = any(status == \"created\")), by = user_id], by = \"user_id\", all.x = TRUE)\nconv[is.na(converted), converted := FALSE]\n```\n\nAssignment was balanced: `r format(n_control, big.mark = \",\")` users in control vs. `r format(n_treat, big.mark = \",\")` in treatment (SRM check p = 0.41). Bots, internal users (e.g. anyone with a `kestrel.dev` address) and users who never reached the cart were excluded before assignment, not after. About 0.8% of sessions were dropped because old app versions (< 5.12) ignore the flag and keep sending the unbatched operations. These users were in both arms in equal numbers, so this shouldn't bias anything.\n\n## Results\n\n### Primary metric: checkout conversion\n\n```{r primary, fig.cap=\"Conversion by arm with 95% CI.\"}\nres <- conv[, .(rate = mean(converted), n = .N), by = arm]\nres[, se := sqrt(rate * (1 - rate) / n)]\nggplot(res, aes(arm, rate)) +\n  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = rate - 1.96 * se, ymax = rate + 1.96 * se)) +\n  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent)\n```\n\nTreatment converted at 4.71% and control at 4.56%. The absolute difference is 0.15 percentage points (95% CI: 0.03 to 0.27). That is a relative lift of 3.2%. Is that a lot? For checkout, yes: at current volume it is worth roughly $41k per month in recovered orders, give or take novelty effects, seasonality, etc. The U.S. holiday season starts in four weeks, so the real number may well be higher.\n\n### Secondary metrics\n\n- __Time to interactive on the payment step__ dropped from 1.84 s to 1.12 s at the median. The p90 improved even more (3.9 s to 2.2 s), mostly in ap-southeast-2.\n- __Gateway load.__ Batching cut checkout-related requests by 61%. CPU per request went up a bit because the batched operation is larger, but total checkout CPU fell by approx. 35%.\n- __Error rate__ was flat at 0.21% in both arms. We were worried that one failing subgraph would now fail the whole batch. It didn't, because the router returns partial data plus an `errors` array instead of failing the operation (see Fig. 2 in the gateway docs).\n\n### By region\n\n```{r by-region}\n#| tbl-cap:   \"Relative lift by region with 95% CI\"\n#| echo: false\nby_region <- conv[, .(rate = mean(converted)), by = .(region, arm)]\nknitr::kable(dcast(by_region, region ~ arm, value.var = \"rate\"), digits = 4)\n```\n\nThe effect is largest in ap-southeast-2 (+5.9%), where round-trips are slowest, and smallest in us-east-1 (+2.4%). That matches the latency story nicely! Note that the per-region intervals are wide; with n = 14,180 per arm in ap-southeast-2 we can't claim the regions differ from each other (interaction p = 0.18).\n\n| Region | Control | Treatment | Lift |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| us-east-1 | 4.61% | 4.72% | +2.4% |\n| eu-west-1 | 4.55% | 4.69% | +3.1% |\n| ap-southeast-2 | 4.38% | 4.64% | +5.9% |\n\n## Caveats\n\n1. The experiment overlapped with INC-2291. We excluded the 47 minutes of the eu-west-1 brownout (14:02 to 14:49 UTC on Oct. 17). Including them moves the lift to 3.0%, so the conclusion holds.\n2. \"Conversion\" means an order was created, not that it was paid. Payment failures are tracked separately and were flat (0.9% in both arms).\n3. Novelty effects are unlikely for a pure latency change. We'll keep a 5% holdout for another month anyway!\n\n## Recommendation\n\nShip it. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01TqZA36CCS8hLrMfkopygRH","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t---\n2\t# fmt: skip file\n3\ttitle: Directives\n4\tdescription: Tell Yamark what to format, skip, preserve, or configure from inside the file.\n5\t---\n6\t\n7\t<!-- fmt: skip file -->\n8\t\n9\tThe source file is the primary interface. Put a small `fmt:` directive next to\n10\tthe text it controls, then let an editor or repository integration run Yamark.\n11\tBecause directives are comments, the formatting choice stays with the text.\n12\tThe comment marker depends on the file:\n13\t\n14\t| File | Directive comment |\n15\t| --- | --- |\n16\t| Markdown and Quarto | `<!-- fmt: ... -->` |\n17\t| YAML, Python, and R | `# fmt: ...` |\n18\t\n19\tQuarto chunk options use `#|`; for example, `#| fmt: skip`.\n20\t\n21\t## Target the next value or block\n22\t\n23\tMost directives apply to the next supported target. In a YAML file, that target\n24\tis usually a scalar node. In a Python or R file, it is usually a string literal\n25\tor a contiguous source-comment block. The directive does not format the\n26\tsurrounding Python or R source code.\n27\t\n28\t## YAML files\n29\t\n30\tMark a scalar as Markdown and choose sentence wrapping for that scalar:\n31\t\n32\t```yaml\n33\t# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence\n34\tdescription: \"Explain the project in a few clear sentences.\"\n35\tother_value: \"This is ordinary YAML, not Markdown.\"\n36\t```\n37\t\n38\tThe directive attaches to `description`, the next scalar. A tagged scalar is\n39\tanother way to mark Markdown when the setting should travel with the value:\n40\t\n41\t```yaml\n42\tinstructions: !markdown |\n43\t  # Review\n44\t\n45\t  Read the diff and report concrete correctness issues.\n46\t```\n47\t\n48\tUse the same placement for an embedded formatter. The formatter name is the\n49\tlanguage after `fmt:`:\n50\t\n51\t```yaml\n52\t# fmt: python\n53\tscript: |\n54\t  def check(items):return all(item > 0 for item in items)\n55\t```\n56\t\n57\tYAML also supports directives on a collection parent when the setting describes\n58\tthe collection rather than a scalar:\n59\t\n60\t```yaml\n61\t# fmt: table\n62\t- {name: alpha, type: string, default: \"\"}\n63\t- {name: beta, type: integer, default: 0}\n64\t```\n65\t\n66\t## Python files\n67\t\n68\tPut `# fmt: markdown` immediately before the string literal or comment block\n69\tthat contains Markdown:\n70\t\n71\t```python\n72\t# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence\n73\tREVIEW_PROMPT = \"\"\"\n74\t# Review\n75\t\n76\tRead the diff and report concrete correctness issues. Prefer specific examples.\n77\t\"\"\"\n78\t```\n79\t\n80\tThe `#` lines inside the string are Markdown content. Python outside the\n81\tmarked target is left for a Python formatter such as Ruff.\n82\t\n83\tThe same directive can target a Markdown comment block:\n84\t\n85\t```python\n86\t# fmt: markdown\n87\t# # Filters\n88\t#\n89\t# Apply the most specific filter first.\n90\t#\n91\t# - Each filter is a single expression.\n92\t```\n93\t\n94\tFor a non-Markdown embedded language, use its formatter name:\n95\t\n96\t```python\n97\t# fmt: r\n98\tanalysis = \"\"\"\n99\tf <- function(x) x + 1\n100\t\"\"\"\n101\t```\n102\t\n103\t## R files\n104\t\n105\tR uses the same `# fmt:` marker. It can target a raw string literal used for a\n106\tvignette, help text, or a Shiny message:\n107\t\n108\t```r\n109\t# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence\n110\thelp_text <- r\"(\n111\t# Filters\n112\t\n113\tApply the most specific filter first. Explain why a filter matched.\n114\t)\"\n115\t```\n116\t\n117\tIt can also target a contiguous Markdown comment block:\n118\t\n119\t```r\n120\t# fmt: markdown\n121\t# # Filters\n122\t#\n123\t# Apply the most specific filter first.\n124\t#\n125\t# - Each filter is a single expression.\n126\t```\n127\t\n128\tFor source code inside a YAML literal scalar, use the language formatter name\n129\tin the same way as in a YAML file:\n130\t\n131\t```yaml\n132\t# fmt: r\n133\tanalysis: |\n134\t  f <- function(x)x+1\n135\t```\n136\t\n137\t## Control a region or a whole file\n138\t\n139\tThe scope is part of the directive. `next` is the default for target directives.\n140\tUse `from-here` for the rest of a region, and `file` for a document-wide\n141\tsetting:\n142\t\n143\t| Scope | Applies to |\n144\t| --- | --- |\n145\t| `scope=next` | The next supported string, scalar, collection, or comment block. |\n146\t| `scope=from-here` | Supported content from this point until another directive changes the setting. |\n147\t| `scope=file` | The whole file, including supported content before the directive. |\n148\t\n149\tSkip one target:\n150\t\n151\t```yaml\n152\tnormal: [1, 2, 3]\n153\t# fmt: skip\n154\tmanual:\n155\t    -   [ 1,2,3]\n156\t```\n157\t\n158\tPreserve a region and resume formatting afterward:\n159\t\n160\t```markdown\n161\t<!-- fmt: off -->\n162\t#   Keep this heading ##\n163\t\n164\t<!-- fmt: on -->\n165\t```\n166\t\n167\tSkip a whole file by putting the file directive at the top. YAML, Python, and R\n168\tuse the same hash-comment form:\n169\t\n170\t```text\n171\t# fmt: skip file\n172\t```\n173\t\n174\tMarkdown uses an HTML comment:\n175\t\n176\t```markdown\n177\t<!-- fmt: skip file -->\n178\t```\n179\t\n180\tA whole-file skip is useful for generated files or files whose layout is\n181\tintentionally outside Yamark's scope.\n182\t\n183\tMarkdown skip controls retain trailing spaces and line endings in the selected\n184\tcontent, including supported nested Markdown.\n185\t\n186\t## Preserve intentional table widths\n187\t\n188\tYamark normally fits table columns to their contents. Keep a table's authored\n189\twidths while still formatting its contents:\n190\t\n191\t```markdown\n192\t<!-- fmt: table-widths=preserve scope=next -->\n193\t+----------+------------------+\n194\t| Name     | Description      |\n195\t+==========+==================+\n196\t| A        | Short text       |\n197\t+----------+------------------+\n198\t```\n199\t\n200\tUse `scope=file` to preserve widths throughout the document, or\n201\t`scope=from-here` for subsequent tables. A later\n202\t`table-widths=fit scope=from-here` resumes fitting widths. Both modes retain\n203\tcolumn alignment. Fitting widths can change the rendered proportions of\n204\tPandoc tables; preserving widths can retain excessive or cramped padding.\n205\t\n206\tFor Markdown inside YAML, Python, or R, the same option can accompany the\n207\ttarget marker: `# fmt: markdown table-widths=preserve`.\n208\t\n209\t## Set file-specific Markdown options\n210\t\n211\tUse `scope=file` when the file should have a different Markdown policy from the\n212\trepository default:\n213\t\n214\t```markdown\n215\t<!-- fmt: wrap=sentence:72 scope=file -->\n216\t```\n217\t\n218\tThis puts one sentence per line and wraps long sentences at column 72. Other\n219\tfile-wide Markdown options include `canonical=true` and\n220\t`footnotes=preserve`:\n221\t\n222\t```markdown\n223\t<!-- fmt: canonical=true footnotes=preserve scope=file -->\n224\t```\n225\t\n226\tFor a YAML file or a hashpipe YAML stream in Python or R, use the same scope to\n227\tset YAML behavior for the whole file:\n228\t\n229\t```yaml\n230\t# fmt: compact=false scope=file\n231\t```\n232\t\n233\tAn option-only directive such as `# fmt: canonical=true` adjusts the next\n234\talready-marked Markdown scalar. It does not turn an ordinary YAML scalar into a\n235\tMarkdown target:\n236\t\n237\t```yaml\n238\t# fmt: canonical=true\n239\tfirst: !markdown \"This is __strong__ Markdown.\"\n240\tsecond: \"This is ordinary YAML text.\"\n241\t```\n242\t\n243\t## Arrange for Yamark to run automatically\n244\t\n245\tOnce directives are in the files, configure Yamark to run as part of the\n246\tworkflow:\n247\t\n248\t- In an editor, enable format on save. The [Editors](editors.qmd) page shows\n249\t  the VS Code and Positron settings. At the top level, that region is the physical file. |\n28\t\n29\tNot every directive accepts every scope. The tables below list the supported\n30\tforms. An unsupported or misspelled explicit scope is an error. Template\n31\tdelimiter directives use the contextual rule described below instead of one\n32\tfixed default.\n33\t\n34\tScopes stop at the current parsed document or nested-region boundary. RStudio's visual writer does not\n33\trecognize the combined value.\n34\t\n35\t### Table widths\n36\t\n37\t`fit` sizes supported pipe, simple, grid, and multiline table columns from\n38\ttheir contents, with consistent padding. It can shrink excessive widths or\n39\texpand cramped columns. Both modes preserve column alignment and multiline\n40\tcell breaks.\n41\t\n42\t`preserve` retains the source widths while still formatting cell contents.\n43\tFor Pandoc tables, this keeps the borders and gaps that determine widths. For\n44\tpipe tables, it keeps separator lengths and row widths, even when the original\n45\trows are not aligned with one another.\n46\t\n47\tPandoc can use source widths to determine rendered column proportions and\n48\twrapping. A later `table-widths=fit scope=from-here` resumes fitting widths.\n61\tWithout an explicit scope, this option follows the usual Markdown directive\n62\tdefault of `scope=file`.\n63\t\n64\tThe setting also works in front matter, `yamark.toml`, and the command line.\n65\tExplicit renderer settings such as Quarto's `tbl-colwidths` remain unchanged.\n66\t`fmt: skip` preserves the entire table when exact source layout matters.\n67\tUnsupported table structures remain unchanged in either mode.\n68\t\n69\t### Canonical and footnote values\n70\t\n71\t`canonical` accepts `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0` in front matter\n72\tand directives. A bare `canonical` directive means `canonical=true`. Canonical\n73\tmode rewrites supported `_emphasis_` and `__strong__` spans as `*emphasis*` and\n74\t`**strong**`. It preserves protected or unsupported spans, including intraword\n75\tunderscores, code spans, link destinations, raw HTML, and template content.\n76\t\n77\tFor `footnotes`, `wrap`, `format`, `true`, `yes`, and `1` format footnote\n78\tdefinitions. `preserve`, `none`, `false`, `no`, and `0` preserve them.\n79\t`--preserve-footnotes` preserves Markdown footnote definitions byte-for-byte.\n80\t\n81\t## YAML settings\n82\t\n83\t| Behavior | Control | Default | Effect |\n84\t| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n85\t| Structural line width | `--line-width <n>` | 80 | Expands block-renderable flow collections when they exceed the width. Over-width flow collections that cannot be rendered safely in block style may be preserved. Also bounds compact and layout-repair output. |\n86\t| Folded scalar prose width | `--prose-width <n>` | 72 | Wraps eligible folded YAML prose. |\n87\t| Block indentation | `--indent-width <n>` | 2 | Sets indentation for emitted block mappings and sequences. |\n88\t| Compact collections | `--compact`, `[format].compact`, or `fmt: compact` | Off | Collapses eligible block collections to flow style when they fit. |\n89\t| Aligned flow mappings | `fmt: table` or `fmt: compact table` | Off | Aligns a following sequence of compatible flow mappings. The compact form first collapses eligible block rows. |\n90\t\n91\tAll width and indentation values must be positive integers.\n92\t\n93\tCanonical mode also permits limited rewrapping of short existing folded YAML\n94\tprose scalars when their value stays unchanged.\n95\t\n96\t## Execution controls\n97\t\n98\t| Control | Effect |\n99\t| --- | --- |\n100\t| `--diagnostics` | For YAML input, emits trace counters; it also emits notes for skipped or failing optional embedded formatters. |\n101\t| `--skip-embedded-formatters` | Disables external formatters while keeping Yamark's Markdown, YAML, front matter, and recursive Markdown formatting active. |\n102\t| `--config <path>` | Uses one explicit `yamark.toml` for all selected files instead of discovering one per file. |\n103\t\n104\t### Embedded formatter controls\n105\t\n106\t| Need | Control |\n107\t| --- | --- |\n108\t| Select a target | Use a recognized Markdown fence language or a [`fmt: <name>` directive](reference-directives.qmd#templates-and-embedded-formatters). |\n109\t| Register or replace a formatter | Add an [`[embedded.<name>]` table](reference-config.qmd#embedded) to `yamark.toml`. |\n110\t| Disable external formatters for one run | Pass `--skip-embedded-formatters`. |\n111\t| Explain an optional formatter skip | Pass `--diagnostics`. |\n112\t\n113\tWrite, check, diff, and stdin behavior is documented under\n114\t[Command line](cli-help.qmd#modes-output-and-status).\n115\t\n116\t## Document Markdown options\n117\t\n118\tMarkdown front matter can set document-local options under\n119\t`editor_options.markdown`:\n120\t\n121\t```markdown\n122\t---\n123\teditor_options:\n124\t  markdown:\n125\t    wrap: sentence:72\n126\t    canonical: true\n127\t    footnotes: preserve\n128\t    table-widths: preserve\n129\t---\n130\tThis is __strong__. This is _emphasis_.\n131\t```\n132\t\n133\t| Key | Accepted values |\n134\t| --- | --- |\n135\t| `wrap` | `none`, `paragraph`, `sentence`, `sentence:<n>`, or a positive integer column. |\n136\t| `table-widths` | `fit` or `preserve`. |\n137\t| `canonical` | `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. |\n138\t| `footnotes` | `wrap`, `format`, `preserve`, `none`, `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. |\n139\t\n140\tUnknown front-matter keys and unrecognized values are ignored; the\n141\tcorresponding base setting remains active. Invalid `yamark.toml` keys or\n142\tdirective values are errors instead.\n143\t\n144\tThese options apply after the front matter to the Markdown body, recursive\n145\t`markdown` or `md` fences, and Markdown-valued YAML scalars in nested YAML\n146\tregions.\n147\t\n148\tYamark also reads `editor.markdown` for compatibility, but only when\n149\t`editor_options.markdown` is absent. It does not merge the two tables. Git\n150\tfilter subcommands use their own wrapping options and do not read document\n151\toptions.\n152\t\n153\t## Interaction rules\n154\t\n155\tMarkdown settings are applied in this order:\n156\t\n157\t1. Command defaults and config establish the base settings. Explicit `--wrap`\n158\t   and `--table-widths` values override their corresponding `[format]` config\n159\t   values.\n160\t2. Prefer concrete suggestions: name the function, name the case.\n90\t  summarizer:\n91\t    # fmt: markdown\n92\t    instructions: |\n93\t      You write release notes.\n94\t\n95\t      - One bullet per user-visible change.\n96\t      - No internal refactors.\n97\t```\n98\t::::\n99\t\n100\tThe tagged value contains only prose, so Yamark rewraps it as a folded block.\n101\tThe comment-marked value contains a list, so Yamark keeps literal block style\n102\t(`|`) because folding would destroy the line breaks Markdown depends on.\n103\t\n104\t### Source code in YAML\n105\t\n106\tYAML values can also contain source code. Use `# fmt: python`, `# fmt: r`, or\n107\tthe name of another configured formatter before a literal block. When the\n108\tformatter is available, Yamark formats the block and restores its indentation\n109\tin the YAML file.\n110\t\n111\t:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n112\t**Before**\n113\t\n114\t```yaml\n115\t# fmt: python\n116\tpreflight: |\n117\t  def check(items):return all(x>0 for x in items)\n118\t```\n119\t\n120\t**After**\n121\t\n122\t```yaml\n123\t# fmt: python\n124\tpreflight: |\n125\t  def check(items):\n126\t    return all(x > 0 for x in items)\n127\t```\n128\t::::\n129\t\n130\t### YAML scalar presentation\n131\t\n132\tYamark changes scalar spelling only when the parsed YAML value and tag\n133\tstay equivalent. It can simplify safe quoted strings, keep strings that\n134\twould be misread as booleans, convert hard newlines to literal blocks,\n135\tand fold long prose strings.\n136\t\n137\t:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n138\t**Before**\n139\t\n140\t```yaml\n141\ttitle: \"hello\"\n142\tboolish: \"true\"\n143\tbody: \"alpha\\nbeta\\n\"\n144\tsummary: \"This package formats YAML front matter and configuration files while preserving semantics, comments, and repository-friendly diffs.\"\n145\t```\n146\t\n147\t**After**\n148\t\n149\t```yaml\n150\ttitle: hello\n151\tboolish: \"true\"\n152\tbody: |\n153\t  alpha\n154\t  beta\n155\tsummary: >-\n156\t  This package formats YAML front matter and configuration files while\n157\t  preserving semantics, comments, and repository-friendly diffs.\n158\t```\n159\t::::\n160\t\n161\t## Markdown links, footnotes, and tables\n162\t\n163\tLong inline links are split at Markdown syntax boundaries. Footnote\n164\tdefinitions wrap under the marker unless the document or CLI asks to\n165\tpreserve them.\n166\t\n167\t:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n168\t**Before**\n169\t\n170\t```markdown\n171\tPlease be mindful of our [code of conduct](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/main/.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) as you interact with other community members.\n172\t\n173\tBody text with a footnote.[^long]\n174\t\n175\t[^long]: This footnote explains that comments were removed because people used comments to hold parsing directives and enough extra words to wrap.\n176\t```\n177\t\n178\t**After**\n179\t\n180\t```markdown\n181\tPlease be mindful of our [code of conduct](\n182\t  https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/main/.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md\n183\t) as you interact with other community members.\n184\t\n185\tBody text with a footnote.[^long]\n186\t\n187\t[^long]: This footnote explains that comments were removed because\n188\t  people used comments to hold parsing directives and enough extra words\n189\t  to wrap.\n190\t```\n191\t::::\n192\t\n193\tSimple GFM pipe tables are aligned by display width. Git clean/smudge filters\n194\talways use compact pipe-table output.\n195\t\n196\t:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n197\t**Before**\n198\t\n199\t```markdown\n200\t| package | label |\n201\t|---|---|\n202\t| dplyr | tidy |\n203\t| tidyr | pivoting |\n204\t```\n205\t\n206\t**After**\n207\t\n208\t```markdown\n209\t| package | label    |\n210\t| ------- | -------- |\n211\t| dplyr   | tidy     |\n212\t| tidyr   | pivoting |\n213\t```\n214\t::::\n215\t\n216\t## Markdown in source files\n217\t\n218\t### Hashpipe YAML in source files\n219\t\n220\tConsecutive own-line `#|` comments in Python and R are a YAML block. Yamark\n221\tformats the comment body as YAML, restores the hashpipe prefix, and leaves the\n222\tsurrounding source code unchanged. This recognition is automatic; it does not\n223\tneed a `fmt:` directive.\n224\t\n225\t:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n226\t**Before**\n227\t\n228\t```r\n229\t#| name: demo\n230\t#| launcher:\n231\t#|  vanilla: true\n232\t#|  default-packages: [base,utils]\n233\t\n234\tmain <- function() NULL\n235\t```\n236\t\n237\t**After**\n238\t\n239\t```r\n240\t#| name: demo\n241\t#| launcher:\n242\t#|   vanilla: true\n243\t#|   default-packages: [base, utils]\n244\t\n245\tmain <- function() NULL\n246\t```\n247\t::::\n248\t\n249\t### Embedded Markdown in Python\n250\t\n251\tWhen a prompt lives next to the code that uses it, Yamark can format the prose\n252\twithout changing the surrounding Python. Add `# fmt: markdown` before the\n253\tstring:\n254\t\n255\t:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n256\t**Before**\n257\t\n258\t```python\n259\t# fmt: markdown\n260\tREVIEW_PROMPT = \"\"\"\n261\t# Review\n262\t\n263\tRead the diff and flag anything that violates the style guide, has obvious correctness issues, or looks untested.\n264\t\n265\t-   Prefer specific suggestions over vague concerns.\n266\t-   Name the function and the case.\n267\t\"\"\"\n268\t```\n269\t\n270\t**After**\n271\t\n272\t```python\n273\t# fmt: markdown\n274\tREVIEW_PROMPT = \"\"\"\n275\t# Review\n276\t\n277\tRead the diff and flag anything that violates the style guide, has\n278\tobvious correctness issues, or looks untested.\n279\t\n280\t- Prefer specific suggestions over vague concerns.\n281\t- Name the function and the case.\n282\t\"\"\"\n283\t```\n284\t::::\n285\t\n286\tPython source outside the marked string is left untouched. Run `ruff format` for\n287\tthat.\n288\t\n289\t### Embedded Markdown in source comments\n290\t\n291\tThe same directive can target a contiguous source comment block. This is useful\n292\tfor generated help text or documentation snippets where a string literal is not\n293\tthe right host.\n294\t\n295\t:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n296\t**Before**\n297\t\n298\t```python\n299\t# fmt: markdown\n300\t# #   Filters\n301\t#\n302\t# Apply one or more filters. Put the most specific filter first.\n314\t#\n315\t# - Each filter is a single expression.\n316\t```\n317\t::::\n318\t\n319\t### Embedded Markdown in R\n320\t\n321\tThe same pattern works for R raw strings. It can format package vignettes,\n322\tdocumentation fragments, and Shiny help text kept next to the code that renders\n323\tit.\n324\t\n325\t:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n326\t**Before**\n327\t\n328\t```r\n329\t# fmt: markdown\n330\thelp_text <- r\"(\n331\t# Filters\n332\t\n333\tApply one or more filters. Yamark\n362\tinserts a leading `---` document-start marker before every record, including\n363\tthe first, producing a valid YAML multi-document stream. The example below uses\n364\trecords from agent runs.\n365\t\n366\t:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n367\t**Before**\n368\t\n369\t```yaml\n370\t{\"id\":1,\"profile\":{\"name\":\"planner\",\"active\":true}}\n371\t{\"id\":2,\"profile\":{\"name\":\"researcher\",\"active\":true},\"usage\":{\"input_tokens\":640,\"output_tokens\":128}}\n372\t{\"id\":3,\"profile\":{\"name\":\"reviewer\",\"active\":true,\"model\":\"gpt-5\",\"region\":\"us\",\"tools\":[\"search\",\"python\"]},\"events\":[{\"type\":\"tool_call\",\"tools\":[\"search\",\"open\",\"python\",\"write\"]},{\"type\":\"usage\",\"tokens\":{\"input\":900,\"output\":240}},{\"type\":\"completion\",\"status\":\"ok\"}]}\n373\t```\n374\t\n375\t**After**\n376\t\n377\t```yaml\n378\t---\n379\t{id: 1, profile: {name: planner, active: true}}\n380\t---\n381\tid: 2\n382\tprofile: {name: researcher, active: true}\n383\tusage: {input_tokens: 640, output_tokens: 128}\n384\t---\n385\tid: 3\n386\tprofile:\n387\t  name: reviewer\n388\t  active: true\n389\t  model: gpt-5\n390\t  region: us\n391\t  tools: [search, python]\n392\tevents:\n393\t  - {type: tool_call, tools: [search, open, python, write]}\n394\t  - {type: usage, tokens: {input: 900, output: 240}}\n395\t  - {type: completion, status: ok}\n396\t```\n397\t::::\n398\t\n399\tYamark keeps each document as compact as the width allows. The first record\n400\tstays in flow style; the second expands only its root mapping; the third also\n401\texpands `profile` and `events`. Smaller mappings and sequences remain in flow\n402\tstyle whenever they still fit within `--line-width`. This conversion is for\n403\tobject records, not arbitrary JSON values.\n404\t\n405\t### Aligned flow-mapping tables\n406\t\n407\tA sequence of similar flow mappings can be easier to scan as a table. Mark it\n408\twith `# fmt: table` and Yamark aligns columns by key:\n409\t\n410\t:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n411\t**Before**\n412\t\n413\t```yaml\n414\t# fmt: table\n415\t- {name: alpha,type: string,default: [one,two],description: \"Short\"}\n416\t- {name: beta,type: int,default: 0,description: \"Number\"}\n417\t```\n418\t\n419\t**After**\n420\t\n421\t```yaml\n422\t# fmt: table\n423\t- {name: alpha, type: string, default: [one, two], description: Short}\n424\t- {name: beta,  type: int,    default: 0,          description: Number}\n425\t```\n426\t::::\n427\t\n428\t### Compact collections\n429\t\n430\tShort, simple block collections can read better as a single flow line.\n431\tEnable `compact = true` in `yamark.toml` (or pass `--compact`) and\n432\tYamark collapses eligible block mappings and sequences that fit the\n433\tstructural width:\n434\t\n435\t:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n436\t**Before**\n437\t\n438\t```yaml\n439\ttags:\n440\t  - yaml\n441\t  - markdown\n442\t  - docs\n443\tpackage:\n444\t  name: yamark\n445\t  language: rust\n446\t```\n447\t\n448\t**After**\n449\t\n450\t```yaml\n451\ttags: [yaml, markdown, docs]\n452\tpackage: {name: yamark, language: rust}\n453\t```\n454\t::::\n455\t\n456\tCollections with comments, aliases, tags, anchors, multiline scalars, or\n457\tblock scalars stay in block style.\n458\t\n459\t### Collapse to flow by typing a bracket\n460\t\n461\tDrop an unmatched `[` or `{` where a block sequence or mapping value starts and\n462\tYamark reads it as a layout hint: collapse this collection onto one line. The\n463\tfile doesn't parse as you typed it, but the intent is obvious - Yamark removes\n464\tthe opener and emits flow style.\n465\t\n466\t:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n467\t**Before**\n468\t\n469\t```yaml\n470\ttags: [\n471\t  - yaml\n472\t  - markdown\n473\t  - docs\n474\t```\n475\t\n476\t**After**\n477\t\n478\t```yaml\n479\ttags: [yaml, markdown, docs]\n480\t```\n481\t::::\n482\t\n483\tThe opener may also be detached onto the next line after an empty mapping value\n484\theader:\n485\t\n486\t:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n487\t**Before**\n488\t\n489\t```yaml\n490\ttags:\n491\t[\n492\t  - yaml\n493\t  - markdown\n494\t  - docs\n495\t```\n496\t\n497\t**After**\n498\t\n499\t```yaml\n500\ttags: [yaml, markdown, docs]\n501\t```\n502\t::::\n503\t\n504\tAdjacent forms such as `tags:[` and `tags:{` are not repaired as layout hints.\n505\t\n506\tA newline inside an existing flow collection requests the reverse change: expand\n507\tthe collection to block style.\n508\t\n509\t:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n510\t**Before**\n511\t\n512\t```yaml\n513\t- {a: b,\n514\t   c: d}\n515\t```\n516\t\n517\t**After**\n518\t\n519\t```yaml\n520\t- a: b\n521\t  c: d\n522\t```\n523\t::::\n524\t\n525\tSee [Supported files and syntax -> Layout repair](reference-files.qmd#layout-repair)\n526\tfor the acceptance rules.\n527\t\n528\t## Fenced and nested content\n529\t\n530\t### Recursive Markdown code fences\n531\t\n532\tYAML fences are formatted as YAML. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01DorH35FwgefwTbFa8eFU18","type":"tool_result","content":"# Yamark\n\nYamark is a fast formatter for YAML and Markdown. It formats whole files and embedded content, keeping source readable and changes easy to review. Regions without a supported rewrite stay unchanged.\n\nFor supported embedded code, Yamark can also call Ruff, Air, Prettier, or another configured formatter.\n\nSee the [documentation](https://t-kalinowski.github.io/yamark/) for examples, configuration, editor integrations, and the full syntax reference.\n\n## Install\n\nWith [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) installed, run Yamark directly from [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/yamark/) without a separate install:\n\n```sh\nuvx yamark format config.yaml docs/\n```\n\nThis formats the selected files in place. To install a persistent `yamark` command:\n\n```sh\nuv tool install yamark\n```\n\n## Usage\n\nThe examples below use an installed `yamark` command. To keep running from PyPI without installing it, replace `yamark` with `uvx yamark`.\n\nFormat one or more files or directories in place:\n\n```sh\nyamark format config.yaml docs/\n```\n\nFormat the current directory:\n\n```sh\nyamark format\n```\n\nCheck whether files are already formatted without writing changes:\n\n```sh\nyamark format --check docs/\n```\n\nShow a unified diff without writing changes:\n\n```sh\nyamark format --diff docs/\n```\n\nFormat stdin for editor and CI integrations:\n\n```sh\nyamark format --stdin-file-path config.yaml < config.yaml\n```\n\nConvert JSON-family input from stdin to formatted YAML on stdout:\n\n```sh\nyamark to-yaml --stdin-file-path data.json5 < data.json5\n```\n\nThe path is not read or written. Its suffix selects the exact JSON dialect. This is a conversion, not source formatting.\n\nDirectory traversal skips hidden paths and respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and global Git ignore files by default. Pass a hidden path explicitly to format it.\n\nWhile formatting is enabled, standalone `{{< ... >}}` and `{{% ... %}}` shortcode tokens are preserved, including multiline tokens and quoted arguments. Directive-looking text inside a recognized token is data. Yamark does not match shortcode names or interpret their bodies: Markdown between tokens formats normally. An unterminated token or quote preserves the rest of the enclosing Markdown document or fragment. This does not guarantee rendering equivalence for arbitrary Hugo or Jinja templates.\n\nTo disable body formatting, surround the region with `<!-- fmt: off -->` and `<!-- fmt: on -->`. While formatting is disabled, directives follow the existing linewise policy: a recognized `fmt: on` line resumes formatting even if the surrounding text resembles a shortcode argument, code fence, HTML, or math block.\n\nExplicitly skipped Markdown retains its bytes, including trailing spaces and line endings: `<!-- fmt: skip -->` preserves the next selected node, `<!-- fmt: off -->` preserves the disabled region, and `<!-- fmt: skip file -->` preserves the enclosing Markdown document or fragment. This protection survives supported nesting in Markdown fences and divs; surrounding Markdown still formats.\n\n## Editor integrations\n\nThe VS Code and Positron formatter extension lives in `editors/vscode/`. See the [editor guide][editor-docs] for installation and configuration.\n\n=========== DIRECTIVES\n---\n# fmt: skip file\ntitle: Directives\ndescription: Tell Yamark what to format, skip, preserve, or configure from inside the file.\n---\n\n<!-- fmt: skip file -->\n\nThe source file is the primary interface. Put a small `fmt:` directive next to\nthe text it controls, then let an editor or repository integration run Yamark.\nBecause directives are comments, the formatting choice stays with the text.\nThe comment marker depends on the file:\n\n| File | Directive comment |\n| --- | --- |\n| Markdown and Quarto | `<!-- fmt: ... -->` |\n| YAML, Python, and R | `# fmt: ...` |\n\nQuarto chunk options use `#|`; for example, `#| fmt: skip`.\n\n## Target the next value or block\n\nMost directives apply to the next supported target. In a YAML file, that target\nis usually a scalar node. In a Python or R file, it is usually a string literal\nor a contiguous source-comment block. The directive does not format the\nsurrounding Python or R source code.\n\n## YAML files\n\nMark a scalar as Markdown and choose sentence wrapping for that scalar:\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence\ndescription: \"Explain the project in a few clear sentences.\"\nother_value: \"This is ordinary YAML, not Markdown.\"\n```\n\nThe directive attaches to `description`, the next scalar. A tagged scalar is\nanother way to mark Markdown when the setting should travel with the value:\n\n```yaml\ninstructions: !markdown |\n  # Review\n\n  Read the diff and report concrete correctness issues.\n```\n\nUse the same placement for an embedded formatter. The formatter name is the\nlanguage after `fmt:`:\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: python\nscript: |\n  def check(items):return all(item > 0 for item in items)\n```\n\nYAML also supports directives on a collection parent when the setting describes\nthe collection rather than a scalar:\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: table\n- {name: alpha, type: string, default: \"\"}\n- {name: beta, type: integer, default: 0}\n```\n\n## Python files\n\nPut `# fmt: markdown` immediately before the string literal or comment block\nthat contains Markdown:\n\n```python\n# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence\nREVIEW_PROMPT = \"\"\"\n# Review\n\nRead the diff and report concrete correctness issues. Prefer specific examples.\n\"\"\"\n```\n\nThe `#` lines inside the string are Markdown content. Python outside the\nmarked target is left for a Python formatter such as Ruff.\n\nThe same directive can target a Markdown comment block:\n\n```python\n# fmt: markdown\n# # Filters\n#\n# Apply the most specific filter first.\n#\n# - Each filter is a single expression.\n```\n\nFor a non-Markdown embedded language, use its formatter name:\n\n```python\n# fmt: r\nanalysis = \"\"\"\nf <- function(x) x + 1\n\"\"\"\n```\n\n## R files\n\nR uses the same `# fmt:` marker. It can target a raw string literal used for a\nvignette, help text, or a Shiny message:\n\n```r\n# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence\nhelp_text <- r\"(\n# Filters\n\nApply the most specific filter first. Explain why a filter matched.\n)\"\n```\n\nIt can also target a contiguous Markdown comment block:\n\n```r\n# fmt: markdown\n# # Filters\n#\n# Apply the most specific filter first.\n#\n# - Each filter is a single expression.\n```\n\nFor source code inside a YAML literal scalar, use the language formatter name\nin the same way as in a YAML file:\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: r\nanalysis: |\n  f <- function(x)x+1\n```\n\n## Control a region or a whole file\n\nThe scope is part of the directive. `next` is the default for target directives.\nUse `from-here` for the rest of a region, and `file` for a document-wide\nsetting:\n\n| Scope | Applies to |\n| --- | --- |\n| `scope=next` | The next supported string, scalar, collection, or comment block. |\n| `scope=from-here` | Supported content from this point until another directive changes the setting. |\n| `scope=file` | The whole file, including supported content before the directive. |\n\nSkip one target:\n\n```yaml\nnormal: [1, 2, 3]\n# fmt: skip\nmanual:\n    -   [ 1,2,3]\n```\n\nPreserve a region and resume formatting afterward:\n\n```markdown\n<!-- fmt: off -->\n#   Keep this heading ##\n\n<!-- fmt: on -->\n```\n\nSkip a whole file by putting the file directive at the top. YAML, Python, and R\nuse the same hash-comment form:\n\n```text\n# fmt: skip file\n```\n\nMarkdown uses an HTML comment:\n\n```markdown\n<!-- fmt: skip file -->\n```\n\nA whole-file skip is useful for generated files or files whose layout is\nintentionally outside Yamark's scope.\n\nMarkdown skip controls retain trailing spaces and line endings in the selected\ncontent, including supported nested Markdown.\n\n## Preserve intentional table widths\n\nYamark normally fits table columns to their contents. Keep a table's authored\nwidths while still formatting its contents:\n\n```markdown\n<!-- fmt: table-widths=preserve scope=next -->\n+----------+------------------+\n| Name     | Description      |\n+==========+==================+\n| A        | Short text       |\n+----------+------------------+\n```\n\nUse `scope=file` to preserve widths throughout the document, or\n`scope=from-here` for subsequent tables. A later\n`table-widths=fit scope=from-here` resumes fitting widths. Both modes retain\ncolumn alignment. Fitting widths can change the rendered proportions of\nPandoc tables; preserving widths can retain excessive or cramped padding.\n\nFor Markdown inside YAML, Python, or R, the same option can accompany the\ntarget marker: `# fmt: markdown table-widths=preserve`.\n\n## Set file-specific Markdown options\n\nUse `scope=file` when the file should have a different Markdown policy from the\nrepository default:\n\n```markdown\n<!-- fmt: wrap=sentence:72 scope=file -->\n```\n\nThis puts one sentence per line and wraps long sentences at column 72. Other\nfile-wide Markdown options include `canonical=true` and\n`footnotes=preserve`:\n\n```markdown\n<!-- fmt: canonical=true footnotes=preserve scope=file -->\n```\n\nFor a YAML file or a hashpipe YAML stream in Python or R, use the same scope to\nset YAML behavior for the whole file:\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: compact=false scope=file\n```\n\nAn option-only directive such as `# fmt: canonical=true` adjusts the next\nalready-marked Markdown scalar. It does not turn an ordinary YAML scalar into a\nMarkdown target:\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: canonical=true\nfirst: !markdown \"This is __strong__ Markdown.\"\nsecond: \"This is ordinary YAML text.\"\n```\n\n## Arrange for Yamark to run automatically\n\nOnce directives are in the files, configure Yamark to run as part of the\nworkflow:\n\n- In an editor, enable format on save. The [Editors](editors.qmd) page shows\n  the VS Code and Positron settings. This is the most direct way to see a\n  directive take effect while editing.\n- In a pre-commit hook, run `yamark format`. In CI, use\n  `yamark format --check` to verify files without changing them.\n\nThe experimental [Git Filter](git-filter.qmd) serves a narrower workflow: it\nstores selected Markdown files sentence-per-line while keeping the working tree\ncolumn-wrapped.\n\n## When a repository default is better\n\nUse `yamark.toml` for settings that should apply broadly rather than to one\npiece of text. This page is\nan exact syntax lookup. For a guided path through YAML, Python, and R examples,\nsee [Directives](directives.qmd).\n\n## Comment forms\n\n| Host | Form | Placement |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Markdown | `<!-- fmt: ... -->` | An own-line HTML comment. |\n| YAML | `# fmt: ...` | An own-line hash comment. `fmt: table` and `fmt: compact table` may also be same-line comments on an empty-valued collection parent; a populated parent is an error. |\n| Python and R | `# fmt: ...` | An own-line hash comment before a supported comment or string target. |\n\n## Scopes\n\n| Scope | Meaning |\n| --- | --- |\n| `scope=next` | Apply to the next supported target. This is the default for target-selecting, compact, table, and embedded-formatter directives. |\n| `scope=from-here` | Apply from the directive until another directive changes the same state. |\n| `scope=file` | Apply throughout the current parsed document or nested region, including supported nodes before the directive. At the top level, that region is the physical file. |\n\nNot every directive accepts every scope. The tables below list the supported\nforms. An unsupported or misspelled explicit scope is an error. Template\ndelimiter directives use the contextual rule described below instead of one\nfixed default.\n\nScopes stop at the current parsed document or nested-region boundary. A\ndirective inside a recursive fence affects that fence, not its Markdown host or\nsibling fences. A `scope=file` directive inside one hashpipe YAML block does not\nspan later blocks. `fmt: skip file` in Markdown front matter is the exception:\nit preserves the outer Markdown document.\n\n## Preserve content\n\n| Directive | Scope | Effect |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `fmt: skip` | Next | Preserve the next supported target. `fmt: skip scope=next` is equivalent. |\n| `fmt: skip file` | File | Preserve the current parsed document or nested region. `fmt: skip scope=file` is equivalent. |\n| `fmt: off` | From here | Preserve content until `fmt: on`, or through the end of Markdown and source regions. `fmt: off scope=from-here` is equivalent. |\n| `fmt: on` | - | Resume formatting after `fmt: off`. It does not accept an explicit scope. |\n\nThe same control uses the host's comment form:\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: skip\nmanual: [[ 1,2,3], [4,5,6]]\n```\n\n```markdown\n<!-- fmt: off -->\n*   keep\n    this\n    list\n<!-- fmt: on -->\n```\n\nPreserve-control lifecycle checks are host-specific. YAML rejects a targetless\n`skip`, a stray `on`, a nested `off`, and an `off` without a later `on`.\nMarkdown and source regions allow `skip` at the end and let `off` preserve\nthrough the end of the region.\n\n## Markdown targets and settings\n\n| Form | Default scope | Effect |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `fmt: markdown` | Next | Mark the next supported target as Markdown: a Markdown block, including a supported fence; a YAML scalar; or a source string or comment block. |\n| `fmt: markdown wrap=sentence canonical=true` | Next | Mark the next supported target as Markdown and set its options. |\n| `fmt: wrap=sentence` | `scope=next` in YAML; `scope=file` in Markdown or source regions | Change wrapping for an already recognized Markdown region without marking unrelated content. |\n| `fmt: table-widths=preserve` | `scope=next` in YAML; `scope=file` in Markdown or source regions | Preserve widths in supported Markdown tables while formatting contents. Use `scope=next` immediately before one table. |\n| `fmt: canonical` | `scope=next` in YAML; `scope=file` in Markdown or source regions | Enable canonical Markdown spelling. `canonical=true` is equivalent. |\n| `fmt: footnotes=preserve` | `scope=next` in YAML; `scope=file` in Markdown or source regions | Preserve footnote definitions in the affected Markdown. |\n\nOption-only YAML directives tune the next scalar only if it is already marked\nas Markdown:\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: canonical=true\nfirst: !markdown \"This is __strong__.\"\nsecond: \"This is __not__ Markdown.\"\n```\n\nFor `scope=from-here` or `scope=file`, `fmt: markdown` must include at least one\nactual Markdown option. A broad-scope directive changes Markdown settings; it\ndoes not turn every plain scalar into Markdown.\n\nAccepted option values:\n\n| Option | Values |\n| --- | --- |\n| `wrap` | `none`, `paragraph`, `sentence`, `sentence:<n>`, or a positive integer. |\n| `table-widths` | `fit` (the default) or `preserve`. Both preserve alignment. |\n| `canonical` | `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. A bare `canonical` means `true`. |\n| `footnotes` | `wrap`, `format`, `preserve`, `none`, `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. |\n\nFor `footnotes`, `wrap`, `format`, `true`, `yes`, and `1` request formatting;\n`preserve`, `none`, `false`, `no`, and `0` request preservation.\n\n## YAML collections\n\n| Directive | Scope | Effect |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `fmt: compact` | Next | Enable block-to-flow compaction for the next eligible collection. |\n| `fmt: compact false` | Next | Disable compaction for the next eligible collection. `fmt: compact=false` is equivalent. |\n| `fmt: compact scope=from-here` | From here | Enable compaction until another compact directive changes the state. |\n| `fmt: compact=false scope=file` | File | Disable compaction throughout the current YAML document or one source-file hashpipe YAML block. |\n| `fmt: table` | Next | Align the next compatible sequence of flow mappings. |\n| `fmt: compact table` | Next | Collapse eligible block mapping rows before aligning them. `fmt: table compact` and `fmt: table compact=true` are equivalent. |\n\n`fmt: table` accepts only its default next-target scope. Compact directives\naccept `next`, `from-here`, and `file`.\n\n`compact`, `compact=true`, `compact=yes`, `compact=1`, and `compact true`\nenable compaction. `compact=false`, `compact=no`, `compact=0`, and\n`compact false` disable it. The separated form accepts only `true` or `false`.\n\n## Templates and embedded formatters\n\n| Directive | Scope | Effect |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `fmt: template.delimiters \"<<\" \">>\"` | Inferred | Add one non-empty double-quoted delimiter pair using the placement rule below. |\n| `fmt: template.delimiters \"<<\" \">>\" scope=next` | Next | Add the pair to the next supported target. |\n| `fmt: template.delimiters \"<<\" \">>\" scope=from-here` | From here | Add the pair to following supported targets. |\n| `fmt: template.delimiters \"<<\" \">>\" scope=file` | File | Add the pair throughout the current document or nested region. |\n| `fmt: embedded python` | Next | Format the next supported string or YAML literal scalar with the named formatter. |\n| `fmt: python` | Next | Shorthand for `fmt: embedded python`. |\n\nA bare `fmt: template.delimiters` directive uses the next target when placed\ndirectly before one. When blank lines or range boundaries isolate it from\ncontent on both sides, it applies from there onward. The directive requires an\nexplicit scope in every other placement.\n\nDelimiter arguments must be non-empty double-quoted tokens; single quotes are\nnot accepted. Inside a token, `\\\"`, `\\\\`, `\\n`, `\\r`, and `\\t` represent a\ndouble quote, backslash, newline, carriage return, and tab.\n\nEmbedded formatter directives accept only `scope=next`. The name can select a\nbuilt-in alias or an entry from [`[embedded]`](reference-config.qmd#embedded).\n\nYAML can also mark a scalar as Markdown with the `!markdown` or `!md` tag:\n\n```yaml\nbody: !markdown \"A paragraph with [a link](https://example.com).\"\n```\n\n## Source files and fenced chunks\n\n| Host | Directive | Effect |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Python or R comment or string | `fmt: markdown` | Format the next supported comment block or string as Markdown. [Formatting settings](reference-options.qmd) describes how to change\nthe output.\n\n## Files and regions\n\n| Input | What Yamark formats | Selection |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `.yaml` and `.yml` | The whole YAML stream. | Automatic for path-aware formatting. |\n| `.md`, `.qmd`, `.Rmd`, and `.rmd` | Markdown, YAML front matter, and recognized fenced content. | Automatic, except constructs described as preserved below. |\n| `.py`, `.R`, and `.r` | `#|` hashpipe YAML blocks, marked Markdown comments or strings, and marked external-formatter targets. | Hashpipe blocks are automatic; other targets require a `fmt:` directive. Surrounding source code is unchanged. |\n| `.json`, `.jsonc`, `.json5`, `.jsonl`, and `.ndjson` | A YAML projection of the whole JSON-family input. | Explicit through `yamark to-yaml` or `Yamark: View JSON as YAML`. Normal formatting does not select these files. |\n| Markdown fences named `yaml`, `yml`, `markdown`, or `md` | YAML, or recursively formatted Markdown. | Automatic unless the fence is locally skipped. |\n| Markdown source fences | Python, R, JSON, GraphQL, CSS, HTML, JavaScript, TypeScript, and related aliases. | Delegated when a matching embedded formatter is available. |\n| YAML scalars tagged `!markdown` or `!md` | The scalar value as Markdown. | Explicit tag. |\n| YAML scalars following `# fmt: markdown` | The scalar value as Markdown. | Explicit directive. |\n| YAML literal scalars following `# fmt: <name>` or `# fmt: embedded <name>` | The scalar value through a built-in or configured embedded formatter. | Explicit directive. |\n\nExtension matching is ASCII case-insensitive. In path mode, unsupported\nextensions are counted as skipped and do not make the run fail. An unsupported\n`--stdin-file-path` is an error because stdin mode requires file-aware behavior.\n\nDirectory traversal skips hidden paths and respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`,\nand global Git ignore files. Passing a hidden path explicitly selects it.\n\n## JSON-to-YAML projection\n\nFormatting preserves the source language and produces output that can replace\nthe input. JSON-to-YAML projection has a different contract: it parses a\nJSON-family input and emits formatted YAML for inspection or conversion.\n\nUse `yamark to-yaml --stdin-file-path` to project JSON-family input from stdin\nto formatted YAML on stdout:\n\n```sh\nyamark to-yaml --stdin-file-path data.json < data.json\n```\n\nThe command does not read or write the path. It uses the extension to select\none exact input grammar:\n\n| Extension | Accepted input |\n| --- | --- |\n| `.json` | Strict JSON. |\n| `.jsonc` | JSON with line comments, block comments, and trailing commas. Other JSON5 syntax is rejected. |\n| `.json5` | JSON5 strings, identifiers, numbers, comments, and trailing commas. |\n| `.jsonl` and `.ndjson` | One strict JSON value per physical line. Blank records are rejected. |\n\nObject member order and duplicate names are preserved. JSON and JSONC keep the\nsource spelling of numbers. JSON5 spellings that YAML would interpret\ndifferently are normalized, including `0X` hexadecimal prefixes, leading or\ntrailing decimal points, unary plus, `Infinity`, and `NaN`. Negative\nhexadecimal integers are emitted in decimal because YAML would otherwise treat\nthem as strings.\n\nJSONC and JSON5 comments become YAML comments. JSONL and NDJSON output a YAML\ndocument-start marker before every record. A record may be an object, array, or\nscalar; this does not change how ordinary YAML such as `1\\n2` is interpreted by\n`yamark format`.\n\nString escapes are decoded before YAML emission. Lone UTF-16 surrogate escapes\nare rejected because they do not represent Unicode scalar values. All\nJSON-family inputs reject nesting deeper than 256 levels. JSON5 also rejects\nlegacy numeric escapes such as `\\1`, invalid escaped identifier characters, and\nU+0085 as whitespace. Characters that YAML cannot carry inside a comment are\nshown as visible hexadecimal escapes.\n\nProjection does not scan JSON strings or comments for embedded Markdown or\nformatter directives, and it does not dispatch to Prettier or another embedded\nformatter.\n\n`yamark format` continues to skip JSON-family paths and never rewrites them.\n`Yamark: View JSON as YAML` in VS Code and Positron uses the same JSON-to-YAML\nprojection.\n\n## Markdown\n\n| Construct | Result | Details |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Paragraphs | Formats | Wraps by column, paragraph, sentence, or not at all, according to the active Markdown settings. |\n| ATX headings | Formats | Normalizes spacing. Preserves and, when safe, compacts heading attributes. |\n| Lists and task lists | Formats | Reflows list paragraphs with container indentation accounted for. Git clean/smudge filters otherwise use compact pipe-table output. |\n| Pandoc tables | Formats when supported | Fits supported simple, grid, and multiline tables to their contents while preserving column alignment and multiline cell breaks. `table-widths=preserve` retains source widths. |\n| Definition lists | Formats when supported | Normalizes marker spacing and wraps definitions. |\n| Display math | Preserves | Keeps own-line `$$` display math blocks byte-for-byte. |\n| Standalone Hugo shortcodes | Preserves tokens; formats between | Complete `{{< ... >}}` and `{{% ... %}}` tokens retain their bytes, including multiline tokens and quoted arguments. Markdown between tokens formats normally. |\n| Raw HTML, TeX, table captions, and line blocks | Preserves | Leaves the construct unchanged when Yamark does not have a safe rewrite. |\n| Template spans | Preserves contents; reflows prose | Complete single-line expressions using default or configured delimiters are opaque words in paragraphs and supported prose containers. See [template configuration](reference-config.qmd#template). |\n\nFor Quarto header promotion, a supported fence is a YAML or Markdown fence, a\nlanguage with a built-in or configured formatter, or one of the opaque\nlanguages Yamark preserves safely: `bash`, `sh`, `shell`, `zsh`, `ojs`, `text`,\n`console`, `rust`, `toml`, `lua`, `mermaid`, `ini`, `julia`, `sql`, `java`, `c`,\n`tex`, `latex`, `output`, `powershell`, and `cmd`.\n\n## YAML\n\n| Construct | Result | Details |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Block mappings and sequences | Formats | Normalizes indentation and spacing. Does not reorder keys. |\n| Flow mappings and sequences | Formats | Normalizes spacing. Expands multiline or over-width collections to block style when safe. |\n| Compact collections | Formats when enabled | Collapses eligible block collections to flow style with `--compact`, `[format].compact`, or `fmt: compact`. |\n| Scalar folding | Formats when safe | Can emit and rewrap folded prose scalars at the active prose width, including prose already split across plain or quoted continuation lines. Preserves decoded whitespace and comments. |\n| Literal scalars | Preserves by default | Changes a literal scalar only when it is explicitly marked as Markdown or an embedded formatter target. |\n| Quoted scalars with hard newlines | Formats when safe | Can emit literal block style when the YAML value stays unchanged. |\n| Scalars below a mapping key or sequence marker | Formats when safe | Retains the complete entry when preserving a value. Ordinary scalar entries with parent tags, anchors, or comments retain their layout; editable siblings still format. |\n| Unsafe plain scalars | Quotes | Quotes scalars whose meaning would change in block or flow context. |\n| Core booleans and nulls | Formats | Normalizes plain values to YAML 1.2 spellings such as `true`, `false`, and `null`. Normalizes explicit core tags when safe. |\n| Tags and anchors | Preserves | Preserves custom tags, anchors, aliases, and tag/anchor order. May remove a redundant core collection tag when syntax already implies the type. |\n| Comments and directives | Preserves and reads | Preserves comments around supported nodes. Reads `fmt:` comments as local controls. |\n| Duplicate keys | Formats around | Does not validate or reorder duplicate keys. Explicit Markdown targets still format; their block content uses deeper indentation when needed to keep the following comment outside the value.\n\n### JSON Lines (JSONL) as YAML streams\n\nPath-aware formatting recognizes a `.yaml` or `.yml` stream made of two or more\nunmarked, one-line YAML flow-mapping roots, one per physical line with no\nseparate trivia lines. It inserts the `---` document-start marker before every\nrecord, including the first.\n\nJSON objects are the common case, but the trigger is based on YAML shape and is\nnot restricted to strict JSON objects.\n\nNormal `--line-width` rules still determine whether each record and its nested\ncollections stay in flow style or expand to block style. A single flow-mapping\nroot or a stream containing any non-flow-mapping root follows the normal YAML\npath instead.\n\nSee the generated [JSON Lines example](examples.qmd#json-lines-as-a-yaml-stream).\n\n## Python and R source files\n\n| Construct | Result | Details |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Consecutive own-line `#|` comments | Formats | Parses the comment body as YAML and emits it with the original hashpipe prefix. |\n| Marked Markdown comments and strings | Formats | Formats supported own-line comment blocks and supported multiline string literals, accounting for their prefix or indentation. |\n| Marked external source strings | Delegates | Sends a supported multiline string literal to the named built-in or configured formatter and re-indents the result. |\n| Surrounding Python or R | Preserves | Does not format source outside recognized or explicitly marked targets. |\n\nEvery non-empty line in a comment target must use the same comment prefix;\nempty comment lines may omit its trailing space. Python string targets use\ntriple quotes with no prefix, or an `r`, `f`, `rf`, or `fr` prefix; the closing\ndelimiter must be on a later line. R targets use a multiline standard or raw\nstring. Markdown formatting rejects backslashes in non-raw Python and R strings\nbecause rewriting them could change the host-language value.\n\nThe generated [hashpipe YAML example](examples.qmd#hashpipe-yaml-in-source-files)\nshows the automatic source-file transformation.\n\n## Embedded formatter dispatch\n\nExternal formatters run only for explicit targets or recognized Markdown fence\nlanguages. Built-in aliases include `ruff`, `air`, `mdformat`, and the\n`prettier` family.\n\n| Target name or fence language | Built-in formatter |\n| --- | --- |\n| `python`, `ruff` | Ruff |\n| `r`, `air` | Air |\n| `mdformat` | mdformat |\n| `json`, `prettier-json` | Prettier with a `.json` path |\n| `jsonc`, `prettier-jsonc` | Prettier with a `.jsonc` path |\n| `json5`, `prettier-json5` | Prettier with a `.json5` path |\n| `graphql`, `gql`, `graphqls`, `prettier-graphql` | Prettier with a `.graphql` path |\n| `css`, `prettier-css` | Prettier with a `.css` path |\n| `scss`, `prettier-scss` | Prettier with a `.scss` path |\n| `less`, `prettier-less` | Prettier with a `.less` path |\n| `postcss`, `pcss`, `prettier-postcss` | Prettier with a `.pcss` path |\n| `html`, `prettier-html` | Prettier with a `.html` path |\n| `js`, `javascript`, `prettier-js` | Prettier with a `.js` path |\n| `jsx`, `prettier-jsx` | Prettier with a `.jsx` path |\n| `ts`, `typescript`, `prettier-ts` | Prettier with a `.ts` path |\n| `tsx`, `prettier-tsx` | Prettier with a `.tsx` path |\n\nMarkdown fences named `markdown` or `md` are formatted recursively instead of\nusing mdformat. An [`[embedded.<name>]`](reference-config.qmd#embedded) entry\nreplaces the built-in mapping for that exact name.\n\nThe default aliases are optional. A configured formatter is also optional when\nits command's first argv item is exactly `ruff`, `air`, `mdformat`, or\n`prettier`. A missing executable or nonzero exit preserves the target for\neither kind. Yamark reports the reason as a note only with `--diagnostics`.\n\nA successful process that writes to stderr is an error. The example below shows the full tag and comment forms.\n\nA `prompts.yaml` or `agents.yaml` file can use any of these forms. Yamark wraps\nthe selected value as Markdown, choosing folded or literal block style from the\ncontent.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```yaml\nagents:\n  reviewer:\n    instructions: !markdown \"Focus on correctness and tests. Flag any change that lacks a regression\n      test. Prefer concrete suggestions: name the function, name the case.\n  summarizer:\n    # fmt: markdown\n    instructions: |\n      You write release notes.\n\n      - One bullet per user-visible change.\n      - No internal refactors.\n```\n::::\n\nThe tagged value contains only prose, so Yamark rewraps it as a folded block.\nThe comment-marked value contains a list, so Yamark keeps literal block style\n(`|`) because folding would destroy the line breaks Markdown depends on.\n\n### Source code in YAML\n\nYAML values can also contain source code. Use `# fmt: python`, `# fmt: r`, or\nthe name of another configured formatter before a literal block. When the\nformatter is available, Yamark formats the block and restores its indentation\nin the YAML file.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: python\npreflight: |\n  def check(items):return all(x>0 for x in items)\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: python\npreflight: |\n  def check(items):\n    return all(x > 0 for x in items)\n```\n::::\n\n### YAML scalar presentation\n\nYamark changes scalar spelling only when the parsed YAML value and tag\nstay equivalent. It can simplify safe quoted strings, keep strings that\nwould be misread as booleans, convert hard newlines to literal blocks,\nand fold long prose strings.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```yaml\ntitle: \"hello\"\nboolish: \"true\"\nbody: \"alpha\\nbeta\\n\"\nsummary: \"This package formats YAML front matter and configuration files while preserving semantics, comments, and repository-friendly diffs.\"\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```yaml\ntitle: hello\nboolish: \"true\"\nbody: |\n  alpha\n  beta\nsummary: >-\n  This package formats YAML front matter and configuration files while\n  preserving semantics, comments, and repository-friendly diffs.\n```\n::::\n\n## Markdown links, footnotes, and tables\n\nLong inline links are split at Markdown syntax boundaries. Footnote\ndefinitions wrap under the marker unless the document or CLI asks to\npreserve them.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```markdown\nPlease be mindful of our [code of conduct](https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/main/.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) as you interact with other community members.\n\nBody text with a footnote.[^long]\n\n[^long]: This footnote explains that comments were removed because people used comments to hold parsing directives and enough extra words to wrap.\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```markdown\nPlease be mindful of our [code of conduct](\n  https://github.com/quarto-dev/quarto-cli/blob/main/.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md\n) as you interact with other community members.\n\nBody text with a footnote.[^long]\n\n[^long]: This footnote explains that comments were removed because\n  people used comments to hold parsing directives and enough extra words\n  to wrap.\n```\n::::\n\nSimple GFM pipe tables are aligned by display width. Git clean/smudge filters\nalways use compact pipe-table output.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```markdown\n| package | label |\n|---|---|\n| dplyr | tidy |\n| tidyr | pivoting |\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```markdown\n| package | label    |\n| ------- | -------- |\n| dplyr   | tidy     |\n| tidyr   | pivoting |\n```\n::::\n\n## Markdown in source files\n\n### Hashpipe YAML in source files\n\nConsecutive own-line `#|` comments in Python and R are a YAML block. Yamark\nformats the comment body as YAML, restores the hashpipe prefix, and leaves the\nsurrounding source code unchanged. This recognition is automatic; it does not\nneed a `fmt:` directive.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```r\n#| name: demo\n#| launcher:\n#|  vanilla: true\n#|  default-packages: [base,utils]\n\nmain <- function() NULL\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```r\n#| name: demo\n#| launcher:\n#|   vanilla: true\n#|   default-packages: [base, utils]\n\nmain <- function() NULL\n```\n::::\n\n### Embedded Markdown in Python\n\nWhen a prompt lives next to the code that uses it, Yamark can format the prose\nwithout changing the surrounding Python. Add `# fmt: markdown` before the\nstring:\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```python\n# fmt: markdown\nREVIEW_PROMPT = \"\"\"\n# Review\n\nRead the diff and flag anything that violates the style guide, has obvious correctness issues, or looks untested.\n\n-   Prefer specific suggestions over vague concerns.\n-   Name the function and the case.\n\"\"\"\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```python\n# fmt: markdown\nREVIEW_PROMPT = \"\"\"\n# Review\n\nRead the diff and flag anything that violates the style guide, has\nobvious correctness issues, or looks untested.\n\n- Prefer specific suggestions over vague concerns.\n- Name the function and the case.\n\"\"\"\n```\n::::\n\nPython source outside the marked string is left untouched. Run `ruff format` for\nthat.\n\n### Embedded Markdown in source comments\n\nThe same directive can target a contiguous source comment block. This is useful\nfor generated help text or documentation snippets where a string literal is not\nthe right host.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```python\n# fmt: markdown\n# #   Filters\n#\n# Apply one or more filters. Put the most specific filter first.\n#\n# -   Each filter is a single expression.\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```python\n# fmt: markdown\n# # Filters\n#\n# Apply one or more filters. Put the most specific filter first.\n#\n# - Each filter is a single expression.\n```\n::::\n\n### Embedded Markdown in R\n\nThe same pattern works for R raw strings. It can format package vignettes,\ndocumentation fragments, and Shiny help text kept next to the code that renders\nit.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```r\n# fmt: markdown\nhelp_text <- r\"(\n# Filters\n\nApply one or more filters. Filters are evaluated top-to-bottom; the first match wins, so put the most specific filter first.\n\n-   Each filter is a single expression.\n-   Multiple filters combine with AND.\n)\"\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```r\n# fmt: markdown\nhelp_text <- r\"(\n# Filters\n\nApply one or more filters. Filters are evaluated top-to-bottom; the\nfirst match wins, so put the most specific filter first.\n\n- Each filter is a single expression.\n- Multiple filters combine with AND.\n)\"\n```\n::::\n\n## YAML layout\n\n### JSON Lines as a YAML stream\n\nGive a JSON Lines file containing two or more object records a `.yaml` or\n`.yml` extension, with one record per line, then format it normally. Yamark\ninserts a leading `---` document-start marker before every record, including\nthe first, producing a valid YAML multi-document stream. The example below uses\nrecords from agent runs.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```yaml\n{\"id\":1,\"profile\":{\"name\":\"planner\",\"active\":true}}\n{\"id\":2,\"profile\":{\"name\":\"researcher\",\"active\":true},\"usage\":{\"input_tokens\":640,\"output_tokens\":128}}\n{\"id\":3,\"profile\":{\"name\":\"reviewer\",\"active\":true,\"model\":\"gpt-5\",\"region\":\"us\",\"tools\":[\"search\",\"python\"]},\"events\":[{\"type\":\"tool_call\",\"tools\":[\"search\",\"open\",\"python\",\"write\"]},{\"type\":\"usage\",\"tokens\":{\"input\":900,\"output\":240}},{\"type\":\"completion\",\"status\":\"ok\"}]}\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```yaml\n---\n{id: 1, profile: {name: planner, active: true}}\n---\nid: 2\nprofile: {name: researcher, active: true}\nusage: {input_tokens: 640, output_tokens: 128}\n---\nid: 3\nprofile:\n  name: reviewer\n  active: true\n  model: gpt-5\n  region: us\n  tools: [search, python]\nevents:\n  - {type: tool_call, tools: [search, open, python, write]}\n  - {type: usage, tokens: {input: 900, output: 240}}\n  - {type: completion, status: ok}\n```\n::::\n\nYamark keeps each document as compact as the width allows. The first record\nstays in flow style; the second expands only its root mapping; the third also\nexpands `profile` and `events`. Smaller mappings and sequences remain in flow\nstyle whenever they still fit within `--line-width`. This conversion is for\nobject records, not arbitrary JSON values.\n\n### Aligned flow-mapping tables\n\nA sequence of similar flow mappings can be easier to scan as a table. Mark it\nwith `# fmt: table` and Yamark aligns columns by key:\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: table\n- {name: alpha,type: string,default: [one,two],description: \"Short\"}\n- {name: beta,type: int,default: 0,description: \"Number\"}\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```yaml\n# fmt: table\n- {name: alpha, type: string, default: [one, two], description: Short}\n- {name: beta,  type: int,    default: 0,          description: Number}\n```\n::::\n\n### Compact collections\n\nShort, simple block collections can read better as a single flow line.\nEnable `compact = true` in `yamark.toml` (or pass `--compact`) and\nYamark collapses eligible block mappings and sequences that fit the\nstructural width:\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```yaml\ntags:\n  - yaml\n  - markdown\n  - docs\npackage:\n  name: yamark\n  language: rust\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```yaml\ntags: [yaml, markdown, docs]\npackage: {name: yamark, language: rust}\n```\n::::\n\nCollections with comments, aliases, tags, anchors, multiline scalars, or\nblock scalars stay in block style.\n\n### Collapse to flow by typing a bracket\n\nDrop an unmatched `[` or `{` where a block sequence or mapping value starts and\nYamark reads it as a layout hint: collapse this collection onto one line. The\nfile doesn't parse as you typed it, but the intent is obvious - Yamark removes\nthe opener and emits flow style.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```yaml\ntags: [\n  - yaml\n  - markdown\n  - docs\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```yaml\ntags: [yaml, markdown, docs]\n```\n::::\n\nThe opener may also be detached onto the next line after an empty mapping value\nheader:\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```yaml\ntags:\n[\n  - yaml\n  - markdown\n  - docs\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```yaml\ntags: [yaml, markdown, docs]\n```\n::::\n\nAdjacent forms such as `tags:[` and `tags:{` are not repaired as layout hints.\n\nA newline inside an existing flow collection requests the reverse change: expand\nthe collection to block style.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n```yaml\n- {a: b,\n   c: d}\n```\n\n**After**\n\n```yaml\n- a: b\n  c: d\n```\n::::\n\nSee [Supported files and syntax -> Layout repair](reference-files.qmd#layout-repair)\nfor the acceptance rules.\n\n## Fenced and nested content\n\n### Recursive Markdown code fences\n\nYAML fences are formatted as YAML. Markdown fences are formatted\nrecursively, so nested YAML inside nested Markdown is formatted too.\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n`````markdown\n```yaml\n# fmt: table\n- {name: a,type: int,default: 0}\n- {name: long_name,type: string,default: \"\"}\n```\n\n````markdown\n#   Inner\n\n```yaml\nitems: [a,b]\n```\n````\n`````\n\n**After**\n\n`````markdown\n```yaml\n# fmt: table\n- {name: a,         type: int,    default: 0}\n- {name: long_name, type: string, default: \"\"}\n```\n\n````markdown\n# Inner\n\n```yaml\nitems: [a, b]\n```\n````\n`````\n::::\n\n### Prettier-backed web and data fences\n\nWhen `prettier` is on `PATH`, JSON, JSONC, JSON5, GraphQL, CSS, SCSS, Less,\nPostCSS, HTML, JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, and TSX fenced blocks are handed to\nit. Python and R fences go to Ruff and Air the same way:\n\n:::: {.showcase-before-after}\n**Before**\n\n````markdown\n```json\n{\"name\":\"yamark\",\"tags\":[\"yaml\",\"markdown\",\"formatter\"],\"engines\":{\"node\":\">=18\"}}\n```\n\n```ts\nfunction format(input:string):string{return input.trim()}\n```\n````\n\n**After**\n\n````markdown\n```json\n{\n  \"name\": \"yamark\",\n  \"tags\": [\"yaml\", \"markdown\", \"formatter\"],\n  \"engines\": { \"node\": \">=18\" }\n}\n```\n\n```ts\nfunction format(input: string): string {\n  return input.trim();\n}\n```\n````\n::::\n\nA missing `prettier` leaves the fence unchanged. Override or disable a\nlanguage with `[embedded.<language>]` in `yamark.toml`, or skip them all with\n`--skip-embedded-formatters`.\n\n---\n\nOnce an example has shown you the behavior, see [Directives](directives.qmd)\nfor how to place those instructions in Markdown, YAML, Python, and R files.\nUse [Reference](reference.qmd) to look up exact directive grammar, formatting\nsettings, supported syntax, and failure behavior.","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":"toolu_01Gvk1ggD1NHUZ5frpaQFjfW","agent_id":"a437806447bf9e4db","session_id":"0e7cfb1b-67a4-4c6e-bc49-6d823e4685c0","uuid":"96dbc4be-052b-41f8-9db8-f9df04e0350a","timestamp":"2026-11-17T17:25:43.737Z","tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01PmazHSA5R1YdMcnzDWPRVd","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}],"subagent_type":"general-purpose","task_description":"Write realistic test corpus H"}
